children.text: taṃ natvā vimalaṃ śivārkakiraṇe śāstre pare racyate
children.translated_text: Having bowed to that pure one, in this supreme scripture [called] the Ray of <s>Śiva</s>'s Sun (<s>Śivārkakiraṇa</s>), there is composed
a brief commentary (<s>vivṛti</s>) that leads [the reader] through the words, beginning with the chapter called <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge),
where the determination of the subject matter has been proclaimed at length through reasoning and scripture,
generally [applicable], made by me for cutting through the doubts of opposing doctrines, as [found] extensively elsewhere.

body.text: purā kila bhagavatomāpatinā garutmato 'nugrahaṃ kurvatā yathā yādṛgrūpaṃ ca śāstramupadiṣṭaṃ tathā tādṛgrūpaṃ ca kaścittacchiṣyaḥ praśiṣyo vā svaśiṣyebhyaḥ kathayati
body.translated_text: Long ago, when the blessed lord <s>Umāpati</s> (Śiva) was bestowing grace upon <s>Garutmat</s> (Garuḍa), in whatever manner and of whatever form the scripture was taught, in that same manner and of that same form, a certain disciple or grand-disciple relates it to his own students:

children.translated_text: Seated upon the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>,
<s>Soma</s> (Śiva), who bears the half-moon as his crest,
having seen <s>Hara</s> (Śiva), <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa) spoke
these words, preceded by praise.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yattu prathamamevotsūtraṃ kaiścicchāstrasvarūpaṃ tatsambandhābhidheyādi cātra varṇyate tatsūtraireva teṣāṃ vakṣyamāṇatvādayuktameva|
athādau pravṛttihetutvenāvaśyaṃ tadvaktavyamiti cet|
śāstrāntarāṇāmivātra tadabhidhānena pravṛttyayogāt|
atra hi gurūpasadanātprabhṛti guruvākyādeva sarvatra pravartitavyaṃ nānyata iti
darśayiṣyāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti (Commentary): As for the introductory verse (<s>utsūtra</s>) that some [commentators] place first, describing the nature of the scripture, its connection, subject matter, and so on — since these will be stated through the sūtras themselves, [such an introduction] is indeed unnecessary. But if [one argues that] these must be stated first as a cause for [the reader's] engagement — [the reply is:] here, unlike other scriptures, engagement does not arise from such a statement. For here we shall demonstrate that from the time of approaching the teacher onward, one must proceed everywhere on the basis of the teacher's word alone, not otherwise.

body.text:
tatra kailāsasya śikharamagrapradeśaḥ| tasminnāsīnaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvetyanena yogimadhyasthitatvena vakṣyamāṇādasya brahmaviṣṇulokābhyāmūrdhvamaṇḍalamadhye vakṣyamāṇasya devasya viśeṣaḥ|
sahomayā vartate yastamityanena kailāsaśikharāsīnāntarācchrīmannandikeśvarāderviśeṣaḥ||
body.translated_text: In this context, the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s> is its summit. 'Seated thereon, having seen him' — by this, the special status of this deity is indicated, who, by virtue of being situated in the midst of yogīs, is [established] above the realms of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, in the midst of the upper sphere, as will be described. 'He who exists together with <s>Umā</s>' — by this, he is distinguished from the venerable <s>Nandikeśvara</s> and others among those seated on the peak of <s>Kailāsa</s>.

body.text:
atha rūḍhiryogamapaharatīti nyāyato 'tra somaśabdena kaściccandrameva pratyeṣyatīti tadarthametatsomārdhaṃ śekhare śirasi yasya taṃ dṛṣṭveti|
kiñca harati bandhanāni puṃbhyaḥ puṃso 'pyūrdhvaṃ padamiti haraḥ taṃ svaguruṃ tārkṣyo dṛṣṭvetyarthaḥ|
ata evāsya nirvāṇadīkṣā sampanneti pratīyate|
nādīkṣitānāṃ śravaṇādhikāra iti vakṣyati yataḥ|
haraśabdasya rūḍhyaivomāpatyarthatve vyākhyāyamāne gatārthatvaṃ vyavacchedāntarābhāvāditi viśiṣṭakriyāyogābhidhānenaiva vyākhyānaṃ jyāyaḥ|
atra ca praṇāmasāmarthyādeva darśanasya siddhernāyamartho haraṃ dṛṣṭveti|
api tu stutipūrvaṃ dṛṣṭveti stutipūrvamiti padamatra kriyāviśeṣaṇatvena vyākhyeyam| na tu vacoviśeṣaṇatvena|
tataśca vakṣyamāṇāndhakamathanādikarmastutyā viśiṣṭakarmayuktaṃ bhagavantamārādhyedaṃ vacanaṃ vainateyo 'bravīdityatrārthaḥ| tanna doṣaḥ kaściditi||
body.translated_text: Now, since the convention that 'established usage overrides etymology' applies here, someone might understand the word '<s>Soma</s>' to mean only the moon; therefore [the text says] 'bearing the half-moon on his crest.' Furthermore, '<s>Hara</s>' means one who removes the bonds from souls and [leads them to] the state beyond the soul — having seen him, his own teacher, <s>Tārkṣya</s> [spoke] — this is the meaning. For this very reason it is understood that his <s>nirvāṇadīkṣā</s> (initiation for liberation) has been accomplished, since it will be stated that 'those who are uninitiated have no eligibility to hear.' When the word '<s>Hara</s>' is explained by conventional usage alone as meaning 'son of <s>Umā</s>,' since there would be no further distinction to make [redundancy results], the explanation through the statement of connection with a specific action is preferable. And here, since the accomplishment of 'seeing' is already achieved through the power of prostration, the meaning is not 'having seen <s>Hara</s>.' Rather, 'having seen, preceded by praise' — the word '<s>stutipūrvam</s>' (preceded by praise) is to be construed here as qualifying the action [of seeing], not as qualifying the speech. And thus the meaning is: having worshipped the blessed Lord — who is endowed with specific deeds — through the praise of his exploits such as the slaying of <s>Andhaka</s> and the like, which will be described, the son of <s>Vinatā</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) spoke these words. There is no fault in this.
Now, what is that praise which preceded the seeing, as stated? To that it is replied:

children.translated_text: Victory! O you who are skilled in sundering the bonds
of broad-shouldered <s>Andhaka</s>,
Victory! O lord of the foremost heroes,
burner of the besieged cities (<s>Tripura</s>),
Victory! O ruler of all the gods,
terrifying in the severing of heads [of <s>Brahmā</s>],
Victory! O you of renowned power,
destroyer of the body of <s>Manmatha</s> (Kāma, the god of love),
Victory! O you who cause the destruction of the body of <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>),
remover of the force of the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison,
Victory! O you who hold back the current
of the river with its great swirling eddies,
Victory! O you who delude the wives of the sages
in the grove of <s>Dāruvana</s>,
Victory! O you whose great commencement of dance
is dreadful in its playful agitation [of the cosmos],
Victory! O you whose fierce form and furious onset
terrified both gods and demons,
Victory! O you who displayed streams of blood
from the face of the cruel lord of demons [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>],
Victory! O you who, by the exertion of the hero [<s>Vīrabhadra</s>],
destroyed the sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa</s>,
Victory! O you who are proud of the power and form
of the wondrous great <s>liṅga</s>,
Victory! O you who, on account of [the sage] <s>Śveta</s>,
cast down the fierce body of Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>),
Victory! O you, the abode of all happiness,
by whom the mountain-born [<s>Gaurī</s>] is enchanted with desire,
Victory! O remover of the darkness of the net of delusion
that was the suffering of <s>Upamanyu</s>,
Victory! O burner of the worlds and non-worlds
above the base of the netherworlds (<s>Pātāla</s>).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
andhakasya mahāsurasya yau vistīrṇau skandhau tayorbandho vicitraḥ sanniveśaḥ tasya bhedo vidāraṇam| tasminyo vicakṣaṇaḥ paṇḍitastvameva, nānyaḥ| tasyāmantraṇaṃ he tathābhūta bhagavan jayeti|
kiñca prakṛṣṭo varo brahmadatto yeṣāṃ te pravarāśca vīrāśca pravaravīreśāḥ| taireva samuparuddhaṃ yattripuraṃ tasya dāhaka he bhagavañjayeti|
tathākhilānāṃ surāṇāmīśāno brahmā tasya yacchiraḥ tasya cchedaḥ purāṇetihāsādibhiruktastena bhayānako raudramūrtiḥ tasya sambodhanam|
kiṃ ca sakalatrailokyamohakatvena yaḥ prathitasāmarthyo manmathaḥ kāmastasya bhogādisthitihetutvātsthitiḥ śarīraṃ tasya nāśana he bhagavan jayeti|
api cācyutasya viṣṇostanudhvaṃsanahetutvāttanudhvaṃsaḥ kālakūṭastasya vegastamapaharatīti| yaduktaṃ vāyupurāṇe
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The two broad shoulders (<s>skandhas</s>) of the great demon <s>Andhaka</s> — the bond is their complex configuration; its sundering is the tearing apart [of that bond]. The one who is skilled in that — it is you alone, none other. The address to him: 'O such blessed one, victory!' Furthermore, those who have the most excellent boon, granted by <s>Brahmā</s>, are the foremost heroes (<s>pravaravīreśas</s>); the <s>Tripura</s> (three cities) that was besieged by them — its burner: 'O blessed one, victory!' Similarly, the ruler (<s>Īśāna</s>) of all the gods — <s>Brahmā</s>; the severing of his head, as narrated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Itihāsas</s> — the one who is fearsome by that, of terrifying form — such is the address. Furthermore, <s>Manmatha</s> (<s>Kāma</s>), who is renowned for his power to delude the entire three worlds — his body, [which is] the cause of the continued existence of enjoyment and the like — the destroyer of that: 'O blessed one, victory!' Moreover, <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — the destroyer of his body, the cause of the destruction of his body. <s>Kālakūṭa</s> — its force — he removes that. As stated in the <s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s>:
'When the poison, having the radiance of the fire of cosmic dissolution, had just arisen,

body.text:
tasya balānyapaharatīti balāpaho yastasya sambodhanam|
kiñca āvartaḥ paribhramastenātyantabhīṣaṇāṭopo vegavatpravāhaḥ sa yasyāḥ saritaḥ prakaraṇājjāhṇavyāḥ sāvartamahāṭopasarit| tasyā vego balaṃ tadvidhāraṇa| kila śirasi tathābhūtā mahānadī bhagavataiva dhāryate nānyenetyatiśayastutiḥ|| 2--4||
body.translated_text: he removes its forces' — thus he is the remover of its power; such is the address. Furthermore, the 'eddy' (<s>āvarta</s>) is the whirlpool; the great tumultuous force of the current-laden river — in this context, the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Gaṅgā) — with its great swirling eddies; its current, its force — the holder of that. Indeed, such a great river is borne on the head of the blessed Lord alone, not by anyone else — this is a superlative praise. || 2-4 ||

body.text:
kiñca dārūṇi devadārūṇi teṣāṃ vane yadudyānamāśramastasminye munayasteṣāṃ teṣāṃ ca yāḥ patnyastāsāṃ vimohaka| avijitakāmakrodhādīnmunīnpatnīśca kenāpi prayojanena vimohayatītyatra praśaṃsārtho 'nyathā kutsaiveyaṃ kutaḥ stutiriti|
tathā nṛttaṃ vicitrābhinayādyātmako gātravikṣepastasya mahārambhalakṣaṇā krīḍā| asya vailakṣaṇyena tāṇḍavarūpaṃ viharaṇam| tayā vikṣobho 'navasthitirjagatastena dāruṇa bhīṣaṇa he bhagavañjayeti| tadidamuktam|
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the <s>dāru</s>s are <s>devadāru</s> trees; in their forest, the grove (<s>udyāna</s>) that is the hermitage — the sages therein, and their wives — the deluder of those [wives]. He deludes the sages, who have not conquered desire, anger, and the like, along with their wives, for some purpose — here the term is meant in a laudatory sense; otherwise this would be censure — how then could it be praise? Similarly, the dance (<s>nṛtta</s>), consisting of various gestures of expression and the like, is the movement of the limbs; the sport characterized by its great commencement — his extraordinary <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance; by that, the agitation, the instability of the universe — the one who is dreadful through that: 'O blessed one, victory!' As it has been said:

body.text:
calati mahī dalanti girayaḥ skhalantyudadhayo namanti khecarā ityādi
tribhuvanamasvatantramiha yasya nṛttasamaye sa pātu no hara ityantam|
body.translated_text: 'The earth trembles, mountains crack, oceans overflow, sky-dwellers bow down' and so on — 'At the time of whose dance the three worlds become powerless — may that <s>Hara</s> protect us.'

body.text:
kiñca ugraṃ bhīṣaṇaṃ yadbhairavākāraṃ rūpamumāsantrāsadānāya ghaṭata itītihāsapurāṇādigītaṃ tasya saṃrambho jagattrāsalakṣaṇābhinayānukārastena trāsitā devāsurā yena tasya sambodhanam|
kiñca krūrajanānāṃ rakṣasāmindro rāvaṇastasyāsyeṣu darśito 'sṛgeva sunirjharaḥ prapāto yena tasyāmantraṇam|
kiñca vīro vīrabhadraḥ tasya parispandaḥ preṣaṇaṃ tena dakṣasya prajāpateryajñavināśana he bhagavañjayeti praśaṃsārtho 'nyathā nindaiva kutsitatvādasyeti|
kiñca adbhutamāścaryabhūtaṃ yanmahāliṅgaṃ sakalatrailokyasya vyāpakaṃ tasya saṃsthānamākāraviśeṣo jvālātmakaḥ tasya balaṃ tejaso 'sahyatvaṃ tena garvita brahmaviṣṇvādibhyo 'pi sātiśaya he bhagavañjayeti| yaduktaṃ vāyupurāṇādau
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the fierce and terrifying form in the shape of <s>Bhairava</s>, assumed to frighten <s>Umā</s>, as sung in the <s>Itihāsas</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like — the fury characterized by the dramatic enactment of cosmic terror — by which the gods and demons were terrified; such is the address. Furthermore, the lord of the cruel ones — <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, king of the <s>Rākṣasas</s> — in whose faces were displayed streams of blood, as it were, cascading forth; such is the address. Furthermore, the hero <s>Vīrabhadra</s> — his exertion, his dispatch — by which the sacrifice of <s>Dakṣa</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> was destroyed: 'O blessed one, victory!' — this is in a laudatory sense; otherwise it would be censure, since [the act] is reprehensible. Furthermore, the wondrous, amazing great <s>liṅga</s> that pervades the entire three worlds — its configuration, the specific form made of flames — its power, the unbearable intensity of its radiance — proud of that, surpassing even <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and others: 'O blessed one, victory!' As stated in the <s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s> and elsewhere:

body.text:
akasmādbrahmaviṣṇvādyairjvālāliṅgaṃ tadadbhutam|
dṛṣṭamabhyudgataṃ yena vyāptaṃ sarvaṃ carācaram|| iti|| 5--7||
body.translated_text: 'Suddenly, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the others saw that wondrous <s>liṅga</s> of flames, which had arisen and pervaded everything, moving and unmoving.' || 5-7 ||

body.text:
kiñca śveto mahāmuniḥ tannimittamugrasya mṛtyudehasya nipātana he bhagavañjayeti|
api cāśeṣasya sukhasyābhiraterāvāsaḥ sthānaṃ kāmastena mohitā śailajā gaurī yeneti kāmo 'pi yasya vaśe gaurī vā sarvalokeśvarī yaṃ prati sābhilāṣeti praśaṃsārthaḥ|
kiñca upamanyoryaḥ santāpa stapojanitaśarīraklamaḥ yacca mohajālameva pañcavidhaviparyayātmakaṃ tamovṛtti tvāttamastaddharati yastasya sambodhanam|
kiñcānyat| pātālānāṃ mūlaṃ kālāgnibhuvanaṃ tata ūrdhvaṃ lokaḥ sthāvarādimanuṣyāntaḥ ṣaḍvidho bhūtasamūhaḥ| alokastu tadvilakṣaṇaḥ piśācādipitā mahānto 'ṣṭavidho daivasargaḥ| yaduktaṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, <s>Śveta</s> is a great sage; on his account, the casting down of the fierce body of Death (<s>Mṛtyu</s>): 'O blessed one, victory!' Moreover, the abode — the dwelling place — of all happiness and delight; by whom the mountain-born <s>Gaurī</s> is enchanted with desire — meaning that even <s>Kāma</s> is under his control, or that <s>Gaurī</s>, the sovereign of all worlds, is desirous toward him — this is in a laudatory sense. Furthermore, the suffering of <s>Upamanyu</s> — the bodily exhaustion produced by austerity — and the net of delusion, which is the fivefold <s>viparyaya</s> (misconception), being a function of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) — the one who removes that darkness; such is the address. Furthermore, the base of the netherworlds (<s>Pātāla</s>) is the realm of <s>Kālāgni</s> (the fire of time); above that, the six kinds of beings from immovable [entities] to humans constitute the world (<s>loka</s>). The non-world (<s>aloka</s>), distinct from that, is the eightfold divine creation — the great ones beginning with <s>Piśācas</s> and ending with the fathers. As stated by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>:
'The divine [creation] is of eight varieties; the animal [creation] occurs in five ways;
the human [creation] is of one kind — such is the material creation in brief.'

body.text:
tasya dāhaketyupalakṣaṇam| sthitisaṃrakṣaṇadānabhavānugrahakartaḥ he bhagavan jaya| jayeti jayatyevāsya śrīkaṇṭhanāthasyādhikārāt|
tadevamapadāna ṣoḍaśakātmikayā stutyā bhagavataḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthasyāsyaiva darśanaṃ, na yogināṃ vidyeśānāṃ vā madhyapaṭhitasyeti darśyate|
tathaitāvadbhirevāpadānairiyaṃ stutirdṛṣṭā nāpadānāntaraiścakraprasādadehārdhagaurīdhāraṇādibhirapīti|
body.translated_text: The word 'burner' is used figuratively [to encompass]: the one who maintains, protects, gives stability, and bestows grace: 'O blessed one, victory!' 'Victory' [means] he alone is victorious, due to the sovereign authority of Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>. Thus, through this praise consisting of sixteen exploits, it is the vision of the blessed Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> alone, not of the yogīs or <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> (lords of knowledge) mentioned in between, that is indicated. And this praise is seen [to consist] of these exploits alone, not of other exploits such as the granting of the discus, the bearing of half [the body of] <s>Gaurī</s>, and the like.

body.text:
andhayatītyandhako malaḥ tasya pṛthuskandhāvūrdhvādhodṛkpratirodhaśaktī tābhyāṃ bandhanaṃ puṃsāṃ dṛkkriyāvarodhaḥ| tasya bhede dīkṣādvāreṇa yo vicakṣaṇastasya sambodhanam| ityevaṃ sarvatheyamatra dīkṣānirvartyakāryastutirgauṇalākṣaṇikayā vṛttyeti vyācakṣate|
teṣāṃ prasiddhasyārthasya parityāge 'trāsiddhasya ca kalpane kiṃ kāraṇamiti vaktavyam| kāraṇaṃ vinaiva hi tathātve sarvatra gauṇamukhyārthāvyavasthitiḥ padavākyayorapratipa ttireva| taduktam|
body.translated_text: That which blinds is <s>Andhaka</s> — [meaning] <s>mala</s> (impurity); its two broad shoulders are the powers of obstruction of upper and lower vision; by these, the bondage of souls is the obstruction of their vision and action. The one who is skilled in sundering that through the means of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) — such is the address. Thus, in every way, this praise here concerns the effects accomplished by <s>dīkṣā</s>, through figurative and secondary meanings — so the [commentators] explain. Against them, it must be asked: what is the reason for abandoning the well-known meaning and constructing an unestablished one? For without a reason, if [one were to apply] such [secondary meanings] everywhere, the determination of figurative and primary meanings of words and sentences would be impossible — there would be no understanding at all. As it has been said:
'There is no overstepping of the primary meaning of a word without a purpose being indicated.'

body.text: narte\devdot laṅghanam Source unknown. Quoted also ad \Mat\VP\ 3:20 and on p.12 of the

body.translated_text: In the venerable <s>Raurava</s> and other [āgamas], since the praise pertains to <s>Paramaśiva</s> (the supreme <s>Śiva</s>), and since <s>Paramaśiva</s> is bodiless and therefore attributes such as bearing a half-moon crest are impossible, the construction of an unestablished meaning is indeed justified — hence there is no contradiction. || 8-9 ||

body.text: atha kiṃ tadvaco yadabravīttārkṣyaḥ stutipūrvaṃ dṛṣṭvetyuktam| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: Now, what are those words that <s>Tārkṣya</s> spoke, having seen [<s>Hara</s>] preceded by praise, as stated? To that it is replied:

children.translated_text: To me, your devotee, who is frightened,
proclaim the supreme knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>,
having obtained which, all people
attain liberation (<s>mukti</s>) alone.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
bhajatīti bhaktaḥ sevakaḥ bibhe tīti ca bhītaḥ|
tasya yadyapi dīkṣayā saṃsārabhītatvamapākīrṇaṃ tathāpi nityanaimittikādikarma coditatvādanuṣṭheya m|
tadananuṣṭhāne viparītānuṣṭhāne vā punarapi saṃsārādbhītatvamastyeva| yaduktam
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: One who serves (<s>bhajati</s>) is a devotee (<s>bhakta</s>); and one who fears (<s>bibheti</s>) is frightened (<s>bhīta</s>). Although his fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> has been removed through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), nevertheless the prescribed daily and occasional duties (<s>nityanaimittika karma</s>) must be performed. If these are not performed, or performed incorrectly, fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> remains. As it has been stated:
'Through transgression of the command, the state of being a flesh-eater [in rebirth] for a hundred years is proclaimed.'

body.text: ājñā@\devdot samāḥ Attributed with the expression

nanu vedādijñānānyevaṃ hariharahiraṇyagarbhādyātmakaprasiddhaśivakṛtāni parāṇi bhaviṣyantīti| tadayuktaṃ teṣāmaśivatvarūpamuktyupadeśakatvena śivakṛtatvāsiddheḥ| samalatvameva hyātmanāmaśivatā| tadvirahaḥ kevalitvaṃ śivateti| malakaivalyaṃ ca tairmuktāvupadiṣṭaṃ malasvarūpasyāparicchedāt| aparicchinnasya hartumaśakyatvāditi| yajjñānaṃ prāpya narā muktimāyānti kevalāṃ tadvadeti vedādiśāstraniṣedhaḥ
| \crux sarva iti
body.translated_text: Now [one might object:] the knowledge of the <s>Vedas</s> and the like, being made by <s>Śiva</s> — who is well known as having the form of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and the like — would be supreme? That is not valid, because their being made by <s>Śiva</s> is not established, since they teach liberation in a form that is non-<s>Śiva</s> (impure). For the impurity of souls is itself the state of non-<s>Śiva</s>; freedom from that — the state of being alone (<s>kevalatva</s>) — is <s>Śiva</s>-hood. And the isolation from <s>mala</s> (impurity) that [these systems] teach as liberation is [not genuine], because the true nature of <s>mala</s> has not been ascertained [by them]. Since what has not been ascertained cannot be removed. 'Proclaim that knowledge, having attained which, people reach liberation alone' — thus the <s>Vedas</s> and other scriptures are rejected. 'All' means:

body.text: Testimonium: tathā kiraṇavṛttau bhagavatā rāmakaṇṭhācāryeṇa\devdot (See 1:1.11--12) yadavāpya narāssarva ityatra `sarva iti ``brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāśśūdrā mlecchādyo pi hī''ti śrutyadhikāriṇa eva garutmato dhikāraprakramatassarvapadasyāniyatārthatvād' iti vyākhyātam| {Śaivāgamādimāhātmya
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā mlecchādayo 'pi hi| iti
body.translated_text: <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, <s>Śūdras</s>, <s>Mlecchas</s>, and others indeed —

body.text: śrutyadhikāriṇa eva| garutmato 'dhikāraḥ prakṛtaṃ sarvapadasya niyatārthatvāt\crux | yaduktam
body.translated_text: are those eligible for hearing. The eligibility of <s>Garutmat</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) is the subject at hand, since the word 'all' has a restricted meaning. As stated:
'The meaning, the context, the indicatory mark, and the proximity of another word —
these are declared to be the causes for determining the specific sense of general terms.'

body.text:
evaṃ ca dīkṣitatve 'pyaviditaśāstravivekasya tārkṣyasyāyaṃ praśnastathābhū
taśāstrādhigamāyeti pratīyate na tu jñasyeti||
body.translated_text: Thus, even though [<s>Garuḍa</s>] has been initiated, this question of <s>Tārkṣya</s>, who does not know the discernment of scripture, is understood to be for the purpose of comprehending such a scripture — not [the question] of one who already knows.
Now the reply:

children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, thus addressed, spoke,
the crescent moon blazing on his crest.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ stutipūrvadarśanapūrvakaṃ śāstravi ṣayāvivekapradarśanataḥ śāstraṃ vainateyena paryanuyuktaḥ san savismayatve satyutpannaśiraḥkaṃpatvādviśeṣeṇa sphuraccandraśekharaḥ śrīkaṇṭhadevaḥ prāha|
kiñca prāhetyucyate|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
Thus, preceded by praise and preceded by the vision [of the subject matter], having demonstrated the [student's] lack of discernment regarding the subject of the scripture, the Lord <s>Śrīkaṇṭhadeva</s> — whose crescent moon on the head shimmers with special [radiance] due to the head-nodding [that arose] from his being amazed — when questioned by <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), spoke.
And what does he say? It is stated:

children.translated_text: 'Excellent is what you have asked;
listen to this knowledge of great fruition,
the great <s>tantra</s> called <s>Kiraṇa</s> (Ray),
which bestows the supreme immortal bliss,
which is gracious to all, resplendent,
which illuminates the categories of reality, and is clear.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadetadbhadraṃ sakalānyaśāstraphalavilakṣa ṇaśreyaḥsādhakaṃ śāstraṃ vadeti tvayā pṛ ṣṭaṃ tacchṛṇūcyata iti pratijñā| ata evātra bhadrapadasyaiva maṅgalādyarthatvādādisūtratve 'pi nāthaśabdānupādānāderdoṣaḥ|
mahāṃśca darśanāntarasiddhyānabhibhāvya udayaḥ siddhilakṣaṇo yasmādityanenāsya śāstrasya prayoja namuktam|
ata eva tathābhūtārthaprakāśakatvāt kiraṇākhyametaduktam|
mahacca tatparameśvaraprayuktatvāt| tantramityanenāsya prāmāṇyamuktam|
īśvarakṛtatvenaiva śāstra sya prāmāṇyāt, nākṛtakatvenāsaṃbhavāt| racanā kartāraṃ navyabhicaratīti yataḥ|
paraṃ ca tatsarvārthavyāpakatvādamṛtaṃ cāvinaśvaramiti parāmṛtaṃ yatsukhaṃ parā paripūrṇatā sarvajñatvakartṛtvābhivyaktiḥ|
taddadātītyupāyatvenābhivyanaktītyarthaḥ|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
This scripture, which is 'excellent' (<s>bhadra</s>) — a means to the highest good, which is distinct from the fruits of all other scriptures — has been asked about by you; 'listen, it is being stated' — this is the declaration. And therefore, because the word '<s>bhadra</s>' itself serves the purpose of auspiciousness and the like at the beginning, even though [this is] the opening sūtra, there is no fault in not employing the word '<s>nātha</s>' (lord) [etc.].
The great [fruition] — an attainment that cannot be surpassed by the accomplishments of other philosophical systems — is the result (<s>udaya</s>) characterized by <s>siddhi</s> (spiritual accomplishment); by this, the purpose of this scripture is stated.
For this reason, because it illuminates realities of such a nature, it is called <s>Kiraṇa</s> (Ray).
It is 'great' (<s>mahat</s>) because it is propounded by the Supreme Lord. By the word '<s>tantra</s>', its authoritativeness is stated.
For the authoritativeness of scripture derives from its being made by the Lord, not from being uncreated — since that is impossible; for composition does not deviate from [requiring] a composer.
'Supreme' (<s>para</s>) because it pervades all meanings; and 'immortal' (<s>amṛta</s>) means imperishable — the supreme bliss is the supreme fullness, the manifestation of omniscience and agency.
'It gives that' means 'it reveals that as a means' — this is the meaning.

body.text: Testimonium: śrīmatā rāmakaṇṭhena kiraṇavṛttau kiraṇākhyaṃ mahātantraṃ parāmṛtasukhapradaṃ| ityatra parañca tat sarvārthavyāpakatvādamṛtañcāvinaśvaraṃ| yatsukhaṃ| parā paripūrṇatā sarvajñatvasarvakarttṛtvābhivyaktiḥ taddadātyupāyatvenābhivyanaktīti parāmṛtasukhapradamiti| J\ñānaprakāśa's

śubhramiti vakṣyamāṇapādacatuṣṭayaśobhāyuktatvāt| na tvānarthakyalūnaviśīrṇātmakamiti viśi ṣṭasvarūpakathanam| padārthā artharāśayaḥ ṣaṭ paśvādayo vakṣyamāṇāsteṣāmuddyotakamityanenāsyābhidheyakatha
nam| sphuṭamityanena saṃhitāntarebhyo 'sya viśeṣaḥ|
tāni hyasphuṭaṃ kṛtvā padārthānāmuddyotakānyatastairagatārthatvamityarthaḥ|
evaṃ ca svarūpāgatārthatvaprāmāṇyādhikārisambandhābhidheyaprayojanāni śāstrasyoktānīti pratijñārūpa metadevādisūtram
athāto 'nādi madhyāntetyādi śrīmadraurava
body.translated_text:
'Resplendent' (<s>śubhra</s>) because of its being endowed with the beauty of the four chapters to be described; but [this means] not that it is worthless, broken, or decayed — this is a statement of its distinctive nature. The 'categories' (<s>padārthas</s>) are groups of meanings — the six, beginning with <s>paśu</s>, to be described — 'illuminating them' — by this, the subject matter (<s>abhidheya</s>) of [the scripture] is stated. 'Clear' (<s>sphuṭa</s>) — by this, the distinction of this [scripture] from other <s>saṃhitās</s> is [indicated].
For those [other saṃhitās] illuminate the categories unclearly, and therefore have unascertained meaning — this is the meaning.
Thus, the nature, ascertained meaning, authoritativeness, qualified student, relation, subject matter, and purpose of the scripture have been stated — and this opening sūtra itself has the form of a declaration.
[Like] 'Now, therefore, that which is without beginning, middle, or end' etc. in the glorious <s>Raurava</s>.

body.text:
atha kiṃ tasya śubhratvam| kīdṛśāśca te padārthā yeṣāmetaddyotakamuktam|
kiyatsaṃkhyāśce ti tadarthametatpratijñāsūtrāntaram||
body.translated_text: Now, what is its 'resplendence'? And of what nature are those categories that this is said to illuminate? And how many are they? For this purpose, this is another declaration-sūtra:

children.translated_text: '<s>Paśu</s> (the bound soul), <s>pāśa</s> (the bond), <s>pati</s> (the Lord), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) —
it sets forth the investigation [of these];
endowed equally with <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action) and <s>caryā</s> (conduct),
it brings the fullness of <s>yoga</s> and supernatural powers (<s>bhūti</s>).'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
paśuśabdo nirmalānāmaprayogātsamalānāmevātmanāmabhidhāyakaḥ|
te ca bahavo 'pi sakalākalabhedena dvirūpāḥ| tatra sakalā dvirūpāḥ sūkṣmadehāḥ sthūladehāśca|
akalā api vijñānākalāḥ pralayākalāśceti dvirūpā eva| te sarva eva paśavaḥ paśuśabdavācyāḥ tāvadatraikaḥ padārthaḥ paśurityucyate|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
The word '<s>paśu</s>' (bound soul), because it is not used for the pure [souls], designates only the impure selves (<s>ātmans</s>).
Though they are many, they are of two kinds through the distinction of <s>sakala</s> (with parts) and <s>akala</s> (without parts). Among these, the <s>sakalas</s> are of two kinds: those with subtle bodies and those with gross bodies.
The <s>akalas</s> too are of two kinds: <s>vijñānākalas</s> and <s>pralayākalas</s>. All of these are <s>paśus</s> — denoted by the word <s>paśu</s>. This is the first category, called <s>paśu</s>.
The <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) are:

body.text: Testimonium: pāśastu malakarmamāyayosteṣāṃ paśūnāṃ trividhā| iti rāmakaṇṭhe (sic)\Isana\ Vol.III, p.23.
55cd,which reads bhogādvā karmaṇaḥ kṣayāt to give a metrical last {pāda}.

māyīyastu kalādikṣityantatriṃśattattvātmakaḥ pratipuruṣaṃ sūkṣmadehātmanā bhinno navatyadhikaśatatrayabhuvanātmanā cābhinnaḥ pratibhuvanaṃ bhūtātmaka sthūladehatvena bhinnaścābhinnaśca sthūladehasyātmāntarairapi bhogyatvādityapi nivedayiṣyāmaḥ| māyāpi pāśayonitvātpāśaḥ| tirobhāvanaśaktirapi māyāgarbhādhikārīśvarābhivyaktā pāśa evetyetāvadarthajātamatra dvitīyaḥ padārthaḥ pāśa ityucyate|
body.translated_text: The <s>māyīya</s> (derived from <s>māyā</s>) — consisting of the thirty-one <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>kalā</s> to <s>kṣiti</s> (earth) — is differentiated for each individual soul as the subtle body, and undifferentiated as the three hundred and ninety worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>); and differentiated for each world as the gross body consisting of the elements, and also undifferentiated — and the gross body can also be enjoyed by other selves, as we shall explain. <s>Māyā</s> too, being the source of bonds, is a <s>pāśa</s>. The power of concealment (<s>tirobhāvana-śakti</s>) too, manifested by the presiding lord within <s>Māyā</s>, is indeed a <s>pāśa</s>. This entire collection of meanings constitutes the second category, called <s>pāśa</s>.
<s>Pati</s> (the Lord) is the blessed <s>Śiva</s>, through the twofold division of the <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s> <s>tattvas</s>, and through the fivefold division of worlds (<s>bhuvanas</s>).

body.text:
vicārayati puruṣakarmānusāreṇa jagataḥ sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇātmanaḥ sṛṣṭisaṃhārādikamiti vicāro 'tra pañcamapadārthatayā vidyā vidyeśātmakatattvadvayarūpaṣaḍviṃśatibhuvanabhedabhinno 'rtharāśiḥ pratipādyate|
eṣāṃ pañcānāṃ padārthānāṃ pratipādakaṃ śāstraṃ vidyāpādātmakaṃ śṛṇviti pratijñātārthānuṣaṅgaḥ| na tu paśupāśapatīnāṃ yat jñānaṃ yaśca vicāro 'numānaṃ tayoḥ pratipādakametacchāstraṃ śṛṇviti vyākhyeyam|
śāstrasya śabdātmakatvenānanvayāt| na hi śabdāt jñānaṃ pratīyate| \crux vācakatvenāsya vācyasaṃketitvāt\crux | api tvartha eva| jñānaṃ tu tato 'numeyam|
body.translated_text:
[The Lord] investigates — that is, [performs] creation, dissolution, and the like of the world, both common and individual, in accordance with the <s>karma</s> of individual souls. Thus the 'investigation' (<s>vicāra</s>) — here as the fifth category, <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is set forth, consisting of the two <s>tattvas</s> of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>vidyeśvara</s>, differentiated into twenty-six worlds.
The scripture that teaches these five categories, consisting of the <s>vidyāpāda</s> (knowledge section) — 'listen' is connected with the previously declared content. But [the sūtra] should not be interpreted as: 'This scripture teaches the knowledge of, and investigation (inference) about, <s>paśu</s>, <s>pāśa</s>, and <s>pati</s> — listen.'
Because the scripture, being of the nature of words, does not [directly] lead to [inferential] knowledge. For knowledge is not derived from words [directly] — because [words] are signifiers of designated objects. Rather, [the scripture teaches] the objects themselves; knowledge is to be inferred from that.

body.text:
atha jñānaśabdo 'trārthātpaśvādijñānahetau vākye prayukto vicāraśabdo 'pi tadanumānahetau liṅga iti vyākhyāyate|
\crux evamapi rūḍhārthatyāgenānayoratra pravṛtteraviśeṣādvaraṃ\crux\
padārtha viṣayataiva yukteti| padārthānāṃ pañcatvasiddhiḥ| yaduktaṃ śrīmadraurave
body.translated_text:
Now, the word '<s>jñāna</s>' here is applied in the sentence as the cause of knowledge of <s>paśu</s> and the rest, and the word '<s>vicāra</s>' is interpreted as the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) which is the cause of inferring that.
Even so, since there is no difference between these [interpretations] — both involving the abandonment of the conventional meaning — it is better [to take them] as referring to the categories themselves. Thus the five-fold nature of the categories is established. As stated in the glorious <s>Raurava</s>:
'The categories are well-known as five, born from the mouth of <s>Vidyeśvara</s>:' ||

body.text: padārthāḥ\devdot samāsataḥ \RauS\ 4:48; cf. vidhiḥ kriyā kalā yogaḥ śivaśceti samāsataḥ| padārthāḥ pañca vijñeyāḥ śaivaśāstre hyanuttare quoted by Alaka ad

body.translated_text: '<s>Vidhi</s> (ordinance), <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>kalā</s>, <s>yoga</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> — in brief.'

body.text:
iti pūrvaiva vyākhyā yuktā| kriyā karaṇaṃ saṃskaraṇaṃ dīkṣeti| caryā caraṇaṃ nityādikarmānuṣṭhānaṃ tābhyāṃ samaṃ tulyatvenopetaṃ kriyācaryātmakapādadvaya yuktamapyetacchāstraṃ śṛṇvityarthaḥ|
yo yogaścetaso dhyeyenārthena sambandhastadviṣayaḥ samādhirekāgratārūpo vā
tasya bhūtiḥ pratyāhārādyaṅgāvaikalyena bhavanaṃ tasyābharo 'nantaphalāvirbhāvaḥ
tamāvahati yacchāstraṃ tacchṛṇviti caturthasya pādasya pratijñetyarthādatra pādasaṃkhyāpi pratītā| kriyādipādatrayapratipādyaścārthaḥ
ṣaṣṭhaḥ padārthaḥ kathyate yaḥ śrīmataṅgādāvupāyapadārthatvenoktaḥ|
arthatathātvasthitiśca saṃhitāntarātsaṃhitāntara saṃśayaviṣayeṣu yuktaikakartṛkatvācchrutyādiśāstreṣvivetya doṣaḥ|
tadevaṃ
body.translated_text:
Thus the previous interpretation is appropriate. <s>Kriyā</s> means ritual — the consecration (<s>saṃskaraṇa</s>) that is initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>). <s>Caryā</s> means conduct — the performance of regular and other rites. 'Endowed equally with' these two — meaning the scripture, though consisting of two chapters on <s>kriyā</s> and <s>caryā</s>, [should be heard] — this is the meaning of 'listen.'
<s>Yoga</s> is the connection of the mind with the object of meditation — the subject of which is <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), in the form of one-pointedness.
Its '<s>bhūti</s>' (prosperity) is its coming-into-being through the completeness of its limbs such as <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal) and the rest. Its 'fullness' (<s>bhara</s>) is the manifestation of infinite fruits.
The scripture that brings this — 'listen' — thus the declaration of the fourth chapter [is made]; and thereby the number of chapters is also understood. The content taught in the three chapters on <s>kriyā</s> and the rest
is the sixth category, which is stated as the category of 'means' (<s>upāya</s>) in the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> and elsewhere.
The constancy of the meaning of things is [determined] from one <s>saṃhitā</s> to another; in matters of doubt between <s>saṃhitās</s>, [since they share] a single author, [consistency is maintained] — this is not a fault in the <s>śruti</s> and other scriptures.
Thus:
'This scripture has four chapters and teaches six categories.'
This is the meaning of the incidental declaration-sūtra.
Here [follows] the initial objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>):

children.translated_text: 'If this is so, then that <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) —
of what nature is it? How is it bound?
How is it liberated? Please explain
for the removal of doubt.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadyevaṃ paśvādayaḥ ṣaṭpadārthāstvayā vyākhyeyatvenoddiṣṭāḥ|
tatra yaḥ prathamapadārthatvena saṅgṛhītaḥ paśuḥ sa kīdṛśa iti tasya tāvallakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyaṃ yataḥ
saugatairasau pratikṣaṇaṃ dhvaṃsitvena vijñānasantānātmakaḥ|
vedāntavidbhiśca kaiścidbrahmakāryatvenānitya iṣyate|
naiyāyikādibhistu nityaḥ| tathā cārvākaiścaturmahābhūtātmakaḥ|
vaiśeṣikādibhistu tadvilakṣaṇaḥ| tathā sāṃkhyaistu baddhāvasthāyāṃ muktyavasthāyāmiva jñatvasvabhāvaścākartā ca|
jaiminīyādibhistu jñaḥ kartā ceti|
naiyāyikādibhiśca buddhisukhaduḥkhecchādveṣaprayatnadharmādharmasaṃskārairnavabhirguṇairyuktaḥ|
sāṃkhyaistu nirguṇaḥ| evaṃ puruṣakāravādibhiḥ prabhuḥ svatantraḥ | daivavādibhiścāsvatantraḥ| tathā digambarairjīvotpattivādibhiśca vedāntavidbhiravyāpakaḥ| naiyāyikādibhiśca vyāpaka ityevamanekāpratiṣṭhitakuyuktyadhigamātsaṃśayo 'smākam|
tatastannivṛttyarthamākhyātavyaṃ bhavatā ko 'tra pakṣaḥ sarvajñenānena darśanenānugṛhīto ya āgamasaṃvāditvātpramāṇaṃ
ko vānanugṛhīto ya āgamaviruddhatvādapramāṇamiti|
kiñca badhyate kathamiti kena pra kāreṇa| kiṃ naiyāyikādīnāmiva śarīrendriyairevātha sāṃkhyādīnāmiva buddhyādibhirapīti saṃśayaḥ|
kiñca mucyate kathamiti kiṃ jñānenaiva sāṃkhyādīnāmiva| kiṃ yogena pātañjalādīnāmiva sannyāsena vā vedāntavādināmiva kriyayā vā jaiminīyā nāmiva|
yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
If this is so — if the six categories beginning with <s>paśu</s> have been indicated by you as the subject to be explained —
then the <s>paśu</s> that has been included as the first category: of what nature is it? — its definition must first be stated. Because:
According to the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>), it is a continuum of consciousness that perishes every instant.
According to some <s>Vedāntins</s>, it is non-eternal, being an effect of <s>Brahman</s>.
According to the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, it is eternal. According to the <s>Cārvākas</s>, it consists of the four great elements.
According to the <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> and others, it is different from those [elements]. According to the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, even in the state of bondage, as in the state of liberation, it is by nature a knower and a non-agent.
According to the followers of <s>Jaimini</s> and others, it is both a knower and an agent.
According to the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, it possesses nine qualities: intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), pain (<s>duḥkha</s>), desire (<s>icchā</s>), aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>), effort (<s>prayatna</s>), merit (<s>dharma</s>), demerit (<s>adharma</s>), and latent impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
According to the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, it is without qualities. Thus, according to the proponents of human effort (<s>puruṣakāravādins</s>), it is sovereign and independent; while according to the fatalists (<s>daivavādins</s>), it is not independent. According to the <s>Digambaras</s> and proponents of the origination of the soul, and [some] <s>Vedāntins</s>, it is non-pervading; while according to the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others, it is pervading.
Thus, because of the apprehension of many unstable and fallacious arguments, we have doubt.
Therefore, for its removal, you must explain: which position (<s>pakṣa</s>) is endorsed by this omniscient system — which, being in accordance with scripture (<s>āgama</s>), is a valid means of knowledge — and which is not endorsed — which, being contrary to scripture, is not a valid means of knowledge.
Furthermore, 'how is it bound?' — by what means? Is it by the body and senses alone, as the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others [hold], or also by the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and the like, as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others [hold]? — this is the doubt.
Furthermore, 'how is it liberated?' — is it by knowledge alone, as the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> and others [hold]? Or by <s>yoga</s>, as the <s>Pātañjalas</s> and others [hold]? Or by renunciation, as the <s>Vedāntins</s> [hold]? Or by ritual action, as the followers of <s>Jaimini</s> [hold]?
As they say:
'One should perform the regular and occasional [rites] out of the desire to avoid sin;

body.text: mokṣārthī na pravarteta tatra kāmyaniṣiddhayoḥ|| iti|
body.translated_text: one seeking liberation should not engage in the optional and prohibited [rites].'
Thus, there is doubt regarding these matters too; therefore, it must be explained for the removal [of doubt].
Now, the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>) for the removal of the eightfold doubt:

children.translated_text: 'The <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) is eternal, immaterial, unknowing,
without action, without qualities, not sovereign,
all-pervading, situated within the womb of <s>māyā</s>,
a contemplator of the means of experience.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
nityatvaśrutyātra saugatādimatatiraskāreṇa naiyāyikādidṛṣṭahetūnāmanugrahaḥ|
kiṃ cāmūrta iti| mūrtiḥ kāṭhinyaṃ vidyate yasya sa mūrtaḥ sparśavadarthaḥ
mahābhūtacatuṣṭayātmaka ucyate tadrūpo na bhavatīti bhūtacaitanyavāditiraskāreṇa tadvailakṣaṇyapratipādakasaugatādidṛṣṭahetūnāmanugrahaḥ|
api cājño niṣkriya ityakalāvasthāyāṃ
jñānakriyārahita eva saka lāvasthāyāṃ
cālavaṇaḥ sūpa itivadalpajño 'lpakriyaśceti sāṃkhyādi pratikṣepeṇa
jaiminīyādipakṣānugrahaḥ|
nirguṇa ityanena tu naiyāyikādidṛṣṭabuddhisukhaduḥkhādinavātmaguṇapratikṣepeṇa sāṃkhyādidṛṣṭasya nirguṇatvasyānugrahaḥ|
aprabhurityane nāpyalpaprabhutvaṃ prāgvaducyate|
idānīmarjanīyadṛṣṭādṛṣṭaphalavicitrāgniṣṭomādikarmaviṣaya eva prabhuḥ prāga rjitakarmabhoge tvaprabhureveti puruṣakāradaivavādinordvayorapyekāṃśitayānugrahaḥ|
vyāpītyanenāvyāpakajīvapudgalavādipratikṣepeṇa tadvyāpakavādinaiyāyikādyanugrahaḥ| ityata eva sarvānyāgamadarśanajñatvāt garutmato nātrātmanityatvādisiddhau hetavaḥ kathitāḥ|
tairvināpi sthāṇupuruṣa viṣayasaṃśayasya sthāṇurayamityāptavākyādi vāsyāpi saṃśayasya cakrasyānyatarapakṣānugraheṇa taduktahetvanugraheṇa vā nivṛttisiddhesteṣāmala nupayogāt|
yadivānubhavasiddhatvamane nātmanaḥ pratipādyate anubhavasiddhau hetūnāmanupayogāt yathā ghaṭo 'yaṃ lohitaḥ parivartula ityatrānubhavasiddhatvānnāsya hetuḥ sambhavati|
tathā grāhakātmanyapi parātmaprakāśakatayānubhavasiddheḥ sthairyamanubhavasiddhameva tathāvagamāt| iti kimatra hetunā kāryam|
na ca kṣaṇike tasminkālādāviva vibhramāt sthairyamadhyāropitamiti vācyam|
svātmani kriyāvirodhenāvikalpatvādvikalpānāmadhyāropāsambhavāditi darśitamasmābhirmataṅgavṛttau
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
By the statement of eternality, the <s>Saugata</s> (Buddhist) and other doctrines are set aside, and the arguments adduced by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others are endorsed.
Furthermore, 'immaterial' (<s>amūrta</s>): <s>mūrti</s> (materiality) is solidity — that which possesses it is <s>mūrta</s> (material), meaning an object possessing touch —
it is said to consist of the four great elements; [the soul] is not of that nature — thus, by setting aside the <s>Cārvāka</s> doctrine of consciousness-from-elements, the arguments of the <s>Saugatas</s> and others that establish its distinctness [from matter] are endorsed.
Moreover, 'unknowing' (<s>ajña</s>) and 'without action' (<s>niṣkriya</s>) — in the <s>akala</s> state,
devoid of knowledge and action; but in the <s>sakala</s> state,
like 'the soup is without salt' [meaning it has little salt], having little knowledge and little action — thus, by rejecting the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other [views], the position of the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> and others is endorsed.
'Without qualities' (<s>nirguṇa</s>) — by this, rejecting the <s>Naiyāyika</s> and other view that the nine [attributes] — intellect, pleasure, pain, and the rest — are qualities of the self, the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other view of the self's quality-less nature is endorsed.
'Not sovereign' (<s>aprabhu</s>) — by this too, 'having little sovereignty' is stated as before.
Now, [the soul is] sovereign only with respect to the <s>karmas</s> whose visible and invisible fruits are yet to be acquired, such as <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and the like; but with respect to the enjoyment of previously acquired <s>karma</s>, it is not sovereign — thus both the proponents of human effort and the fatalists are endorsed, each in one aspect.
'All-pervading' (<s>vyāpī</s>) — by this, rejecting the <s>Jain</s> doctrine of non-pervading <s>jīvas</s> (<s>pudgalas</s>) and the like, the <s>Naiyāyika</s> and other view of pervadingness is endorsed. And therefore, precisely because <s>Garuḍa</s> knows all other scriptural systems, the reasons for establishing the eternality of the self and the like are not stated here.
Even without those [reasons], since the doubt regarding 'Is it a post or a person?' is resolved by a trustworthy person's statement 'This is a post,' and since the doubt about a wheel [i.e., a circular argument] is resolved by endorsing one side with its supporting reasons, those [formal proofs] are unnecessary.
Alternatively, by [the statement] 'immaterial,' the self-established nature of the self through experience is being taught — since formal reasons are unnecessary for what is established by experience. Just as in 'This pot is red and round' — since this is established by experience, no reason for it is possible.
Similarly, for the self as grasper, since it is established by experience through its capacity to illumine another self, its permanence too is established by experience alone, being understood as such. So what use is a reason here?
Nor should it be said that in something momentary, permanence is superimposed through error, as in the case of time and the like.
Because in one's own self, due to the impossibility of conceptual construction — since there is a contradiction with activity [if the self were momentary] — and because superimposition of conceptual constructions is impossible, [this has been] shown by us in the <s>Mataṅga-vṛtti</s>.

body.text:
kiñca amūrtatvamasya prāgvadeva mūrtopalakṣitasparśayuktamahābhūtākāraśarīrādanyatvaṃ tadgrāhakatayā prakāśanādityanubhavenaiva
bhūtātmaniṣedhaḥ|
ata eva bhūtodbhūtāccāsya vilakṣaṇatvenānubhavānna bhūtebhyaḥ samutpattiḥ|
pratijanma pūrvatarajanmānubhavasaṃskārotpannasmaraṇapūrvaceṣṭādarśanato 'nāditvena nityatvena siddheśceti pradarśitaṃ rauravavṛttiviveke
body.translated_text:
Moreover, its immateriality — as before — means its being different from the body characterized by touch, marked by materiality, consisting of the four great elements; [this is established] by experience through its being the illuminator [of such objects].
Therefore, since [the self] is also established by experience as being of a different nature from what is produced from the elements, there is no origination of it from the elements.
And it is demonstrated in the <s>Raurava-vṛtti-viveka</s> that [its] eternality is established through its beginninglessness — from the observation, in every birth, of memory arising from the latent impressions of experiences in previous births, and of prior [habitual] actions.
'The first arrangement of the organs, the upward movement of breath,

body.text: ādyaḥ\devdot pūrvavedanām \Vakya\ 1:130. Quoted ad \Paramoksa\ 44 and \Nar\ 1:19, p.45.

body.translated_text: and the striking of the [vocal] places — [these] are not possible without prior experience [from a past life].' ||

body.text:
tathāsya kiñcijjñatvakartṛtvālpaprabhutvam prāgvadanubhavasiddhameva| evaṃ nirguṇatvamapi buddhisukhaduḥkhādīnāṃ kādācitkatvenānubhavato ghaṭāderiva grāhyatvena tadviruddhadharmatayānubhavāt|
sarvadaiva hi krameṇa yugapadvānekagrāhyaviṣaya grāhakarūpamapyabhinnamevātmatattvamanubhavasiddhamiti darśitamasmābhirnareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśe|
body.translated_text: Likewise, its limited knowledge (<s>kiñcijjñatva</s>), limited agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), and limited lordship (<s>alpaprabhutva</s>) are established through experience, as before. Similarly, its quality-less nature (<s>nirguṇatva</s>) is also [established]: since <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), pleasure, pain, and the like are experienced as occasional, like a pot and the like, being objects of apprehension and of a nature contrary to [the <s>Ātman</s>], [its quality-less nature is established]. For it has been demonstrated by us in the <s>Nareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśa</s> that the <s>Ātman</s>-reality, though undivided, is of the nature of the grasper of multiple objects of apprehension — sequentially or simultaneously — and is established through experience at all times.
That substance whose real existence is unlimited by place and time,
that [the Śaivas] consider to be eternal and all-pervading — hence the all-pervasiveness and eternity of the <s>Ātman</s>.

body.text: anubhavata eva sarvadharmayuktasyāsya siddhiriti darśayituṃ nātra hetavaḥ kathitāḥ| śrutirapyevamāha
body.translated_text: Since its establishment as possessing all attributes is through experience alone, no [separate] proofs are stated here. Scripture too says the same:

body.text: tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti|
body.translated_text: 'Everything shines forth following Its shining; by Its light all this is illuminated.'

body.text: tameva bhāntamanubhāti sarvaṃ tasya bhāsā sarvamidaṃ vibhāti

ityavirodhaḥ| tadevaṃ parasparaviruddhārthānekapaśudarśanajanitaṃ paśuviṣayasaṃśayaṣaṭkaṃ tāvadapākṛtya svadarśanaprasiddhamevāsyāvasthābhedena sthānavaicitryamucyate|
māyāyā udarañcāntaśca tayoḥ sthita iti|
tatra māyodare pralayakevalī sthitaḥ| māyāprānte tanmastake tu vijñānakevalīti bhedaḥ| māyodaramevānta iti tu vyākhyāyamāne viśeṣaṇamaphalameva|
ata eva pralayakevaligatatvena praśno bhaviṣyati|
sthito māyodare kathamiti|
body.translated_text: Thus there is no contradiction. Having thus set aside the sixfold doubt concerning the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul), generated by the many views of [various] <s>paśu</s>-doctrines that have mutually contradictory meanings, the diversity of states well-known in our own doctrine is now stated according to the difference in its conditions: 'Situated within the womb of <s>Māyā</s> and at its [outer] boundary.' There, the <s>pralayakevalin</s> (soul in dissolution) is situated within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, while the <s>vijñānakevalin</s> (soul endowed with knowledge) is at the boundary, at its crown — this is the distinction. If, however, 'within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>' is interpreted as meaning simply 'within,' the qualifier would be fruitless. Therefore the question will arise [later] regarding the <s>pralayakevalin</s> state: 'How is one situated within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>?'
Now [begins] the resolution of the doubt: 'How is one bound?'

children.translated_text: Of that impure one, the connection
<s>Kalā</s> comes from <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tasyetyanena prakṛtasya paśoreva parāmarśaḥ|
nātrāśuddhasya malayuktasyeti vyākhyeyam|
nāpi kalādiyuktasya sakalasya anukrameṇa vakṣyamāṇatvāt|
api tu malakarmayuktasyeti tato 'yamarthaḥ --- tasya paśormalakarmayuktasyaiva kalā sambandhamāyāti na tu karmarahitasya vijñānakevalinaḥ| yadvakṣyati
bhogaṃ bhuṅkte svakarmata iti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: By 'of that' (<s>tasya</s>), there is reference to the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) under discussion. Here, it should not be interpreted as 'of the impure one, i.e., the one endowed with <s>mala</s> (impurity).' Nor [should it mean] 'of the <s>sakala</s>, i.e., the one endowed with <s>kalā</s> and the rest,' because that will be stated sequentially later. Rather, [it means] 'of the one endowed with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s>,' and therefore the meaning is: <s>Kalā</s> comes into connection with that <s>paśu</s> who is endowed with <s>mala</s> and <s>karma</s> alone, but not with the <s>vijñānakevalin</s>, who is free from <s>karma</s>. As [the text] will state: 'He experiences enjoyment from his own <s>karma</s>.'

body.text: nanu kalaiva tāvadasiddheti kutastasyāḥ preraṇataḥ kartā sidhyatīti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: Objection: But <s>Kalā</s> itself is not yet established — so how can the agent be established through its impelling? To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: By that [<s>Kalā</s>], his consciousness is empowered;
[his] range of objects is manifested by [the tattva called] <s>Vidyā</s>;
tinged by <s>Rāga</s> (attachment),
and [connected] with <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) of the nature of the <s>guṇas</s>,
the host of instruments [beginning with] <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) —
through the connection [with all these], the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) is bound.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tayā kalayodbalitaṃ malanivṛttidvāreṇa samarthīkṛtaṃ caitanyaṃ yasya puṃsaḥ sa tathoktaḥ| etaduktaṃ bhavati --- vakṣyamāṇasya yuktisiddhasya puṃso dṛkkriyāvaraṇātmano malasyāvaśyaṃ sakalāvasthāyāṃ kaścitparimito 'rtho nivarttako 'bhyupagantavyaḥ|
anyathā pralaya kevalināṃ muktānāmiva saṃvedanasya kiñcidviṣayasyānubhūyamānasyānupapattiḥ|
sa ca na tāvatpuruṣaḥ prāgvadaśakteḥ| nāpi karma ata eva bhogānyathānupapattisiddheśca|
na hi yatkāryāntarānyathānupapattyā saṃsiddhasattākamatyantātīndriyaṃ
vastu tatkāryāntarakāraṇatvena śakyamadhyavasātumanekendriyādikāraṇāntarakḷpterapyabhāvaprasaṅgāt|
ata eva nendriyādi neśvaro veti yastasya nivartakaḥ sā kaleti kalālakṣaṇena tāvadbandhena prathamaṃ badhyata iti|
tadanu vidyākhyāpito gocaro viṣayo yasya sa tathoktaḥ| vinivṛttamalasyāpi hi puṃsaḥ smṛtipratibhāvikalpādivakṣyamāṇabuddhivṛttyātmakasaṃvittau avaśyaṃ karaṇāntareṇa bhavitavyaṃ saṃvittitvādindriyārthasaṃvittivat|
na cātra buddhiḥ karaṇaṃ karmatvāttasyāḥ|
na cāpyahaṃkārādayaḥ teṣāṃ śarīradhāraṇādikriyāntara karaṇatvena vakṣyamāṇatvādatrāpi karaṇatvāsiddher \crux ityuktam\crux |
ato yattatra karaṇaṃ sā vidyeti bandhāntarasiddhiḥ|
kiñca rāgeṇābhiṣvaṅgātmanā rañjito baddhaḥ|
ayamarthaḥ --- yo 'yaṃ viṣaya viṣayo rāgo 'bhiṣvaṅgātmako nāyaṃ viṣayadharmo 'dhyātmanyeva parispanddātmakatvādvītarāgābhāvaprasaṅgācca|
nāpyavairāgyalakṣaṇo buddhidharmaḥ|
tasya bhāvātmakatayā vāsanārūpatvenāvasthiterasaṃvedyatvāt|
nāpi tadvṛttyātmakaḥ abhilaṣaṇīyatānusandhāne 'pi vītarāgasya tadadarśanāt|
nāpi karmādīnāṃ malanivṛttyādivadityuktam|
pāriśeṣyādyasya dharmaḥ sa rāgo 'nyo bandhaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: By that <s>Kalā</s>, [the soul's] consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>) is 'empowered' — made capable through the doorway of the removal of <s>mala</s> (impurity) — the person whose [consciousness] is thus is so called. What is stated amounts to this: for the soul, whose <s>mala</s> is of the nature of obstructing perception and action, which will be established through reasoning, some limited agent for its removal must necessarily be accepted in the <s>sakala</s> (fully-bound) state. Otherwise, for the <s>pralayakevalins</s>, the experience of any object of awareness — which is indeed experienced — would be impossible, just as it would be for the liberated. And that [agent] is not the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) itself, because of its powerlessness as before. Nor is it <s>karma</s>, for the same reason, and because the impossibility of experience is otherwise established [as proving karma's existence]. For a thing whose existence is established through the impossibility of otherwise [explaining] one effect, and which is utterly beyond the senses, cannot be determined as the cause of another effect — because then even the non-existence of other causes such as sense-organs and the like would follow. Therefore, that which removes [the obstruction of mala] is not sense-organs and the like, not the Lord — whoever that remover is, that is <s>Kalā</s>. Thus, through the bond characterized as <s>Kalā</s>, [the soul] is first bound. Then, [the soul] whose range of objects is 'manifested by <s>Vidyā</s>' is so called. For even when the <s>mala</s> of the soul has been removed, there must necessarily be some other instrument for [achieving] awareness consisting of the cognitive modifications of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) — such as memory, intuition, conceptual thought, and the like, which will be described — just as [an instrument is needed] for sense-object awareness, because of its being awareness. And here <s>buddhi</s> is not the instrument, because it is the object [of awareness]. Nor are <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego) and the rest, because they will be described as instruments for other activities such as sustaining the body, and since their instrumentality for this [awareness] is not established \crux as stated\crux. Therefore, that which is the instrument for that [awareness] is <s>Vidyā</s> — thus another bond is established. Moreover, [the soul is] 'tinged by <s>Rāga</s>' — bound by attachment, whose nature is clinging. The meaning is: this <s>Rāga</s>, which is attachment of the nature of clinging toward objects, is not a property of the objects, because it is of the nature of activity in the inner self, and because the absence of the desireless [state] would follow [if it were]. Nor is it a property of <s>buddhi</s> characterized by non-dispassion, because being of the nature of a disposition, abiding in the form of a latent impression, it would be unknowable. Nor is it [a modification] of <s>buddhi</s>'s activity, because even in the investigation of what is desirable, the desireless person does not experience it. Nor does it belong to <s>karma</s> and the rest — as has been said, like the removal of <s>mala</s>. By the process of elimination, that whose property it is — that <s>Rāga</s> — is another bond.

body.text:
tataḥ pradhānaṃ sattvādiguṇākāreṇa sthūlabhuvanākāreṇa ca
sambadhyate| caśabdātkālādīnyapi vakṣyamāṇapṛthivyantatattvasahitāni svasvaguṇātmanā bhuvanākāreṇa ca sambadhyanta iti|
tattvasargavadbhuvanasargo 'pyatra bandhatvenoktaḥ|
tataśca buddhyādīni yāni sāṃkhyādiprasiddhāni buddhyahaṃkāramanolakṣaṇāni karaṇāni ca yāni ca pañcabuddhīndriyapañcakarmendriyarūpāṇyanīkaṃ ca yatsamūhātmakaṃ bhūtatanmātrātmakaṃ daśavidhaṃ kāryāntaraṃ tatsambandhāt baddhyata iti sāṃkhyādiprasiddhasya buddhyādervakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa bandhasyānugrahaḥ na tu vaiśeṣikādidṛṣṭasya dehendriyātmana eveti|
ata eva cātra darśanāntarāprasiddhānāṃ kalādīnāmeva bandhānāṃ kāryadvāreṇopanyāso 'prasiddhatvādeva tatprasiddhānāṃ cānuvādamātrameveti na teṣāṃ lakṣaṇānabhidhānādavyāptidoṣa iti|
ata eva niyatyātmano 'pi bandhasya kāryadvāreṇa svarūpam upanyasyate
tato niyatītyādi
body.translated_text: Then <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), in the form of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest — and in the form of the gross worlds, is connected [with the soul]. By the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>), <s>Kāla</s> (time) and the rest, together with the <s>tattvas</s> ending with <s>Pṛthivī</s> (earth) which will be described, are also connected [with the soul] in their respective <s>guṇa</s>-forms and in the form of worlds. Thus the creation of worlds, like the creation of <s>tattvas</s>, is also stated here as a form of bondage. And then, through the connection with the host of instruments (<s>anīka</s>) — namely, <s>Buddhi</s> (intellect), <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego), and <s>Manas</s> (mind), which are the instruments well-known in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other [systems], and the ten [organs] in the form of the five cognitive senses and five action senses, and the tenfold [group of] effects consisting of the gross elements and subtle elements (<s>tanmātras</s>) — [the soul] is bound. Thus the [concept of] bondage through <s>buddhi</s> and the rest, well-known in <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and other systems, is endorsed in the manner to be described, but not [the bondage] of the body and senses alone as seen in <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and other systems. And therefore, the bonds of <s>Kalā</s> and the rest, which are unknown in other doctrines, are presented here through their effects, precisely because they are not well-known; while those [bonds] well-known in those [other systems] are merely restated — hence there is no fault of under-extension through the non-description of their definitions. Therefore, the nature of the bond called <s>Niyati</s> (necessity) too is presented through its effects:

children.translated_text: Then, through connection with <s>Niyati</s> (necessity),
even in what is self-acquired, one is regulated.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tataḥ kāryakaraṇasambandhādanantaraṃ niyatyā yaḥ saṃśleṣaḥ sambandhastato hetoḥ prāgarjite karmaphale niyamyate puruṣaḥ|
ayamarthaḥ---karmaphalaṃ prati niyamaḥ puṃsāṃ na karmahetukaḥ tasya kṛṣyādikarmavat svaphalajananamātra evopayogāt|
nāpi tattvāntarahetuḥ svakāryaireva teṣāṃ siddheḥ kāryāntarahetutve pramāṇābhāvādityuktam|
ataḥ kṛṣyādau rājaniyuktenevātrāpi kenacinniyāmakena bhavitavyam|
yo 'sau niyāmakaḥ sa niyatyākhyo 'paro bandhaḥ|
ata evāsya māyākāryatvena vakṣyamāṇasyāpi kāryakaraṇasambandhottarakālaṃ vyāpāra iti paścādatra nirdeśaḥ| tathā kālasyāpītyadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: 'Then' — immediately after the connection with effects and instruments — through the connection with <s>Niyati</s>, by that cause, the soul is regulated with respect to the fruit of <s>karma</s> acquired previously. The meaning is: the regulation (<s>niyama</s>) of souls with respect to the fruit of <s>karma</s> is not caused by <s>karma</s> [itself], because <s>karma</s>, like agricultural work, is useful only for the mere production of its own fruit. Nor is it caused by another <s>tattva</s>, because those [tattvas] are established by their own effects alone, and there is no proof for their being causes of other effects — as has been said. Therefore, as in agriculture where there must be some regulator appointed by the king, so too here there must be some regulator. That regulator is the other bond called <s>Niyati</s>. Therefore, even though this [<s>Niyati</s>] will be described as an effect of <s>Māyā</s>, its operation [occurs] after the connection with effects and instruments — hence it is mentioned afterward here. The same applies to <s>Kāla</s> (time) — there is no fault.
Now, in what manner is one regulated by <s>Niyati</s>? It is said:

children.translated_text: Through <s>Kāla</s> (time), the reckoning of time,
deluded regarding the effect-enjoyments.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
kālasya sambandhi yatsaṃkhyānalakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ cirakṣiprādi na tu diśaḥ krośayojanādi nāpi saṃkhyāyāḥ śatasahasrādi tena hetunā kālena bhoge mohito yaḥ sa niyatyā niyamyate| kālasyāpi bhogahetutvāt| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: That which is related to <s>Kāla</s> (time) — the effect characterized as reckoning — [consisting of] 'long' and 'short' and the like, but not of direction — [measured in] <s>krośas</s>, <s>yojanas</s>, and the like, nor of number — hundreds, thousands, and the like — by that cause, namely <s>Kāla</s>, one who is deluded regarding enjoyment is regulated by <s>Niyati</s>; because <s>Kāla</s> too is a cause of enjoyment. As they say:

body.text: cireṇa bata labdhāsi na jāne karavāṇi kim|
body.translated_text: 'After so long, at last I have obtained you — I know not what I should do;

body.text: cireṇa bata\devdot nigirāmi kim Source unknown. Also quoted with bhavantīṃ for pibāmi ad \Mat\VP\ 12:20--1, p.346.
praviśāmi kimaṃgeṣu pibāmi nigirāmi kim|| iti|
body.translated_text: should I enter into [your] limbs, should I drink [you], should I swallow [you]?'

body.text: sa ca bhogahetutvenāprasiddhatvādatra kāryadvāreṇopanyastaḥ| svarūpeṇa vaiśeṣikādisiddho 'pi| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: And because [<s>Kāla</s>] is not well-known as a cause of enjoyment, it is presented here through its effects. In its own nature, however, it is well-known in <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and other [systems]. As they say:
'<s>Kāla</s> is [that] whose mark is the cognition of 'long' and 'short.''

body.text: p.63, lines 15--16.} or a paraphrase of {Vaiśeṣikasūtra} 2.2.7.

yattu tasya nityatvādi tairgīyate yadāhuḥ
nityamekaṃ vibhu dravyaṃ parimāṇaṃ kriyāvatām|
body.translated_text: As for its eternity and the like, as celebrated by them — as they say: 'The knowers of <s>Kāla</s> know <s>Kāla</s> as an eternal, single, all-pervading substance,

body.text: nityamekaṃ\devdot kālavido viduḥ \Vakya\ 3.9.1. Also quoted ad \Mat\VP\ 12:3--4, p.337.

body.translated_text: possessing measure [and] possessing activity, apart from [its] operation.'
That [view of its eternality] will be [addressed] since it will be described as an effect of <s>Māyā</s>.
Now, the <s>tattva</s>-nature of <s>Kalā</s> and the rest, their non-pervasiveness, and their being preceded by the gross body, are stated:

children.translated_text: Thus, bound by the <s>tattvas</s> [beginning with] <s>Kalā</s>,
a limited knower, conjoined with a body,
embraced by the delusion of <s>Māyā</s>,
pervaded by it, covered by innate [<s>mala</s>].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tattvāni caitāni kalādikṣityantāni prāguktāni kalāśca tā iti
kāryatvena vakṣyamāṇatvādvyaktatve satyavyāpakatvāt|
body.translated_text: Commentary: These <s>tattvas</s> — from <s>Kalā</s> to <s>Kṣiti</s> (earth) — as previously stated, and those <s>kalās</s> too — because they will be described as effects, being manifest, they are non-pervasive.
'[That which is] caused, impermanent, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent — [such is] the manifest (<s>liṅga</s>);
having parts, dependent — [such is] the manifest; the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite.'

body.text:
tābhirevamuktaprakāreṇa baddhaḥ sakala evāprāptabāhyaśarīraḥ praṇaṣṭabāhyaśarīro vā sūkṣmadehatayetyarthaḥ|
vyāpakatve hyeṣāṃ sūkṣmadehatvānupapattiḥ| yaduktam
body.translated_text: Bound by these in the manner stated above, [the soul] in the <s>sakala</s> state — whether it has not yet obtained a gross body, or has lost a gross body [and exists] as a subtle body — this is the meaning. For if these [tattvas] were pervasive, the subtle-body nature would be impossible. As it was stated: 'The intermediate-state body was rejected by <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>.'
'The intermediate-state body was rejected by <s>Vindhyavāsin</s>.'

body.text:
tattvakalābaddhaḥ sansthūladehasaṃyuktaḥ kiñcijjño bhavati na tu tadabaddha iti sakalasya bhedāntarapratipādanena bhūtasṛṣṭerapi bandhatvamuktam|
sthūladehayuktaśca pumān---māyāyāḥ sambandhī bhujyate anubhūyata iti māyābhogo 'nātmanyātmābhimānarūpo yo mohastena pariṣvakto vyāptaḥ san tanmayo 'nātmanyātmābhimānamayo bhavati|
na kāryakaraṇebhyo vyatiriktamātmānaṃ manyata iti|
idameva tanmāyāyā mohakatvamiti vakṣyāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: Bound by the <s>tattvas</s> [beginning with] <s>Kalā</s>, and conjoined with a gross body, [the soul] becomes a limited knower — but not when unbound by those. By establishing another distinction of the <s>sakala</s> [state], the bondage-nature of elemental creation is also stated. And the person endowed with a gross body — being the experiencer of <s>Māyā</s>, i.e., the delusion (<s>moha</s>) that is the false identification of the non-self as the self, which is called 'the enjoyment of <s>Māyā</s>' — being embraced, pervaded by it, becomes pervaded by it, constituted of the false identification of the non-self as the self. One does not consider the <s>Ātman</s> as distinct from the effects and instruments. This very thing — the deluding power of <s>Māyā</s> — we shall describe.
'Thus the <s>aṇu</s> (atomic soul), standing within the collyrium of <s>Māyā</s>, concealed by its own defects,

body.text: yāti tanmayatāṃ teṣu māyābhogeṣu rañjitaḥ|| iti|
body.translated_text: attains identification with those <s>Māyā</s>-enjoyments, being tinged [by them].'

body.text: malasya tvāvārakatvameva bandhakatvaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ paṭalāderiva pralayakevalādyavasthāyāṃ siddhamityuktam sahajena malenāvṛta iti||
body.translated_text: But the veiling nature of <s>mala</s> (impurity) is itself its binding power — like a cataract upon the eye — which is established in the <s>pralayakevala</s> and other states. This has been stated: 'covered by innate <s>mala</s>.'
Now, the bondage of <s>karma</s>:

children.translated_text: Then, all [experience] beginning with pleasure
— [this] enjoyment one experiences from one's own <s>karma</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tataḥ sthūladehasambandhādanantaraṃ prāgarjita śubhāśubhakarmajanitabhāvapratyayātmanā sukhaduḥkhādikaṃ phalaṃ bhuṅkta iti bhāvasṛṣṭeḥ karmabandharūpatvamuktam|
tathā kṛtsnaṃ niravaśeṣaṃ sarvakarmakṣaye 'pi tatsaṃskāraśeṣeṇa cakrabhramavaddhṛtaśarīratvāttatsaṃvedanamātraṃ bhogaṃ bhuṅkta iti sakalasyāvasthāntaraṃ bandhatvenoktam|
tadiyatā badhyate kathamityetatpraśnasya nirāsāya pāśapadārthaḥ sarvo 'bhihitaḥ||
body.translated_text: Commentary: 'Then' — after the connection with the gross body — one experiences the fruit [consisting of] pleasure, pain, and the like, generated by the mental dispositions produced by previously acquired wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s>. Thus the <s>karma</s>-bondage nature of the creation of mental dispositions (<s>bhāvasṛṣṭi</s>) is stated. Likewise, 'all' means without remainder — even when all <s>karma</s> is exhausted, due to sustaining a body by the residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) [of karma], like a wheel still spinning [after the potter's effort ceases], one experiences the enjoyment that consists merely of awareness. Thus another state of the <s>sakala</s> is stated as a form of bondage. To this extent, 'How is one bound?' — this question has been addressed, and the entire meaning of the term <s>pāśa</s> (bond) has been explained.
Now [begins] the resolution of 'How is one liberated?'

children.translated_text: When <s>karma</s> has become equalized,
through the power of the passage of time, then,
through the descent of intense <s>śakti</s> (power),
when [the soul is] initiated by a <s>guru</s>,
it becomes omniscient, like <s>Śiva</s>,
free from limited knowledge,
complete in the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>-nature,
no longer a worldly being (<s>saṃsārin</s>).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
kālayati kṛṣṇatāṃ nayati malinī karotīti kālo malaḥ|
kālanīlādīnāṃ padānāṃ varṇaviśeṣābhidhāyakatvāt| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: '<s>Kāla</s>' — [here means <s>mala</s>]: that which makes black, leads to blackness, makes impure — [that is] <s>kāla</s>, meaning <s>mala</s> (impurity). Because the words <s>kāla</s>, <s>nīla</s>, and the like denote specific colors. As they say:
'That which, by contact with the Great One, does not undergo any alteration whatsoever —
the sky shines like the Milk Ocean whose darkness has been drunk up by the rays of the moon.'

body.text:
tasyāntaraṃ pariṇāmastasya vaśaḥ sāmarthyaṃ tasmāt kālāntaravaśāt yastīvraḥ śaktipāto na tvasmādbhūtabhaviṣyadādikālāntaravaśāditi tataḥśabdasyārthaḥ|
malaparipākasyaiva śaktipātahetutvāt| yadvakṣyati
body.translated_text: Its (<s>mala</s>'s) 'antara' means transformation; its 'power' (<s>vaśa</s>) means capacity. Therefore, 'through the power of the passage of <s>kāla</s> [i.e., mala]' — the descent of intense <s>śakti</s> is not through the power of another <s>kāla</s> such as past, future, and so forth — this is the meaning of the word 'then' (<s>tataḥ</s>). Because the maturation of <s>mala</s> alone is the cause of the descent of <s>śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>). As [the text] will state:
'Having blocked the power of that [mala], one is made free from the desire for worldly existence.'
In the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [āgama] too:

body.text: kṣīṇe tasminyiyāsā syātparaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prati|| iti|
body.translated_text: 'When that [mala] has been diminished, the desire to proceed toward the supreme good arises.'

body.text:
tena yadasya samamiṣṭanimittamaniṣṭanimittaṃ ca karma|
yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: By 'then' [is meant]: when his <s>karma</s> — both that which is caused by meritorious [actions] and that which is caused by demeritorious [actions] — has become equalized. As they say:
'One who is neither elated by a favor nor angered by an offense.'

body.text: na hṛṣyatyupakāreṇa\devdot ucyate Source unknown, but frequently cited, e.g., by \Agh\ ad \Rat\ 313--4 and in
, IFP T. 985, p.3; by \Narayana\ ad \Mrg\VP\ 5:5, p.136, and in the {anubandha} to vol.1 of the \Mat\ on p.579 and in the {Śataratnollekhanī} p.82.
yaḥ samaḥ sarvabhūteṣu jīvanmuktaḥ sa ucyate|| iti|
body.translated_text: He who is equal toward all beings is called liberated while living (<s>jīvanmukta</s>). || Thus.

body.text:
tasmin sañjāte sati guruṇā mantragaṇeneśvareṇācāryādhikaraṇena dīkṣyate nānyathā|
tathābhūtakarmasamatvaṃ vinācāryasya śaktipātāniścayāt|
na tvatra karmaṇāṃ viruddhaphalānāṃ sāmyaṃ yugapatparipākāttīvravegatvena vā vyākhyeyam|
tannimittasya śaktipātasya mokṣahetutvābhāvāt|
ata evāsau viruddhakarmadvayāpekṣa saṃkaṭāt puṃsāṃ mokṣahetuḥ na bandhāntarāttasya prāgvadaviśeṣāditi darśayiṣyāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: When that [equanimity] has arisen, [the soul] is initiated by the teacher (<s>guru</s>) through the group of <s>mantras</s>, by the Lord, in the role of <s>ācārya</s> (officiating master)—not otherwise. Without such equanimity of <s>karma</s>, the teacher cannot be certain of the descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>). However, this equanimity of <s>karmas</s> with opposing results should not be explained here as [resulting from] the simultaneous maturation [of both good and bad karmas], or through [their] intense velocity. Because the <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) caused by that [simultaneous maturation] cannot be the cause of liberation. For this very reason we shall demonstrate that this [equanimity], which depends on the pair of opposing <s>karmas</s>, is the cause of liberation for souls from [their] predicament—not [any] other bondage, since that would be no different from before.

body.text: iti darśayiṣyāmaḥ ad \Kir\ 5:12cd and elsewhere in the commentary on the fifth

sa caivaṃ dīkṣitaḥ sadyonirvāṇadīkṣayā yadā bhavati tadā śivavatsarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca kiñcijjñatvahetubhirbandhairvivarjitaśca bhavati|
yadā tvasadyonirvāṇadīkṣayā dīkṣito na punaḥ saṃsārī yadā
patitaśarīro bhavati tadā śivatvavyaktisaṃpūrṇo bhavati na prāgārabdhakāryakarmabhogoparodhe na sarvātmanā bandhakṣayasya śivatvasya vyakteścākaraṇāditi vakṣyāmo yenedaṃ taddhi bhogata ityatra|
body.translated_text: And when he is thus initiated through immediate-liberation initiation (<s>sadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s>), he becomes omniscient like <s>Śiva</s>, the agent of all actions, and freed from the bonds that are the causes of limited knowledge. But when he is initiated through non-immediate-liberation initiation (<s>asadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s>), he does not again become a transmigrating being; [yet] when the body falls, only then does the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>-nature become complete—not before—because the experience of <s>karma</s> that has already begun to bear fruit has not ceased, and because the destruction of bondage and the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>-nature have not been accomplished in their entirety. We shall explain this in [the section beginning with] 'for that indeed through experience.'
Now, the conclusion of all the questions and answers.

children.translated_text: Thus, bound in sequence,
one is liberated through the method of [sequential] practice.
Isolated (<s>kevala</s>), composite (<s>sakala</s>), and pure (<s>śuddha</s>)—
the soul (<s>puruṣa</s>) is remembered as having three states.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaduktaṃ badhyate kathaṃ mucyate kathamiti
body.translated_text: Commentary: What was asked—'how is [the soul] bound?' and 'how is it liberated?'—
Even for the conscious, pure field-knower (<s>kṣetrajña</s>), the embodied one,
whose nature is knowledge itself and who is a non-agent—for him, conditioning (<s>saṃskāra</s>) is accepted. ||

body.text: iti saṃkṣepeṇa tryavasthaḥ puruṣo nityatvādidha rmayukta upasaṃhṛta iti|
body.translated_text: Thus, in brief, the soul having three states, endowed with the properties of eternality and the rest, is concluded here.

body.text:
yastu tryavasthaḥ puruṣa ityetatsūtramavasthāntaravyudāsaparatvena niyamārtha iti vyācaṣṭe tena sakalasya tāvadavasthābhedena bhedaḥ prāguktaḥ śuddhasya tu yuktisiddhatvādavaśyābhyupagamanīya ityajñānata eva niyamaḥ pradarśitaḥ|
yadapi vijñānakevalino 'sambhavāt kevalāvasthābhedo nopapanna ityuktaṃ tadapya yuktaṃ, tasyā sambhavāsiddheḥ|
tathā hi yo yadbandhavyatirikto yasya bandhaḥ sa tadvyatirekeṇa tasya sambhavatīti nigaḍavyatirekeṇeva vairadaṇḍādi karmamāyīyabandhavyatiriktaśca malo bhavadbhirapi puṃso bandha iṣyate|
na tadavyatirikto naiyāyikādibhiriveti|
tataḥ kevalamalabaddhaḥ puruṣaḥ saṃbhavati| yo 'pi tannirākaraṇāya prayogo racito malakevalino karmabandhenāpi baddhā anādimalasambandhitvātpralayakevalivaditi|
tatra pakṣastāvanmātā me vandhyetivat|
kevalamalabandhatve karmaṇo 'pi bandhatvānupapatteḥ|
tadupapattau vā kevalārthānupapattitaḥ svavacananirākṛtatvādduṣṭa ityayukta eva|
yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: But one who explains the sūtra 'the soul has three states' as having the purpose of excluding other states—for him, the <s>sakala</s> (composite) state has already been differentiated by differentiation of states as stated before; and the pure (<s>śuddha</s>) state, being established by reasoning, must necessarily be accepted—thus the restriction has been shown out of ignorance alone. As for what was said—that the <s>kevala</s> (isolated) state is not established because a <s>vijñānakevala</s> (one isolated in consciousness alone) is impossible—that too is improper, because its impossibility has not been proven. For thus: whatever bondage is different from [the soul for] which it is a bondage—that [soul] can exist apart from that [bondage], just as a prisoner [can exist] apart from fetters and chains. And <s>mala</s> (impurity), being different from the bondage of <s>karma</s> and <s>māyā</s>, is accepted even by you [Śaiva Siddhāntins] as a bondage of the soul—not as non-different from it, as maintained by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and others. Therefore, a soul bound by <s>mala</s> alone can exist. As for the argument devised to refute this—[namely] that those who have only <s>mala</s> are also bound by <s>karma</s>-bondage, because of their beginningless connection with <s>mala</s>, like the <s>pralayakevalins</s> (souls in dissolution)—there the thesis itself is like [saying] 'my mother is barren.' Because if <s>kevala</s>-<s>mala</s>-bondage [alone] is [the thesis], the bondage of <s>karma</s> too would be impossible to establish. And if that [karma-bondage] is established, then the meaning of '<s>kevala</s>' (isolated) would not hold—hence [the argument] is vitiated by being contradicted by its own statement. As they say:

body.text: na tasya hetubhistrāṇamutpatsyanneva yo hataḥ| iti|
body.translated_text: 'One who is already slain will never find protection from [any] causes.' ||
And it is contradicted by scripture. As stated in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijaya</s> [Tantra] and others:
'The Lord, by his will, at the beginning of creation, the eight <s>vijñānakevalins</s>—
he graces [them as] <s>mantreśas</s> (lords of mantras), who are authorities over what is contained within <s>māyā</s>.' ||

body.text:
kiñca yāvatproktayuktisiddhyasaṃbhavāt vijñānakevalino na nirākṛtāstāvadayaṃ
hetuḥ sandigdhavipakṣavyāvṛttatvāt ahetureva|
yāvaccāsya hetutvaṃ na viniścitaṃ tāvanna te nirākartuṃ śakyā iti itaretarāśrayādvyāptyasiddhernāsya hetutvam| atra ca hetutve pralayakevalinirāse 'pi hetutvameva| teṣāmapi kalādibandhairbhavitavyam| anādimalasambandhitvātsakalavaditi|
sādhu samarthitaḥ svanaya ityalaṃ svaśāstravetālotthāpakaiḥ saha nirbandheneti|
body.translated_text: Moreover, as long as the impossibility of the <s>vijñānakevalins</s> has not been established by the reasoning you have adduced, this reason is either inconclusive (having doubtful exclusion from the counter-thesis) or simply not a valid reason. And as long as its validity as a reason has not been ascertained, they [the <s>vijñānakevalins</s>] cannot be refuted—thus, from mutual dependence, the pervasion is not established, and therefore it has no validity as a reason.
