And if it were a valid reason [even] here, then [by the same logic], even in refuting the <s>pralayakevalins</s>, it would be equally a valid reason—for they too would have to be bound by <s>kalā</s> and other bonds, being beginninglessly connected with <s>mala</s>, just like the <s>sakalas</s> (composite souls). Well argued is your own doctrine! Enough of contention with those who raise the ghosts of their own scriptures!
Now, the conclusion of this entire section.

children.translated_text: The bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) of this nature has been described;
what else do you wish to ask?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
paśupadārtho 'traivaṃvidhaḥ paśvādipadārthapañcakayuktaḥ prakarṣato lakṣaṇenoktaḥ|
vastutaḥ padārthāntarāṇāṃ tādarthyenaiva pravṛttiriti kimanyatparipṛcchasi|
sarvaṃ prāguddiṣṭamatraiva mayā lakṣaṇena
pratipāditamityarthaḥ||
body.translated_text: Commentary: The category of <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) has thus been described in detail, as endowed with the five categories beginning with <s>paśu</s>. In reality, the other categories function only for the sake of this [paśu]; therefore, 'what else do you wish to ask?' All that was enumerated earlier has been explained by me here through their definitions—that is the meaning. ||
Thus ends the first chapter of the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on the glorious <s>Kiraṇa[tantra]</s>, composed by <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, son of <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>. ||
CHAPTER 2

body.text: atha teṣāmeva padārthānāṃ parīkṣārthaṃ praśnapūrvaṃ prakaraṇāntarametāvata eva praśnasyāvaśiṣṭatvāt
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of examining those very categories, a new chapter is commenced with a question, since this much of the question remains:

children.translated_text: That Self which you have described,
as a limited knower and as all-knowing <s>Śiva</s>—
tell the cause of these two,
the pure and impure natures.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatrāsya tāvatprakaraṇasyārambhe pañcavidhaḥ sambandho vaktavyaḥ| taduktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare
body.translated_text: Commentary: At the beginning of this chapter, the fivefold connection (<s>sambandha</s>) is to be stated. As declared in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s> [Āgama]:
'The sūtra that follows from the [preceding] chapter in a tantra—

body.text: anantaraṃ yatpaṭalāt\devdot paṭalācca Not traced. Quoted also at the beginnings of the third

body.translated_text: its connection is to be stated as established in five ways.' ||
'From the tantra-subject, from the sūtra, from the sentence, from the section,
and from the chapter.' ||

body.text:
tatreha tantravastunaḥ ṣaṭpadārthātmanaḥ pratijñātatvāttatsambandhastatparīkṣātmakaḥ|
sautrastu padārthoddyotakapadena| vākyena tu paśurnitya ityādinā|
body.translated_text: Here, the tantra-subject, being the six categories which were declared, has its connection in the form of examining those [categories]. The sūtra-connection is through the word that illuminates the category. The sentence-connection is through [the statement] 'the bound soul is eternal' and so on.

body.text: ayañcātra praśnārthaḥ---yo 'sau nityatvādidharmayuktaḥ sakalākalādyavasthābhedena kiñcijjña ityaśuddhaḥ paśurātmā tvayā proktaḥ prāguktaḥ paśurnitya ityādinā|
body.translated_text: And here, the meaning of the question is: that Self (<s>ātman</s>) which was described by you as a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), endowed with the properties of eternality and the rest, a limited knower due to the differentiation of the <s>sakala</s>, <s>akala</s>, and other states—and therefore impure—as previously stated through 'the bound soul is eternal' and so on;

body.text: yaścāsau sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca śuddhaḥ śivo dṛṣṭāntatvenoktaḥ sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvadityādinānayoḥ śivātmanoḥ sambandhinī ye śuddhāśuddhe nirmalamalayukte svarūpe tadviṣayanimittaṃ brūhi|
body.translated_text: and that [Self] which was mentioned as omniscient, the agent of all actions, and pure—<s>Śiva</s>—cited as an illustration through 'as that all-knowing <s>Śiva</s>' and so on—tell the cause (<s>nimitta</s>) regarding the pure and impure natures—that is, the stainless and stain-possessed forms—belonging to these two, <s>Śiva</s> and the Self.

body.text: Testimonium: rāmakaṇṭho 'pyāha---yaścāsau sarvajñaḥ sarvakartā ca śuddhaḥ śivaḥ tathā kiñcijjño hyaśuddha ātmā| tayoḥ śivātmanoḥ samba(ndhī ye? ndhinī) tu śuddhāśuddhe nirmalamalayukte svarūpe iti [sic] {\=Iśānaśivagurudevapaddhati
kena nimittena śiva eva śuddho nātmā kena nimittenātmaivāśuddho na śivaḥ| na hyaheturniyamo yukta iti praśnaḥ|
body.translated_text: By what cause is <s>Śiva</s> alone pure and not the Self? By what cause is the Self alone impure and not <s>Śiva</s>? For a restriction without a cause is not reasonable—thus the question.
Here is the answer:

children.translated_text: Because of beginningless connection with impurity (<s>mala</s>),
he has been declared by me as a limited knower;
because of freedom from beginningless impurity,
that all-knowing one is therefore <s>Śiva</s>.
When a beginning is established [for something],
then a cause is postulated;
the pure and impure natures are remembered
as such by those two [Śiva and the Self], in accordance with reality.
Why is crystal pure?
Why is copper accompanied by patina?
Just as there is no cause in this [case],
so too there is none for <s>Śiva</s> and the Self.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hyātmano 'nāditvānnānyatsvarūpe nimittaṃ tathā kālikayā saha vartata iti sakālikasya tāmrāderivāśuddhatve 'pi|
yathā ceśvarasya proktena vakṣyamāṇena ca pramāṇena siddhasyānāditvānnānyatsvarūpe nimittaṃ tathā sphaṭikādīnāmiva śuddhatve 'pīti|
ādimato hi vastuno nimittamanviṣyate ghaṭāderivānyathāsiddhyasambhavāditi|
īdṛganādiśuddhāśuddhasvarūpaṃ yathārthataḥ satyārthatvena smṛtaṃ tābhyāmitīśātmābhyāmityarthaḥ|
atra ca malasambandhasyānāditvena malasyāpyanāditvaṃ siddham|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as, because of the beginninglessness of the Self, there is no other cause for its nature—similarly, just as copper and the like, which exist with patina (<s>kālikā</s>)—hence 'accompanied by patina' (<s>sakālikam</s>)—are impure [without an assignable cause]; and just as, because of the beginninglessness of the Lord, established by the proofs stated and to be stated, there is no other cause for his nature—similarly, just as crystal and the like are pure [without an assignable cause]. For only a thing that has a beginning requires a cause to be sought, like a pot and the like—because otherwise its establishment would be impossible. Such is the beginningless pure and impure nature, [known] 'in accordance with reality' (<s>yathārthataḥ</s>)—that is, as having true meaning—remembered 'by those two,' meaning by the Lord and the Self. And here, since the connection [of the Self] with <s>mala</s> is beginningless, the beginninglessness of <s>mala</s> itself is also established.
Now, by way of restating this, another question [arises]:

children.translated_text: For what reason is the Self again bound
by the bond of <s>kalā</s> and the rest?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
dvividhaṃ hi nimittamucyate loke karaṇaṃ prayojanañca| yathā pākāderindhanādi annāderbrāhmaṇa bhojanādi ca|
tatra kalādibandhasyaiva puṃpravṛttau karaṇanimittamuktaṃ karmāṇi|
tasyāśuddhasya sambandhaṃ samāyāti śivātkaletyādinā
body.translated_text: Commentary: For in the world, 'cause' (<s>nimitta</s>) is said to be of two kinds: the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) and the purpose (<s>prayojana</s>)—like fuel and the like for cooking, and feeding a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like for [the purpose of] food. Among these, <s>karma</s> has been stated as the instrumental cause for the operation of <s>kalā</s>-bondage and the like upon the soul, through [the verse] 'he, the impure one, enters into connection with <s>kalā</s> from <s>Śiva</s>' and so on.

body.text: tataḥ sukhādikaṃ kṛtsnaṃ bhogaṃ bhuṅkte svakarmataḥ \Kir\ 1:20ab.

satyam| ata eva tadapyākṣiptamatra| prayojanatvābhāvāt| prayojakasya prayojyasya copakārakaṃ prayojanamucyate vaidyarājñoriva pathyayūṣādinopakāraḥ|
na caitatprayojakasya paripūrṇatvātparopakārāyaiva pravṛtterupakārakam|
nāpi prayojyasya duḥkhamoharūpatvenātyantavinaśvarasukhamātrarūpatvena cānartharūpatvādityanenāpi bhogātmanānarthena kinnimittaṃ bhagavatā pumāṃsaḥ kadarthyanta ityapi praśnārthaḥ| tanna virodhaḥ|
dvitīyastu praśnaḥ sa māyāntargata ityādi
body.translated_text: True. For this very reason, that too is implied here—because of the absence of purpose. For 'purpose' (<s>prayojana</s>) is said to be what is beneficial to both the instigator and the instigated—just as a physician's benefit to a king through wholesome broth and the like. But this [bondage] is not beneficial to the instigator [Śiva], because he is complete and acts only for the benefit of others. Nor is it beneficial to the instigated [soul], because it consists of suffering and delusion, and consists only of utterly perishable pleasure, and is thus of the nature of misfortune. Therefore, the question also means: by what reason does the Lord subject souls to suffering through this [bondage] consisting of experience? That is not contradictory. And the second question is [introduced by] 'he is said to be within <s>māyā</s>' and so on—

children.translated_text: He has been declared by you, O Lord, to be within <s>māyā</s>,
and also to be all-pervading.
Being all-pervading, how is he
situated everywhere [yet] within the womb of <s>māyā</s>?
Since these two [properties] are mutually contradictory,
how will this be [reconciled]?

body.translated_text: Commentary: As was previously stated: 'the all-pervading one is situated within the womb of <s>māyā</s>'—

children.translated_text: For the purpose of liberation, the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) is bound;
otherwise, birth does not occur for him;
as long as the contact with a body
has not taken place, he is not an experiencer of enjoyments.
This <s>māyā</s> is his body;
in the absence of that, there is no satisfaction.
Through this and that, due to lack of independence,
the impure one is rendered impure.

body.translated_text: Commentary: 'It does not transform into a mixture'—

body.text: nāmiśraṃ pariṇamate Source unknown. Also cited ad \Mat\VP\ 2:19, p.35 and \NarP\ 3:2, p.155.

children.translated_text: Just as a cloth, because of its being defective,
situated within impurity, becomes purified,
so too the impure soul (<s>pudgala</s>),
even though situated within the womb of <s>māyā</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atra malino malinīkṛta ityupakramasāmarthyādantaḥśabdo 'ntaraśabdasyārthe vartate|
tadayamarthaḥ---yathā vastraṃ sadoṣatvānmalinatvādeva bhasmagomayādimalāntarasthaṃ viśuddhyati dārṣṭāntike 'pyucyate|
aśuddhaḥ pudgalo 'pyevamityatrāpiśabdo bhinnakramaḥ|
aśuddho 'pi pudgala ātmā māyodaragataḥ sannevamiti viśudhyatyaśuddhyantareṇa yukta ityarthaḥ|
apiśabdādamāyodaragato 'pi vijñānakevalī|
nanuvijñānakevalināmaśuddhyantarasya nivṛttatvāduktadṛṣṭāntanayena śuddhirnopapadyata eva| na|
ata evopapatteḥ nivartyamānenāpi tena vastrādermalanivṛttyanuguṇasya saṃskārasya kṛtasya dṛṣṭatvāt| sarvathā nāśuddhyantaropakāraṃ vinā pūrvāśuddhernivṛttirityatra dṛṣṭāntārthaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Here, by the force of the introductory context 'the impure one is rendered impure,' the word 'within' (<s>antaḥ</s>) is used in the sense of 'another' (<s>antara</s>). The meaning is this: just as a cloth, because of its defect—its impurity—being situated within another impurity such as ash, cow-dung, and the like, becomes purified—the same is said in the case being illustrated. 'So too the impure soul'—here the word 'even' (<s>api</s>) follows a different sequence. Even the impure soul (<s>ātman</s>), being situated within the womb of <s>māyā</s>, is 'thus'—that is, purified through [another] impurity—this is the meaning. By the word 'even,' [this applies] also to the <s>vijñānakevala</s> who is not within the womb of <s>māyā</s>. But is not purification impossible for the <s>vijñānakevalins</s>, since the other impurity [i.e., <s>māyā</s>-bondage] has already ceased for them—according to the principle of the stated example? No. For precisely this reason it is established—because it is observed that even for cloth and the like, when that [impurity-removing agent] is being removed, a purificatory treatment (<s>saṃskāra</s>) conducive to the removal of stain has been applied. In all cases, without the aid of another impurity, the prior impurity is not removed—this is the purport of the illustration.
The refutation of the second question as well:

children.translated_text: What has been called 'the womb of <s>māyā</s>'
is characterized by <s>kalā</s> and the other [evolutes] descending [from <s>māyā</s>];
and [the soul's] dissolution therein was described
in reference to the subtle body.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaśca vyāpakasyāpyātmano māyodare layo vyāpī
body.translated_text: Commentary: And [the soul's] dissolution within the womb of <s>māyā</s>, even though the Self is all-pervading—the all-pervading one—
Now, a question for the purpose of examining the nature of <s>mala</s> (impurity):

children.translated_text: You have declared <s>mala</s> to be beginningless—
is it produced by <s>māyā</s>, or does it belong to the Self itself?
Is it a quality [of the Self], or is it different from it?
Tell me: what is the nature of <s>mala</s>?

body.translated_text: Commentary: Here, previously, the beginninglessness of <s>mala</s> was stated through [the verse] 'because of beginningless connection with <s>mala</s>' and so on.

children.translated_text: <s>Mala</s> is innate (<s>sahaja</s>); <s>māyā</s>
is an effect; <s>āgamika</s>-<s>mala</s> (acquired impurity) [is <s>karma</s>].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ātmanaḥ paramārthato janmānupapatteḥ sahajaśabdenātra tenātmanā sahānādisiddho 'rthāntarabhūto malaḥ kathyate|
tataśca nāvastubhūtaḥ| api tu cakṣuṣaḥ paṭalādivadvasturūpa eva mala ityuktaṃ bhavati|
avastutve hi tasya śaśaviṣāṇāderiva nityanivṛttatvāddīkṣājñānādeḥ sarvasyaitannivṛttihetorānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Since the birth of the Self is impossible in ultimate reality, by the word 'innate' (<s>sahaja</s>) here is meant a <s>mala</s> that is beginninglessly established together with that Self, being a distinct entity. And therefore it is not a non-entity. Rather, <s>mala</s> is said to be a real entity, like a cataract upon the eye. For if it were a non-entity—like a hare's horn—it would be eternally absent, and all means of its removal, such as initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), would be purposeless.

body.text:
yadyevaṃ māyākāryātmaka eva vastubhūto malaḥ
prāgukto vidyate| yaduktam
māyābhogapariṣvaktastanmaya iti|
body.translated_text: If so, then only the <s>mala</s> that consists of <s>māyā</s>-effects, being a real entity, exists as previously stated—as declared [in the text]: 'embraced by the experience of <s>māyā</s>, he consists of that.'

body.text:
tatkimanyenānena kalpiteneti|
tadarthametanmāyākāryamāgāmikastaduttarakālabhāvī
mala \crux ityayamarthaḥ\crux\ yadyevaṃ malinasya māyākāryaṃ bandhāya
bhavet tadā anādimalamuktasya śivasyāpi na kiṃ bhavediti vakṣyāmaḥ|
body.translated_text: Then why postulate this other [beginningless <s>mala</s>]? For this purpose [the text states]: the <s>māyā</s>-effect is the <s>āgamika</s> (acquired) <s>mala</s>—arising at a subsequent time. The meaning is this: if the <s>māyā</s>-effect were the bondage for one who is impure, then would it not also [have to be a bondage] for <s>Śiva</s>, who is free from beginningless <s>mala</s>? We shall explain this.

body.text:
tasmādbandhamokṣānyathānupapattyā māyākāryādvyatiriktaḥ sahajo vastubhūta eva malo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ|
yadyevaṃ māyaivāsau bhaviṣyatīti māyāmalavādinaḥ| tadapyayuktaṃ yataḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore, since bondage and liberation cannot be otherwise explained, <s>mala</s> (impurity), being distinct from the effects of <s>māyā</s>, innate (<s>sahaja</s>), and a real entity, must be accepted. If so, those who hold that <s>māyā</s> is the impurity [object that] 'it will just be <s>māyā</s> itself.' That too is unjustified, because —

children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> is not said to be a deluder [of the soul]
By itself — [rather,] it is a revealer through its effects.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
no niṣedhe| naiva māyāyāḥ svataḥ puṃ malinīkaraṇamupapadyate śaktirūpatvenāvyaktarūpatve satyakriyāvattvāt kṣīrādyavasthitadadhinavanītādiśaktivat| yaduktaṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: 'No' is a negation. <s>Māyā</s> by itself is not capable of contaminating the soul, because, being of the nature of a power (<s>śakti</s>), while remaining in an unmanifest form, it is inactive — like the potentialities of curd, butter, and the like residing in milk. As the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> have stated —
'That which has a cause, is non-eternal, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent — that is the manifest (<s>liṅga</s>);
That which has parts and is dependent — the manifest is [all] this; the unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) is the opposite.' Thus.

body.text:
kiñca yaiva kalādikāryaheturmāyā saiva kiṃ malo 'thānyā| yadyanyā tato vyatirikta eva mala iti nāsti vivādaḥ| saiva cettadayuktam|
yataḥ kāryāditi kāryadvāreṇa
prakāśanakartṛsvabhāvāsiddhā tato na mohinī nāvaraṇakartṛsvabhāvā savitṛvat svabhāvaviruddhakāryāsiddhyā gamyata
ityarthaḥ|
body.translated_text: Moreover, is the <s>māyā</s> that is the cause of effects such as <s>kalā</s> (limited agency) and the rest the same as <s>mala</s>, or is it different? If it is different, then <s>mala</s> is indeed distinct — there is no dispute. If it is the same, that is unjustified. Because 'through its effects' means 'through the medium of its effects' — its nature as an agent of revelation is established, and therefore it is not a deluder, not of the nature of an agent of concealment — just as with the sun, which is understood [not to cause darkness] because a contradictory effect opposed to its nature is not established. This is the meaning.
And let it not be said that this reason is unestablished, because —

children.translated_text: Through the contact with its own effects,
Being of the nature of a revealer of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>),
Having torn apart <s>mala</s> (impurity), it produces the manifestation of consciousness
In a particular domain.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yato malanivṛttipūrvamātmanaścidvyaktimekadeśa eva kāryakaraṇādinaiva sā kurvatī dṛśyata ityuktaṃ tayodbalitacaitanya
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because, having first removed <s>mala</s>, it is seen to produce the manifestation of consciousness of the self in a particular domain only through the body, senses, and the like. Thus it has been said — empowered by those [effects], with consciousness established,

children.translated_text: It is a revealer through its effects.
It is not established as having the nature of a deluder.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
kāryadvāreṇa yataḥ prakāśikā siddhā tato mohakatvena puṃso nāvasthiteti svabhāvaviruddhakāryāsiddhyā pratīyata ityuktam|
tataśca yena kāryeṇa saha yadviruddhaṃ kāryaṃ tattatkāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇajanyaṃ yathā prakāśalakṣaṇakāryaviruddhamandhakārātmakaṃ kāryaṃ prakāśakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇajanyam|
puṃprakāśakāryaviruddhaṃ ca puṃmohātmakaṃ kāryamatastadapi puṃprakāśakāraṇavyatiriktakāraṇajanyamiti
yattatkāraṇaṃ sa māyāvyatirikto malo 'tra kāryaviśeṣānumānasiddha iti tātparyārtho 'sya nigamanavākyasyeti na gatārthatā|
ata evopasaṃhariṣyati vyatiriktaḥ sa yuktita iti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Since it is established as a revealer through the medium of its effects, it is not established as being of the nature of a deluder of the soul — this is understood through the non-establishment of an effect contradictory to its nature. This has been stated. And therefore, whatever effect is contradictory to the effect accompanied by which [something acts], that [contradictory effect] is produced by a cause different from that cause — just as the effect characterized by darkness, which is contradictory to the effect characterized by light, is produced by a cause different from the cause of light. And the effect characterized by the delusion of the soul, which is contradictory to the effect characterized by the soul's illumination — that too is produced by a cause different from the cause of the soul's illumination. That cause is <s>mala</s>, which is distinct from <s>māyā</s> — established here by the inference from the specific [contradictory] effect. This is the purport of this concluding statement, and it is not redundant. For this very reason, he will conclude: 'It is distinct, by reasoning.' [And from <s>Sāṃkhya</s>:]
'The <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) have the natures of mutual suppression, dependence, production, and coupling.' Thus.

body.text:
nanu prakāśaviśeṣa eva moho 'nātmanyātmābhimānātmaka iti sāṅkhyāḥ|
yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Now, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s> [object:] delusion is merely a particular kind of manifestation — in the form of the misconception of Self in the non-Self. As they state —
'The division of <s>tamas</s> (darkness) is eightfold; delusion (<s>moha</s>) is tenfold; great delusion (<s>mahāmoha</s>);
<s>Tāmisra</s> (gloom) is eighteenfold; and likewise <s>andhatāmisra</s> (blinding darkness).' Thus.
Therefore, since the contradiction of nature is not established here, whence the proof of a distinct <s>mala</s>? That is unjustified —

children.translated_text: 'Manifestation' (<s>prakāśa</s>) is [meant by] the word 'expression' (<s>vyakti</s>);
'Concealment' (<s>āvṛti</s>) is [meant by] the word '<s>mala</s>' (impurity).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ayamarthaḥ---nātra prākṛto 'yaṃ moho vivakṣito 'sya śarīrasadbhāva eva siddheḥ|
api tu ātmanaściddharmatvena vyāpakatayā vakṣyamāṇasya sarvajñatvaprasaṅgasya parihārāyāvaśyamāvṛtirūpo malaśabdavācyo 'nya eva moho 'bhyupagantavyaḥ|
sa ca prakāśāvaraṇarūpatvādvyaktiśabdavācyena puṃprakāśena saha virudhyata iti nāsiddho 'tra vyatiriktamalasādhanasvabhāvavirodha iti|
astvasyāvṛtyātmano malasyājñānahetutvānmohakatvaṃ yastvayaṃ prākṛto mohaḥ kathitastasya puṃvyaktirūpatvāttadayuktameveti| na yataḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: This is the meaning — the delusion intended here is not the natural [Sāṃkhya] delusion, since that is established merely by the existence of the body. Rather, since the Self has the nature of consciousness and is pervasive, in order to avoid the consequence of omniscience that will be stated, a different kind of delusion in the form of concealment, denoted by the word '<s>mala</s>,' must necessarily be accepted. And this [<s>mala</s>], being of the nature of the concealment of illumination, is contradictory to the soul's illumination denoted by the word '<s>vyakti</s>' (manifestation) — hence the [reason of] contradiction of nature for establishing a distinct <s>mala</s> is not unestablished here. Let this <s>mala</s>, which is of the nature of concealment, have the capacity to cause delusion through being the cause of ignorance; but the natural delusion that you have described — since it is of the nature of the soul's manifestation — that [identification of it with <s>mala</s>] is indeed unjustified. Because —

children.translated_text: The manifestation of the soul is called '<s>mala</s>'
Clearly, like a lamp and darkness.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā dīpaḥ prakāśako 'pi nīlotpalādau raktotpalādiviparītaprakāśakatvāt andhakāro mohaḥ proktastathātmavyaktirapyanityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmatvena viparītena prakāśamānā sphuṭameva kṛtvā malo mohaḥ proktaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as a lamp, although it is a revealer, is called 'darkness' (delusion) because it reveals blue lotus and the like in a manner opposite [to their true nature] — as if they were red lotus — so too the manifestation of the self, manifesting the impermanent, impure, painful, and non-self as if they were eternal, pure, pleasurable, and self — through this reversed manifestation — is clearly and explicitly called '<s>mala</s>' (delusion).

body.text: IFP T.85, p.6, lines 5--6: yadāhuḥ---anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmapratipattiravidyeti Cf. also {Yogasūtra} 2:5: anityāśuciduḥkhānātmasu nityaśucisukhātmakhyātiravidyā

children.translated_text: <s>Māyā</s> too is said to be a deluder,
Through the enjoyment and savoring of objects.

body.translated_text: Commentary: In that very form, by us [it is maintained that] — embraced by the enjoyment of <s>māyā</s>,

children.translated_text: For this [soul] situated wherever,
Due to its own <s>karma</s> and <s>mala</s> as causes,
The bondage arising from <s>māyā</s>
Operates with a [specific] occasion.
Even for <s>Śiva</s> [himself], if released from beginningless <s>mala</s>,
Would there not be [bondage]?
Therefore <s>māyā</s> is not at all <s>mala</s>;
It [<s>mala</s>] is distinct [from <s>māyā</s>], by reasoning.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
kalādikṣityantabhuvaneṣu sarvatra puṃso yathā māyāpravṛttau karmāṇi nimittaṃ tathā malo 'pi|
anyathā tasya ciddharmatvena vakṣyamāṇatvātsarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvena śivatvaprasaṅgato māyīyabandhā pravṛttireva|
nanu karmāṇi tatpravṛttau nimittamastu malena kim|
naivaṃ mala muktasya sarvasya śivatvenānuṣṭhāturabhāvātteṣāṃ karmaṇāmapyasiddheḥ||
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as <s>karma</s> (action) is the occasion for the soul's engagement with <s>māyā</s> in all the worlds from <s>kalā</s> to earth, so too is <s>mala</s>. Otherwise, since the soul will be stated to have the nature of consciousness, there would be the consequence of its being <s>Śiva</s> through omniscience and omnipotence — therefore the engagement with <s>māyā</s>ic bondage [must have <s>mala</s> as its basis]. But let <s>karma</s> alone be the occasion for that engagement — what is the need for <s>mala</s>? Not so, because if <s>mala</s> were removed, all [souls] would be <s>Śiva</s>, and since there would be no one to perform [rituals], those <s>karmas</s> themselves would also be unestablished.

body.text:
nanu karmaivāvaraṇatvena kalpyatāṃ kiṃ maleneti kṣapaṇakāḥ| tadayuktam| tasya kṛṣyādāviva svaphalahetumātratvena siddheḥ āvaraṇatvādarśanāt
arthālocanādāvapyevaṃ tasyaiva hetukalpanenendriyāderabhāvaprasaṅgāccetyuktam|
tataśca māyāpravṛttau karmavyatirikta eva malo 'bhyupagantavya iti| yata evaṃ tasmānna māyā malaḥ|
yathā ca tadvyatiriktastathā yuktito 'numānenaiva sādhita ityupasaṃhāraḥ|
body.translated_text: Now, the Jains [say]: let <s>karma</s> itself be imagined as the concealer — what is the need for <s>mala</s>? That is unjustified, because <s>karma</s> is established merely as a cause of its own fruits, as in agriculture and the like — concealment is not observed [as its function]. And it has been stated that if <s>karma</s> alone were imagined as the cause even for perceiving objects and the like, the consequence would be the non-existence of the senses and the like. Therefore, in the engagement with <s>māyā</s>, <s>mala</s> must be accepted as distinct from <s>karma</s>. Since this is so, therefore <s>māyā</s> is not <s>mala</s>. And just as it is distinct [from <s>māyā</s>], so it has been established by reasoning alone through inference — this is the conclusion.
Here is the objection of the opponent:

children.translated_text: Everything would be an effect of <s>māyā</s> —
Whence is there another innate <s>mala</s>?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
\crux māyākāryaṃ kalādi samastamityavikalaṃ tattvātmakameva bandhanaṃ syāt\crux |
yadvā niravaśeṣabhūtabhuvanātmakaṃ syāditi|
ayamarthaḥ---yadbandhanaṃ tattattvamevādhvani bhuvanādyātmanā vā saṃniviṣṭaṃ yathā māyākāryaṃ bandhanaṃ tadvanmalo bandhanaṃ bhavadbhiruktaṃ so 'pi tattvāntaramadhvani vā bhuvanādyantaramiti tattvātireko bhuvanātirekaśca
prasajyata iti|
atha tattvabhuvanādyātmakatvamasya neṣyate tataḥ śaśaviṣāṇāderiva bandhanatvamapyasyāsiddhamityuktam|
kuto 'nyaḥ sahajo mala iti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: [The objection is:] the entire [system of] <s>kalā</s> and the rest, being effects of <s>māyā</s>, would constitute bondage as the complete set of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) alone. [Or alternatively:] it would consist of the entirety of elements and worlds. The meaning is: whatever bondage exists — whether as <s>tattvas</s> situated in the cosmic path (<s>adhvan</s>), or as worlds and the like — is an effect of <s>māyā</s>. If <s>mala</s> as bondage is asserted by you to be similar, then it too would be another <s>tattva</s> in the path or another world — and the consequence of an excess of <s>tattvas</s> and worlds would arise. And if the nature of being a <s>tattva</s> or world is not accepted for it, then its capacity for bondage would be as unestablished as that of a hare's horn. Thus it is said: 'Whence is there another innate <s>mala</s>?'
Here is the reply:

children.translated_text: Its state of being a bound soul (<s>paśutva</s>) would reside in the Self.
And the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) is situated within the cosmic path.
By whom this is taught, according to that view,
<s>Mala</s> has characteristics different from those [of <s>māyā</s>'s effects].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ayamarthaḥ---karmaṇāsya hetoranaikāntikatvaṃ tasya bandhatve 'pi tattvabhuvanādisthitya bhāvāt|
atha māyātattve sthitatvāttasya nānaikāntikaviṣayateti|
ucyate---yadyevaṃ tadapi paśutvamiti malaḥ paśutattvasthaṃ tena vinātmanāṃ paśutvāyogāt| taddvāreṇa tadapyadhvani sthitamiti māyākāryāttattvabhuvanāderbhinnalakṣaṇo 'pi malaḥ karmavadbandha ityadoṣaḥ||
body.translated_text: Commentary: The meaning is: this reason [against <s>mala</s>] is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) because <s>karma</s>, while being bondage, does not reside in <s>tattvas</s> and worlds. If [you say] it is not inconclusive because <s>karma</s> resides in the <s>māyā</s>-<s>tattva</s> — [we reply:] if so, then <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being a bound soul) is also <s>mala</s>, residing in the <s>paśu-tattva</s> (soul-principle), since without it the souls' state of being bound cannot be accounted for. Through that medium, it too resides in the cosmic path. Thus <s>mala</s>, though having characteristics different from the effects of <s>māyā</s> such as <s>tattvas</s> and worlds, is still bondage, like <s>karma</s> — there is no fault.

body.text: yastu sahajaḥ syānmalo māye tyevamādibhiḥ padacchedairbalādeva
body.translated_text: As for [the reading] 'the innate <s>mala</s> would be in <s>māyā</s>' — forcibly parsed with such word-divisions —

body.text:
yadapyasya dūṣaṇatvenānayoḥ kāryayoḥ śivatvapaśutvarūpatvenaikasminnātmani samāveśātsahāvasthānavirodho nāstye vetyuktaṃ tadapyayuktaṃ parasparaparihārāvirodhe 'pyanayoritaretarābhāvarūpatvādvṛkṣatadabhāvayoriva naikasmātkāraṇādudbhavaḥ sambhavati yataḥ|
ayameva cāsmākamatra pratijñāto 'rtha iti|
viruddhayorapyanayoḥ sahānavasthānopadarśanametaddoṣodbhāvanameva pratijñātārthābādhanāt|
na ca śivatvasyeva paśutvasyāpyātmanyavasthānamiti yuktam|
tasya vastvantarākāramalarūpatvena tadvyatiriktatayāvasthiteḥ|
vakṣyati ca ātmano 'nādisambandhāddharma ityupacaryata iti|
body.translated_text: As for what has been said as an objection — that since both these effects, in the form of <s>Śiva</s>-hood and <s>paśu</s>-hood (being bound), co-exist in a single Self, there is no contradiction in their co-existence — that too is unjustified. Because, even though there is no contradiction in their mutual exclusion, since these two are of the nature of each other's absence — like a tree and its absence — they cannot arise from a single cause. And this is precisely the thesis we have proposed here. The demonstration of the co-existence of these two mutually contradictory [states] is itself the bringing forth of the defect [in the opponent's view], since it does not undermine the proposed thesis. And it is not justified [to claim] that <s>paśutva</s> resides in the Self in the same manner as <s>Śiva</s>-hood, because [<s>paśutva</s>], having the form of a real entity different [from the Self], namely <s>mala</s>, is established as distinct from the Self. And it will be stated: 'Due to beginningless association with the Self, it is figuratively called a property (<s>dharma</s>).'

body.text:
yadapi cakṣurādinālokādisahakārisannidhānāsannidhānābhyāṃ prakāśāprakāśādiviruddhaṃ kāryaṃ kurvatāsya hetoranaikāntikatvamuktaṃ tadatitarāmayuktam|
sahakāryasannidhāne hi tatsvakāryamakurvaddṛṣṭaṃ na tu tadviruddhaṃ kurvadabhāvasyāvastutvena karaṇāsambhavāt|
savitā puruṣādīnāmivolūkādeḥ prakāśameva karoti|
sa tu prakāśako 'tyantabhāsvaratvena tasya netropaghātahetutvāt mandanetrasyeva svakāryā karaṇādaprakāśaka ityupacaryata iti na tu tamovadaprakāśakaraṇāditi nānaikāntikaviṣayaḥ|
tataśca sarvadoṣarahitātprāguktātsvabhāvaviruddhakāryopalambhānmāyāvyatirikta eva malaḥ siddhyatītyalamāgamārthabahiṣkṛtaiḥ saha vivādeneti|
body.translated_text: As for the objection that this reason is inconclusive because the eye and the like, through the presence or absence of cooperating conditions such as light, produce contradictory effects like illumination and non-illumination — that is extremely unjustified. For when the cooperating condition is present, [the cause] is seen not producing its own effect — but it is not seen producing a contradictory effect, since non-existence, being unreal, cannot be an agent. The sun produces illumination for humans and the like, just as for owls. But it is figuratively called 'non-illuminating' for the owl because, being excessively brilliant, it causes damage to its eyes, and thus for the weak-eyed, it does not produce its own effect — not because it produces darkness. Hence it is not inconclusive. Therefore, from the previously stated [argument], which is free from all defects, and from the observation of an effect contradictory to [<s>māyā</s>'s] nature, <s>mala</s> as distinct from <s>māyā</s> is established. Enough with disputing those who are outside the meaning of scripture.

body.text: tadevaṃ pramāṇato māyāvyatiriktasya malasya siddhasya saṃhitāntarairabhikhyānapradarśanāya paryāyāntarāṇyucyante|
body.translated_text: Thus, <s>mala</s> as distinct from <s>māyā</s> having been established through valid means of knowledge, its synonyms are stated in order to show its recognition in other scriptural collections —

children.translated_text: <s>Mala</s> (impurity), <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being bound),
<s>Tiraskārakara</s> (that which causes concealment), <s>tamas</s> (darkness),
<s>Avidyā</s> (nescience), <s>āvṛti</s> (veiling), <s>mūrcchā</s> (stupor) —
These are declared as synonyms of that [<s>mala</s>].
And that [<s>mala</s>], with its synonyms <s>avidyā</s> and the rest,
Is established through [various] divisions in each and every system.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atha kimasau malaḥ saṃhitāntareṣviva darśanāntareṣu prasiddhaḥ| netyucyate
body.translated_text: Commentary: But is this <s>mala</s> well-known in other systems besides other scriptural collections? It is said: no.

children.translated_text: Because of its existence, the soul is a bound being (<s>paśu</s>), one to be fettered,
One to be purified, one to be awakened — so it is held in this [system].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tasyāsya malasya sadbhāvādihetyasminneva pārameśvare darśane paśuḥ preryaḥ pāśyaśca kalādinā śodhyaśca dīkṣayā bodhyaśca śāstrātmanā jñānenābhimato na tathā darśanāntareṣu|
tataśca darśanāntaramuktāḥ paśava eva malasya tairajñātatvena vicchettumaśakyatvādityuktaṃ bhavati| yadyevamātmanaḥ pāśyādivṛttibhedā apyanādisthitā eva| tatasteṣāmapi bandhāntaratva prasaṅgaḥ| tadayuktam| yataḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because of the existence of this <s>mala</s>, in this very Śaiva (<s>Pārameśvara</s>) system alone, the soul is to be impelled (<s>prerya</s>), to be fettered (<s>pāśya</s>), to be purified through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) by means of <s>kalā</s> and the like, and to be awakened through knowledge in the form of scripture — not so in other systems. Therefore, those liberated by other systems remain bound souls, because <s>mala</s>, being unknown to them, cannot be severed — this is what is stated. If so, then the activities of being fettered and the like also subsist in the Self beginninglessly; then they too would have the consequence of being another [form of] bondage. That is unjustified, because —

children.translated_text: The activities such as being fettered and the like,
Which are proclaimed as divisions of that [<s>mala</s>],
They come into being when <s>mala</s> exists;
And the state of being an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) is not [another bond] alone.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
eṣāṃ pāśyādivṛttīnāṃ malanivṛttau nivṛttisiddhermalanimittatvaṃ siddhyati pradīpanimittatvamiva prabhāyā iti|
na pṛthagbandhāntaratvamiti| tadiyatā malasyāvastutve māyāsvabhāvatve ca niṣiddhe adhunā ātmano 'pi vā guṇa
body.translated_text: Commentary: Since the cessation of these activities such as being fettered and the like is established upon the cessation of <s>mala</s>, their being occasioned by <s>mala</s> is established — like the dependence of light on a lamp. They are not separately another kind of bondage. Now, having refuted [the views] that <s>mala</s> is unreal and that it is of the nature of <s>māyā</s>, now [comes the question:] or is it also a quality of the Self —

children.translated_text: If it is thus established that [the soul] is one to be fettered,
And <s>mala</s> is associated with the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) —
Is <s>mala</s> not a property (<s>dharma</s>) of the Self?
[Rather,] <s>mala</s> is established by reasoning.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadyevaṃ cidrūpa evātmā pāśyo vyavasthita iti kiñcijjñatvānyathānupapattyāsyāvārako 'pi malaḥ kalpyate|
hanta tarhi ātmana evāsau ajñānātmā malo dharmatvena yuktito 'numānena kalpyatām| yadāhurnaiyāyikavaiśeṣikāḥ---yadyatra kāraṇāntareṇa kriyate tattatra nāstyevāndhakāra iva pradīpādinā kriyamāṇaḥ prakāśaḥ|
kriyate ca kāryakaraṇādibhirātmani vijñānaṃ| tatastadapi tatra nāstītyajñasvabhāva evātmā sidhyati kuto vyatiriktamalasiddhiḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: If the Self is established as being of the nature of consciousness and yet [also] as one to be fettered, then <s>mala</s> is also imagined — since the condition of being a limited knower cannot be otherwise explained — as its concealer. Well then, let this <s>mala</s>, which is of the nature of ignorance, be established by reasoning as a property of the Self itself. As the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> say: 'That which is produced somewhere by another cause does not exist there — like darkness being produced by a lamp that produces light.' And knowledge is produced in the Self by the body, senses, and the like. Therefore that [knowledge] too does not exist there — hence the Self is established as being of the nature of ignorance itself. Whence then the establishment of a distinct <s>mala</s>?
Here is the established conclusion:

children.translated_text: Due to beginningless association with the Self,
It is figuratively called a 'property' (<s>dharma</s>).
How, when [the Self] is endowed with knowledge,
Has it come to possess the quality of ignorance?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
bhavedevaṃ yadyayaṃ heturasmānprati siddhaḥ syāt| asiddhastu kāryakaraṇādīnāṃ tatrāsmābhirjñānavyañjakatvenābhyupagamāt|
body.translated_text: Commentary: This would be so if this reason were established from our perspective. But it is unestablished, because we accept the body, senses, and the like as manifesters of knowledge, not [as its producers].

body.text:
nanu tadbhāvatadabhāvayordarśanādarśanābhyāṃ jñānasya kāryakaraṇādikāraṇatvaṃ sidhyati| na tayorvyañjakatvenāpi saṃbhavenānaikāntikatvāditi nānenā siddhena hetunātmanyajñatvasiddhiḥ|
tataścāvaśyaṃ tasyāśuddhātmano 'nādisambandhenāvaraṇena vyatiriktena bhavitavyamiti|
tadyogādaśuddha ityupacārādāgame kathito draṣṭavyo nājñasvabhāvatvādeveti|
body.translated_text: Now, from the observation and non-observation [of knowledge] in the presence and absence of [its cause], the causality of knowledge by body, senses, and the like is established. Since it is possible that they [body and senses] also serve as mere revealers (<s>vyañjaka</s>), the argument is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). Therefore, the ignorance of the soul is not established by this unproven reason. Hence, there must necessarily be an obscuring [agent] separate [from the soul], connected with that impure soul since beginningless time. It is due to conjunction with that [obscuring agent] that [the soul] is called 'impure' — this should be understood as a figurative expression in the scripture, not as being of an ignorant nature essentially.

body.text: tarhyata eva tatrājñatvasaṃśayo yukto na tajjñatva niścayo yena vyatiriktamalasiddhiriti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: Then, for precisely this reason, doubt about the soul's ignorance is justified, not certainty about its knowledge — by which the existence of a separate <s>mala</s> (impurity) would be established. To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: Its attribute (<s>dharma</s>), if it were an attribute,
would clearly involve transformation (<s>pariṇāma</s>).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
na tasyātmano dharmaḥ svabhāvo vājñānātmā malo ghaṭādivadanātmatvaprasaṅgāt| atha yatra jñānaṃ samavetamutpadyate sa ātmeti| tadapyayuktam|
tasya pūrvamajñānaṃ prati dharmitve ghaṭāderiva paścādapi jñānasamavāyo nopapadyata eva|
athājñānātmanastu tasya jñānābhyupagame sphuṭameva rūpāntarapariṇāmaḥ syādāmalakādeḥ pītatotpattyātmaka iveti vakṣyamāṇo doṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Ignorance, being <s>mala</s> (impurity), is not the attribute or essential nature of the soul — because it would lead to the consequence of the soul being non-soul, like a pot. But if [one defines] the soul as that in which knowledge inheres or arises — that too is unjustified. If ignorance were its prior attribute, then, like a pot, the subsequent inherence of knowledge would simply not be possible. Furthermore, if knowledge were to be accepted for one whose nature is ignorance, there would clearly be a transformation into another form — a defect to be stated later, like the arising of yellowness in an <s>āmalaka</s> (myrobalan fruit).

body.text:
nanu jñānaṃ tāvadasmadādipratyakṣatve satyacākṣuṣapratyakṣatvādrasādivadguṇaḥ|
guṇena ca dravyāśritena bhavitavyamiti yastasyāśrayaḥ sa tadvilakṣaṇatvādajñānarūpa evātmā siddhyati| tadapyayuktam| yataḥ|
ciddharme puṃsītyādi|
body.translated_text: Now, knowledge — being perceptible to us and others, yet being non-visual perception [i.e., not apprehended by the eye] — is a quality, like taste and the like. And a quality must inhere in a substance. Therefore, that which is its substrate — since it is distinct from [knowledge] — is established as the soul, whose nature is ignorance. That too is unjustified. Because: 'In the soul whose nature is consciousness' and so on.

children.translated_text: In the soul whose attribute (<s>dharma</s>) is consciousness (<s>cit</s>),
no attribute — if it were one — would involve transformation.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
cit jñānameva dharmaḥ svabhāvo yasya
sa tathābhūtaḥ \crux pumityanubhavati sarvamiti
pumān\crux\
ātmā svasaṃvedanena svaparātmaprakāśatayā pratipuruṣaṃ siddhyati kimanyena sādhanena|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: That whose attribute, whose essential nature, is <s>cit</s> (consciousness, knowledge) — such is [the soul]. The soul (<s>pumān</s>) — 'it experiences everything' — is established for each individual through self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvedana</s>), as the illuminator of self and other. What need is there of another proof?

body.text:
nanu jñānasya rasāderiva guṇatve heturukta eva|
so 'pyayuktaḥ dṛṣṭāntasyāsmānprati sādhyadharmā siddhatvāt| rasādayo hi bhāvāḥ saṃhatā eva jāyamānāḥ saṃhatā eva niruddhāśca sāṃkhyasaugatādibhirivāsmābhirapi pramāṇasiddhatvādarthakriyākaraṇāḥ kathyante|
na tvanyaḥ kaścitteṣāmāśrayabhūtastadvyatirekeṇa tasyānupalambhanāditi|
kathaṃ tarhi pṛthivyāṃ gandha ityādivyavahāraḥ|
kudarśanābhyāsamūlo bhrānta eva| yadi vā viśiṣṭasamudāyaikadeśapratipādanāya vanasya dhavaḥ śobhana
body.translated_text: Now, the reason stated for knowledge being a quality like taste and the like — that too is unjustified, because the example is one in which the property to be proven is itself [already] what we deny. For entities such as taste and the like, being produced in combination and ceasing in combination, are acknowledged by us — just as by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, <s>Buddhists</s>, and others — to be causally efficacious, since they are established by valid means of knowledge. But there is no other substrate for them distinct [from the combination], since nothing is apprehended apart from them. Then how is the conventional expression 'smell [resides] in earth' and so on [to be explained]? It is simply erroneous, rooted in the habitual practice of a false perspective. Or else, it is for the purpose of indicating a particular part of a qualified aggregate — as [one says] 'the <s>dhava</s> tree beautifies the forest.'

body.text: vanasya dhavaḥ śobhanaḥ cf.\ \NarP\ ad 1:4, p.11.
tasmiñjñānātmakatvāccitsvabhāve puṃsi nājñānaṃ malo dharmo yuktaḥ| āmalakādīnāmiva rūpāntarapariṇāma prasaṅgāt| tathā hi
body.translated_text: In that soul, whose essential nature is consciousness (<s>cit</s>), ignorance — <s>mala</s> — is not a fitting attribute, because of the consequence of transformation into another form, as with <s>āmalaka</s> fruits and the like. For indeed —

children.translated_text: In one [object], knowledge is manifested;
in another, it is concealed.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ekasminrūpādau viṣaye jñānamutpadyate anyasmiṃstu rasādāvutpannamapi naṣṭaṃ bhavadbhiriṣyate yatastataśca rūpāntarapariṇāmo 'syātmanaḥ| ko doṣa ityucyate|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: In one object, such as form, knowledge arises; but in another, such as taste, [knowledge] that had arisen is held by you to have perished — and therefore there would be a transformation of the soul into another form. What is the defect? It is said:

children.translated_text: Transformation belongs to the insentient;
it is not fitting for the sentient.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaḥ pariṇāmī so 'cetanaḥ siddho yathāmalakādirartha iti pariṇāmitvādātmano 'pyacetanatvaprasaṅga ityavaśyaṃ tatprasaṅgaparihārāyātmā naivājñānasvabhāvo 'bhyupagantavyaḥ|
api tu vijñānasvabhāva eveti| tasyāvārakasvabhāvo vyatirikto malaḥ siddhaḥ|
anyathā sarvajñatvaprasaṅgāditi tṛtīyasyāpi praśnasya nirāsaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: That which undergoes transformation is established as insentient — like an <s>āmalaka</s> fruit and other objects. Therefore, if the soul also undergoes transformation, the consequence of insentience would follow. Hence, in order to avoid this consequence, the soul must not be accepted as being of an ignorant nature at all. Rather, it is of a conscious (<s>vijñāna</s>) nature. Therefore, a separate <s>mala</s> whose nature is to obscure is established. Otherwise, the consequence would be omniscience — thus the third question is also refuted.

body.text: yadyevaṃ vyatiriktamalapakṣe 'pyeṣa eva doṣa iti samuccayena codakaḥ|
body.translated_text: If so, even on the view of a separate <s>mala</s>, this very defect [applies] — so the objector [argues], combining [the objections]:

children.translated_text: Since the connection of the two [soul and <s>mala</s>] is beginningless,
there is no separation, due to [<s>mala</s>'s] all-pervasiveness (<s>vibhutva</s>).
When the innate [<s>mala</s>] is destroyed,
would not [the soul's nature] also be destroyed?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tayorātmamalayoryo 'nādyāvāryāvārakalakṣaṇaḥ sambandhaḥ sa svabhāvaviśeṣa eva tasmānna viśleṣo nivṛttiranāditvādeva yathā cetanājjaḍādvā svabhāvādityanirmokṣaḥ|
atha tasmādviśleṣa iṣyate| yadyevaṃ sahajasya svabhāvasya prakṣaye sati tasyāpi nāśaḥ svabhāvāntarotpādarūpaḥ pariṇāmo bhavediti sa eva tadavastho doṣo yaḥ prāgavyatirikta malapakṣe proktaḥ|
atha na tayoḥ svabhāvādviśleṣaḥ api tu parasparasaṃśleṣānnetratadāvaraṇayoriva tato naiṣa doṣa ityucyate so 'pi na yuktaḥ|
vibhutvata iti vyāpakatvāt| avyāpakasya hyavyāpakāddeśāntaranayane viśleṣaḥ| vyāpakasya tu sarvatrāvasthānānna kutaścidviśleṣaḥ sambhavatītyanirmokṣaḥ|
atha tathābhūtasyāpi viśleṣa iṣyate| yadyevaṃ sahajasya sahabhāvina āvarakasya prakṣaye tasyāpyāvāryatvasya svabhāvasya nāśo rūpāntarapariṇāma iti sa doṣastadavastha eva|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The connection of the soul and <s>mala</s>, characterized as the relation of the obscured and the obscurer, is beginningless — it is a specific aspect of [their] very nature. Therefore, there is no separation, no cessation — since it is beginningless, just as [there is no separation of] the sentient from the insentient, or from one's own nature — hence no release. But if separation from that is desired — then, upon the destruction of what is innate, i.e., of [mala's] essential nature, there would be destruction [of the soul] too, a transformation consisting in the arising of another nature — and thus the same defect applies as was stated earlier for the view of non-separate <s>mala</s>. But if their separation is not due to [their essential] nature, but rather due to [their] mutual conjunction — like the eye and its covering — then this defect does not apply, it is said. But that too is not valid — 'due to all-pervasiveness' (<s>vibhutva</s>): because [<s>mala</s>] is all-pervading. For a non-pervading [entity] can be separated from another non-pervading one by being taken to another location. But for a pervading one, since it abides everywhere, separation from anywhere is not possible — hence no release. But if separation is desired even for one that is such — then upon the destruction of the innate, coexistent obscurer, the soul's very nature of being obscurable would also be destroyed — a transformation into another form — and thus the same defect applies.
Here is the settled doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: Even though <s>mala</s> is all-pervading,
the destruction of its power (<s>śakti</s>) is accomplished.
Through a means (<s>upāya</s>), the restraint of [<s>mala</s>'s] power
is effected in some way in [the case of] <s>mala</s>,
just as the burning power of fire
is quickly restrained by a <s>mantra</s>.
Likewise, through the restraint of its power,
[the soul] is said to be separated [from <s>mala</s>].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atra malaviṣayastāvadayamadoṣaḥ| yato na kevalamasyaivāvyāpakasya mohātmanaḥ prākṛtasya malasya yāvadvyāpakasyāpyāṇavamalasyopāyena mantradīkṣātmanā śakterāvārakasvabhāvasyāgnerdāhakatvasyeva vadho 'nyathābhāvaḥ kriyata eva|
kathañcidityārabdhakāryakarmabhogoparodhenāsarvātmanā tadanuparodhena tu sadyonirvāṇadīkṣayā sarvātmaneti|
tataśca malasya pariṇāminityatvābhyupagamānnaiṣa svabhāvāntarapariṇāmasādhanaprasaṅgo yuktaḥ siddhasādhanādityuktaṃ bhavati|
ata eva malasya svabhāvāntarapariṇateḥ svarūpasattve 'pyāmayādviśliṣṭaḥ puruṣa itīva malaśaktirodhādapi viśliṣṭaḥ kathyate|
tato viśleṣo na vibhutvādityayamapyadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Here, with respect to <s>mala</s>, this is not a defect at all. For not only of this non-pervading, delusion-natured, <s>prākṛta</s> (material) <s>mala</s> alone, but even of the all-pervading <s>āṇavamala</s> (innate impurity), the destruction — the alteration — of its power, whose nature is to obscure (just as fire's capacity to burn), is indeed accomplished through a means, namely <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) in the form of <s>mantras</s>. 'In some way' means: partially, through the obstruction of the fruition of karma and enjoyment already commenced — not completely; but through <s>sadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s> (immediate liberation initiation), completely. Therefore, since <s>mala</s> is accepted as eternal and subject to transformation, this consequence of establishing transformation into another nature is not valid — since what is to be proven is already established. For this very reason, even though <s>mala</s> continues to exist in its essential form, just as a person is said to be 'separated' from a disease [even though the disease still exists in potential], so too through the restraint of <s>mala</s>'s power, [the soul] is said to be 'separated.' Therefore, the [objection that] 'there is no separation due to all-pervasiveness' is also not a defect.
Now the defect pertaining to the soul (<s>puruṣa</s>) is also rebutted:

children.translated_text: Having effected the restraint of its [<s>mala</s>'s] power,
[the soul] is made free from desire for [further] existence.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śakteḥ saṃrodhaḥ śaktisaṃrodhaḥ| tasya malasya taṃ kṛtvā bhavaniḥspṛhaḥ krodharāgādirahitaḥ puruṣaḥ kriyate parameśvareṇa|
ata eva śaktipātaniścayāyākrodharāgādīni liṅgāni dīkṣādhikārārthaṃ gurubhiḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ parīkṣyanta ityuktam|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The restraint of the power — that is <s>śaktisaṃrodha</s>. Having effected that [restraint] of <s>mala</s>, the soul is made free from desire for existence — free from anger, attachment, and the like — by the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>). For this very reason it has been stated that, for ascertaining the descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>), the signs such as absence of anger and attachment are examined by teachers in their students for the purpose of determining eligibility for <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation).

body.text: nareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśe parākṛtaḥ It is not certain to which passage this refers.

body.translated_text: As for the defect stated — that upon the cessation of the coexistent obscuring [<s>mala</s>], there would be a transformation of the soul's own nature in the form of the cessation of its obscurability — to that too it is replied:

children.translated_text: The innate tarnish (<s>kālikā</s>) on copper —
upon its destruction, the copper is not destroyed.
Just as [there is] destruction in [the tarnish of] copper, so too
is the destruction of <s>mala</s> for the soul.
Just as when the husk of a grain of rice
is destroyed, the [grain itself] is not destroyed.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
sahacarakālikānivṛttyā na tāmrasya kaścidvikāro dṛśyate yathā tathā malanivṛttyāpyātmano na vikāra ityetāvatāṃśena dṛṣṭāntatvaṃ nānyathā tāmrasya pariṇatidharmatvenābhyupagamāditi|
etaduktaṃ bhavati---aupādhiko 'yaṃ malasannidhānāsannidhānakṛto bhedaḥ|
na tvātmano malānapekṣayārthagrahaṇaikasvabhāvasyānyo 'nāvāryasvabhāvo yo bhedaṃ vidadhyāditi svabhāvāntarapariṇāmābhāvānna pūrvoktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as no alteration of the copper is observed upon the removal of the coexistent tarnish, so too upon the removal of <s>mala</s> there is no alteration of the soul — to this extent the analogy holds, not otherwise, since copper is accepted as having the nature of transformation. What is stated amounts to this: the difference [between the bound and liberated states] is adventitious (<s>aupādhika</s>), caused by the presence and absence of <s>mala</s>. But for the soul, whose sole essential nature is the apprehension of objects, independent of <s>mala</s>, there is no other un-obscurable nature that could constitute a [real] difference — hence, due to the absence of transformation into another nature, the previously stated defect does not arise.

body.text: ayameva pakṣaḥ pramāṇasiddha ityanumānasiddhenāpi dṛṣṭāntāntareṇa poṣyate
body.translated_text: This very position, being established by valid means of knowledge, is further supported by another example established through inference:

children.translated_text: Just as the power associated with poison
is restrained through <s>mantras</s>,
yet the poison itself is not diminished —
so too is the destruction of <s>mala</s> for the soul.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
mohamāraṇahetutvānmalasthānīyāyāṃ sahajāyāmapi śaktau puruṣasthānīyasya viṣasyanivṛttāyāṃ na kadācidvarṇākṛtyādisvarūpanāśo yathā tathā puṃso malakṣaya iti|
aṃśena dṛṣṭāntatvādadhunā pratyakṣasiddhadṛṣṭāntāntareṇa prakaraṇopasaṃhāraḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as when the innate power of poison — which, like <s>mala</s>, causes delusion and death — is removed, there is never any destruction of the poison's own form such as color, shape, and the like; so too is the destruction of <s>mala</s> for the soul. Since this [analogy] is partial, now, with a directly perceivable example, the section is concluded:

children.translated_text: The fruit of the <s>kataka</s> (clearing-nut) tree,
when cast into turbid water,
effects the restraint of the [turbidity's] power —
does it expel anything else from the water?
The knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, likewise,
is the agent of the restraint of its [<s>mala</s>'s] power.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hi katakābhidhānasya vṛkṣaviśeṣasya phalaṃ \crux meghajādi sahajakaluṣayukta\crux\ eva jale prakṣiptaṃ tasyāḥ kaluṣalakṣaṇāyāḥ śakteḥ saṃrodhaṃ vidadhallakṣyate| na tu jalātkiñcidapi svabhāvāntaramanyato 'nyatra kṣipediti kāluṣyamātrameva tasya nivartayati nānyatkiñcidityarthaḥ|
tathā śiva eva jñānaṃ sarveṣāṃ cicchaktivyañjakatvena jñānahetutvāttasyeti malasya śaktisaṃrodhakārakaṃ dīkṣayā tadadhikārotpādanāya vā śaktipātenetyuktam|
yadi vā śivasya jñeyatayā saṃbandhi yaddīkṣitānāṃ nityakartavyatayā
vakṣyamāṇajñānaṃ tadārabdhakāryakarmabhogoparodhenākṣapitasya dīkṣayā sarvātmanā malasyaiva pratyahamapacayāt krameṇa śaktisaṃrodhakārakaṃ na tu puruṣasyeti| tataśca tasyāṃśe 'pi svabhāvāntarapariṇāmābhāvānna pūrvoktamacetanatvaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ malasya tvetadbhūṣaṇameveti na vyatiriktamalapakṣe kaściddoṣa iti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as the fruit of the specific tree called <s>kataka</s>, when cast into water that is endowed with its innate turbidity, is observed to effect the restraint of the power characterized as turbidity — but it does not expel anything whatsoever of another nature from the water — meaning it removes only the turbidity, nothing else. Likewise, the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> — because <s>Śiva</s> is the cause of knowledge for all, by being the revealer of [their] power of consciousness — [effects] the restraint of the power of <s>mala</s>, either through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) or through <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) for generating eligibility for it. Alternatively, the knowledge that pertains to <s>Śiva</s> as its object, which is to be stated as the daily obligatory [practice] for the initiated — that, through the obstruction of the fruition of karma and enjoyment already commenced, is the agent of the gradual daily diminution of <s>mala</s> alone, whose [power] has not been [fully] destroyed by <s>dīkṣā</s>; or through <s>sadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s> (immediate liberation initiation), of <s>mala</s> [destroyed] completely — not of the soul. Therefore, since in [the soul's] case too there is no transformation into another nature, the previously stated defect of insentience does not apply to <s>mala</s> — rather, this [property of transformation] is an ornament for it — and hence there is no defect in the view of a separate <s>mala</s>.
Colophon: Thus ends the second chapter (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) of the Vṛtti on the venerable <s>Kiraṇa</s>, composed by <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, son of <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>.
CHAPTER 3

body.text:
atha padārthānāmeva parīkṣārthaṃ praśnapūrvaṃ rakaraṇāntaram| atra ca sūtrapadārthaprakaraṇasambandhāḥ prāgvaddraṣṭavyāḥ|
pāṭalikastu vyatiriktamalasiddheranantaraṃ malasyaivā rāgatvaparīkṣātmako vākyātmako 'pi rāgeṇa rañjitaśceti
body.translated_text: Now, for the purpose of examining the categories (<s>padārthas</s>), another chapter, preceded by questions. Here, the connections between sūtras, categories, and chapters should be understood as before. However, according to the arrangement, immediately after the establishment of a separate <s>mala</s>, [this chapter] examines whether <s>mala</s> itself is the coloring agent — it is in the form of propositions, and [asks whether the soul] is colored by <s>rāga</s> (attachment):

children.translated_text: The state of being an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) has been declared to arise from <s>mala</s> —
does it not [rather] arise from desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>)?
And that [desire] arises from <s>rāga</s> (attachment) — since [the state of being an experiencer arises] from <s>rāga</s>,
what need is there of <s>mala</s> in this regard?

body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Now, by the word '<s>mala</s>' [meaning] 'obscuration,' and so on —
'The activities of binding and the like — those are declared to be its [<s>mala</s>'s] modifications;

body.text: male sati bhavantyetā bhoktṛtvañca na kevalam|| iti|
body.translated_text: when <s>mala</s> is present, these arise, and the state of being an experiencer — not alone [i.e., not without <s>mala</s>].'

body.text:
ko 'yaṃ praśnaḥ| athāvāryatvamevātra bhoktṛtvamucyate na tu bhogaikarasikatvamiti praśnaḥ|
yadyevaṃ tato mala eva vaktavyaḥ kiṃ rāgeṇeti rāgākṣepapraśno yuktaḥ, na tu malena kimiti|
rāgādyabhāve 'pi pralayakevalādyavasthāyāṃ tatkāryasya bhāvāditi|
satyametat| kintu nātra sarvathā malābhāvaḥ pūrvapakṣīkṛto yadātra bhoktṛtve malena kimiti|
bhoktṛtvaṃ hi bhogaikarasikatvātmakaṃ rāgakāryātprāguktādabhiṣvaṅgādeva dṛṣṭātsiddhamiti kimatra malasyāpi hetutvena kalpitena|
rāgasyaivātra pāramparyeṇa hetutvamiti praśnārthaḥ|
tanna virodha iti| ata evātra malasyābhyupagamenaiva samādhiḥ
body.translated_text: What is this question? If [the question is] that being obscurable is here called 'the state of being an experiencer,' rather than exclusive relish for enjoyment — and if so, then <s>mala</s> alone is to be stated [as the cause], what need is there of <s>rāga</s>? — then the question 'what need of <s>rāga</s>' would be appropriate, but not 'what need of <s>mala</s>.' [However, the objector argues:] even in the absence of <s>rāga</s>, its effect exists in states such as <s>pralayakevala</s> (dissolution-isolation) and the like. True. But the objector here is not denying <s>mala</s> entirely — in which case 'what need of <s>mala</s> for the state of being an experiencer?' The state of being an experiencer, having the nature of exclusive relish for enjoyment, is established as arising from <s>rāga</s> — from the previously stated clinging (<s>abhiṣvaṅga</s>), which is the effect of <s>rāga</s>, and which is directly observed. So what need is there of additionally positing <s>mala</s> as a cause? <s>Rāga</s> alone is the cause here through a succession [of causes] — this is the meaning of the question. There is no contradiction — and for this very reason the resolution is made here by accepting <s>mala</s> [as the ultimate cause]:

children.translated_text: That which is called the state of being an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>)
has beginningless <s>mala</s> as its cause.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadetadbhoktṛtvamasmābhiḥ prāguktaṃ tadanādi| yato malakāraṇamuktaṃ tato
malasyānāditvāttadapyanādi| etaduktaṃ bhavati---anyadevāsmānmohajanitādbhoktṛtvādbhogayogyatvalakṣaṇametadbhoktṛtvam|
pralayākale vidyate na tu vijñānakevale karmābhāvāt|
tasya karmavanmalo 'pi kāraṇaṃ pariṇatamalasya pralayākalasyāpi parameśvarānugrāhyatvānna tatsambhavati yataḥ|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
This capacity for experience (<s>bhoktṛtva</s>) that we have previously mentioned is beginningless. Since <s>mala</s> (impurity) has been stated as the cause, and since <s>mala</s> is beginningless, that [capacity for experience] too is beginningless. What is stated amounts to this: this capacity for experience, characterized by fitness for enjoyment, is different from the capacity for experience born of delusion.
It exists in the <s>pralayākala</s> [state] but not in the <s>vijñānakevala</s>, due to the absence of <s>karma</s>.
Since <s>mala</s> too, like <s>karma</s>, is a cause for the <s>pralayākala</s> whose <s>mala</s> has matured, [and since he] is fit to receive the grace of the Supreme Lord, that [objection] does not arise, because:
Therefore, desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>) is not the cause of this [bondage]. It is said:

children.translated_text: 'Desire [exists only] when the body exists;
that body — from what cause [does it arise]?'
'<s>Rāga</s> (attachment) too, since its cause is that [body],
has arisen [from it].'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
abhilāṣo 'pyayaṃ sati sthūle 'smiñcharīre bhavatīti| taccharīraṃ sūkṣmadehātmakarāgādisambandhāt|
rāgādīnāṃ tu pravṛttau tadbhoktṛtvaṃ nimittamiti kathamasyābhilāṣo nimittamāśaṅkyate| abhilāṣahetorasya rāgāderapyetannimittatvāt|
tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
This desire too exists only when this gross body exists. And that body [exists] because of the connection with <s>rāga</s> and the like, which are of the nature of the subtle body.
But since the capacity for experience is the cause of the operation of <s>rāga</s> and the like, how is desire suspected as the cause? Because even <s>rāga</s> and the like, which are the causes of desire, have this [capacity for experience] as their cause.
An illustration for this:

children.translated_text: 'But of a person,
theft being the seed, on account of [which],
just as [there follows] binding in fetters;
so, on account of <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being a bound soul),
the <s>rāga-tattva</s> (principle of attachment) operates.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā cauryaṃ bījabhūtamā samantādapekṣyapuruṣasya nigaḍādibandhanaṃ pravartate tathaiva prāguktanayena

children.text: pralayakevalinaḥ paśutvaṃ malamapekṣya rāgādayaḥ pravartanta iti kuto rāgasyātra hetutvamāśaṅkyate| tadevaṃ
children.translated_text: for the <s>pralayakevalin</s>, <s>rāga</s> and the like operate on account of <s>paśutva</s> (the state of being bound), which is <s>mala</s>. So how is <s>rāga</s> suspected as the cause here? Thus:

body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
Just as binding in fetters and the like operates for a person on account of theft, which is the seed — so too, by the method previously stated,

children.translated_text: 'From this [<s>mala</s>], the capacity for experience belongs to this [soul];
the body [and] experience arise from other causes.'
'For by <s>paśutva</s>, the capacity for experience [arises];
the bond of <s>māyā</s> is established in the body;
experience consisting of pleasure, pain, and the like
is established for the <s>paśu</s> from <s>karma</s>;
no other [explanation] has been prescribed
for the bondage of experience, experiencer, and [body].'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
paśutvasaṃjñakānmalādasya bhoktṛtvaṃ māyātastaccharīraṃ karmataḥ punarbhogaḥ karmaṇāmeva sukhaduḥkhātmanā pariṇāmāditi sākṣānnimittatvamatroktaṃ na tu paramparayā pāramparyeṇa sarvasyāsya māyātmanaḥ karmākṣiptatvāditi darśayiṣyāmaḥ|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
From <s>mala</s>, designated as <s>paśutva</s>, the capacity for experience belongs to this [soul]; from <s>māyā</s>, the body; from <s>karma</s>, experience — since <s>karmas</s> themselves transform into the nature of pleasure and pain. Thus the direct causation is stated here; but the indirect [causation] — that all this, being of the nature of <s>māyā</s>, is impelled by <s>karma</s> — this we shall demonstrate.

body.text: karmataśca śarīrāṇi viṣayāḥ karaṇāni ca| iti|
body.translated_text: 'And from <s>karma</s> [arise] bodies, objects, and instruments.' Thus.

body.text: nānyathaitasya bhogaśca bhoktṛtvaṃ ca śarīraṃ ca vinirdiṣṭamiti| tadiyatā paśupadārthaḥ parīkṣita iti||
body.translated_text: 'No other [explanation] for the experience, capacity for experience, and body of this [soul] has been prescribed.' Thus, to this extent, the category of <s>paśu</s> has been examined.
Now, for the purpose of a specific examination of the category of <s>pāśa</s> (bond), the following question [arises] incidentally:

children.translated_text: 'That <s>karma</s>, O Lord of gods,
which has been declared as the cause of experience —
the acquisition of <s>karma</s> [requires] the body being present;
[but] at the time of creation, whence comes the body?'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadetatsukhaduḥkhādiko bhoga ityādinā karma bhoganibandhanamuktaṃ tanna vyāpakamityadhyāhāraḥ| yato mahāpralayādanantaraṃ sargārambhakāle prathamaḥ śarīrādibhogaḥ kutaścideva nimittādiṣyate| na karmataḥ|
taduttarakālabhāvināṃ karmanimittatvāditi| yadāhuḥ---
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
That which has been stated as '<s>karma</s> is the cause of experience' through [statements like] 'experience consisting of pleasure and pain' and so on — that is not all-encompassing; this is the implied addition. For at the beginning of creation after the great dissolution, the first experience of body and the like is required to come from some cause. [But there is no <s>karma</s> to produce the first body.]

body.text: ādyo hi dehaḥ puruṣārthamūlastato 'pyanye karmamūlāḥ pratipannā iti|
body.translated_text: 'For the first body has the <s>puruṣa's</s> purpose as its root; subsequent [bodies] are understood to have <s>karma</s> as their root.'

body.text: ādyo hi dehaḥ\devdot pratipannāḥ Source unknown. Also quoted in \NarP, p.212 ad 3:87, but with prapannāḥ for pratipannāḥ

body.translated_text: Here is the established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: 'Just as <s>mala</s> (impurity) of this [soul] is beginningless,
so too <s>karma</s> is beginningless.'
'If [<s>karma</s> is] beginningless, how is it established?
[And] by what cause is the variety [of experiences]?'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
puruṣāṇāṃ hi sarvadā śārīrabhogādivaicitryānyathānupapattyā karmaṇaḥ sattvaṃ sṛṣṭikāle 'pi paśumṛgapakṣisarīsṛpasthāvaramanuṣyādi janmavaicitryaśruteḥ|
mahāpralaye 'pi karmasiddhitaḥ pravāhānādiḥ karmaśarīraprabandhaḥ siddhyati|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
For the variety of bodily experiences and the like of all souls at all times is [explicable] only through the existence of <s>karma</s>, since no other explanation is possible; and at the time of creation too, the variety of births — as <s>paśu</s> (animal), deer, bird, reptile, plant, human, and so on — is known from scripture.
Even at the great dissolution, from the establishment of <s>karma</s>, the beginninglessness of its stream [is established].

body.text: Testimonium: kiraṇavṛttau bhagavatā rāmakaṇṭhena `puruṣāṇāṃ hi sarvathā śarīrabhogavaicitryānyathānupapattyā karmaṇaḥ satvam| prathamasṛṣṭikāle 'pi paśupakṣimṛgasarīsṛpasthāvaramanuṣyādivaicitryaśruteḥ mahāpraLaye 'pi karmasiddhitaḥ pravāhānādiḥ karmaśarīraprabandhaḥ siddhyatī'ti vyākhyātam|

children.translated_text: 'Therefore <s>karma</s> is beginningless;
<s>māyā</s> too is likewise; so too is existence (<s>bhava</s>);
likewise, <s>Śiva</s>, the creator, is beginningless,
established [as the lord] of the entire universe.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ karmanibandhano bhavaḥ kalādikṣitiparyantatattva bhūtabhuvanarūpaḥ saṃsāro māyīyastannibandhanaṃ ca punararjyamānaṃ karmeti karmabhavayoḥ parasparahetutvena pravāhānāditvasiddhiḥ|
bhavānāditvādeva ca tadupādānena karmānāditvācca tadadhikaraṇenāpi prakṛtyātmanānādinā bhavitavyam|
kṛṣyādikarmaṇāṃ prakṛtisaṃskārakatvena dṛṣṭatvānnaiyāyikādiparikalpitātmasaṃskārakatvāyogādātmanaḥ pariṇāmitvaprasaṅgācca|
yacca tadbhavo pādānaṃ karmādhikaraṇaṃ ca sā māyāpyanādisiddhā|
tathā bhavasya tanukaraṇabhuvanātmanaḥ pravāhānāditvenoktatvāttatkartāpīśvaro 'nādiḥ sidhyatīti|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
Thus, existence (<s>bhava</s>) — <s>saṃsāra</s>, consisting of the <s>māyīya</s> <s>tattvas</s> from <s>kalā</s> to <s>kṣiti</s> (earth), the elements, and worlds, caused by <s>karma</s> — and <s>karma</s> that is being re-acquired, being dependent on that [existence] — thus the beginninglessness of the stream [is established] through the mutual causality of <s>karma</s> and existence.
From the beginninglessness of existence,
Now, after the specific examination of the category of <s>pāśa</s>, incidentally for the purpose of examining the category of <s>pati</s> (Lord), a question [is raised]:

children.translated_text: '<s>Śiva</s> has been declared by you as the creator;
how is He known, O Lord?'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
īśvare hi jagatkartari siddhe tasyānāditvaṃ sādhayituṃ śakyam| sa eva kathaṃ gamyate| na tāvatpratyakṣato 'tīndriyatvena tasya bhavadbhirabhyupagamāt| taduktaṃ jaiminīyaiḥ
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
For if the Lord as creator of the world is established, then His beginninglessness can be proven. But how is He known? Not through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), since you accept that He is beyond the senses. As the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> have said:

body.text: na ca kaiścidasau jñātuṃ kadācidapi śakyate|
body.translated_text: 'And He can never be known by anyone at all;

body.text: 57cd, 58ab and 60. Also cited ad \Mat\VP\ 3:6, p.49 and before \Nar\ 2:1, p.113.

body.translated_text: even if perceived in His own nature, creatorship is not ascertained.'
'And through His own statement, this cognition is not firmly established;
for even without having created, He might say [He did], out of desire to establish His own sovereignty.'

body.text: nāpi rūpopalabdhyādinā cakṣurādiriva pūrvoktatanukaraṇabhuvanādikāryānyathānupapatti lakṣaṇenānumānena tasya mahābhūtebhya evotpattidṛṣṭeḥ| yadāhuḥ saugatāḥ
body.translated_text: Nor [is He known] through perception of form and the like, nor through inference characterized by the impossibility of explaining otherwise the effects — body, instruments, worlds, and the like — mentioned before; for their origination from the great elements alone is observed. As the Buddhists (<s>Saugatas</s>) say:
'When a certain thing exists, another thing comes into being; then in imagining [a cause] other [than that],

body.text: 1:26 (with yeṣu satsu for yasminsati). Also cited ad \Nar\ 1:4, p.9 and 2:4, p.120 and \Mat\VP\ 6:21, p.152.

body.translated_text: through the connection with surgical instruments, medicines, and the like, there is the healing of <s>Caitra's</s> wound;

body.text: asambaddhasya kiṃ sthāṇoḥ kāraṇatvaṃ prakalpyate|| iti|
body.translated_text: what creatorship should be imagined for the uninvolved post?'

body.text:
nāpyāgamena tasyākṛtakatvena bhavadbhiranabhyupagamāt|
tatkṛtasyānyonyasaṃśrayeṇāprāmāṇyāt| na ca pramāṇāntaramasti bhavatām|
tatsādhanapramāṇābhāvānna kathaṃcidgamyata ityarthaḥ|
body.translated_text:
Nor through <s>āgama</s> (scripture), since you do not accept it as uncreated.
And if it is made by Him [i.e., God], then [there is] mutual dependence and hence invalidity. And you have no other means of valid knowledge.
Therefore, due to the absence of a validating means of knowledge, He cannot be known in any way — this is the meaning.

body.text: yadyevamata evaitadviṣayasaṃśayo 'stu| nāstīśvara iti kuto bādhakapramāṇābhāvāditi| ucyate|
body.translated_text: If so, then let there be doubt regarding this matter. [One might say:] 'There is no God' — how? Because of the absence of a refuting proof. To this it is said:

children.translated_text: 'Due to the absence of instruments and due to immateriality,
how can creatorship be justified?'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
karaṇānāmabhāvo vaikaraṇyaṃ tasmādīśvaro jagataḥ kartā na saṃbhavati| karaṇābhāvāddaṇḍacakrasūtrādirahitaḥ kumbhakāra iva kumbhe| tadidamuktaṃ jaiminīyaiḥ
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
The absence of instruments is <s>vaikaraṇya</s>; therefore, the Lord is not possible as the creator of the world — due to the absence of instruments, like a potter without staff, wheel, cord, and the like, with respect to a pot. As the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> have said:

body.text: na ca niḥsādhanaḥ kartā kaścitsṛjati kiñcana| iti|
body.translated_text: 'No creator without instruments creates anything.'

body.text: na ca niḥsādhanaḥ kartā kaścitsṛjati kiñcana \Sloka\ {sambandhākṣepaparihāra
kiñca mūrtatvaṃ kaṭhinatā| atra śarīrayogastadabhāvādīśvaro na sambhavati karteti| tadidamuktaṃ taireva
body.translated_text: Moreover, materiality (<s>mūrtatva</s>) means solidity; [it implies] connection with a body — due to its absence, the Lord is not possible as a creator. As those same [<s>Jaiminīyas</s>] have said:
'A bodiless ruler — the self — would be like a liberated self [i.e., incapable of action].'

body.text: aśarīro hyadhiṣṭhātā nātmā muktātmavadbhavet \Slokas\ 78cd. Also quoted ad \Nar\ 2:8, p.130 and frequently in the \MatV.

ityevaṃ sādhakabādhakapramāṇābhāvasadbhāvābhyāmīśvarābhāvasiddhiriti
pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ| atra siddhānto bādhakanirāsapūrvaḥ| tasminhyanirākṛte sādhakasya hetorapravṛttireva|
tatpratijñāvacanasyānumānanirākṛtatvāt| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text:
Thus, through the absence and presence of establishing and refuting proofs, the non-existence of God is established — this is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's position). Here is the <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), preceded by the refutation of the objections. For without refuting those, the establishing reason cannot operate.
Because the proposition-statement has been refuted by inference. As they say:
'When doubt exists, from the statement of a reason, the reason, being ungrounded, is reversed.'
Thus it is commenced:

children.translated_text: 'Just as time, though immaterial,
is seen to bring about results,
so too <s>Śiva</s>, though immaterial,
creates effects through [His] will (<s>icchā</s>).'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatra yastāvadakartṛtvasiddhāvatrāmūrtatvāditi heturuktaḥ sa kālenānaikāntikastasyāmūrtatve 'pi puṣpaphalādikartṛtvaprasiddheḥ|
atha kālasyācetanatvena svakāryaṃ prati kāraṇatvātkartṛtvāsiddheḥ nānaikāntikaviṣayatā| tatrocyate tarhi kālasyātropalakṣaṇatvādasmadādyātmanānaikāntikastasyāmūrtasyāpi svadehaspandādikāryadarśanāt|
dṛṣṭānto 'pyatra sādhyadharmāsiddhaḥ muktātmano 'pyasmābhiḥ sarvādhiṣṭhātṛtvenābhyupagamāditi|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
The reason stated for establishing [God's] non-creatorship — 'because of immateriality' — that is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) because of time (<s>kāla</s>), since time, though immaterial, is well-known as the producer of flowers, fruits, and the like.
But [one might say:] since time is insentient and is a cause only with respect to its own effect, creatorship is not established — hence there is no inconclusiveness. To this it is said: then, because time is merely illustrative here, [the reason is] inconclusive because of ourselves [i.e., embodied selves] and other selves, since even an immaterial [entity] is observed to produce effects such as the movement of its own body.
The example too is unestablished with respect to the property of what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) — because even the liberated self is accepted by us as the ruler of all.

body.text: yastvatravaikaraṇyāditi heturuktaḥ so 'pyasiddha eva| tathā hi
body.translated_text: As for the reason stated here — 'because of the absence of instruments' — that too is simply unestablished. For:

children.translated_text: '<s>Icchā</s> (will) alone is His instrument,
just as it is accepted for the accomplished <s>yogin</s>.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
icchātmikaiva śaktistasya karaṇaṃ yogina iva vidyate yataḥ|
yoginaśca sarvavādināṃ siddhā eva cārvākairapi viṣagrahacikitsākāritvena
maṇyauṣadhādivanna pratikṣeptuṃ śakyāḥ| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
The power that is of the nature of will (<s>icchā</s>) is His instrument — it exists, just as for the <s>yogin</s>.
And <s>yogins</s> are accepted by all schools — even the <s>Cārvākas</s> cannot reject them, since [<s>yogins</s>'] efficacy in treating poison and possession
is like that of gems, medicines, and the like. As they say:
'The power of gems, mantras, and medicines is inconceivable.'

body.text: acintyo hi maṇimantrauṣadhīnāṃ prabhāvaḥ Also occurs in

body.translated_text: But if the intended reason is merely the absence of sense organs — even to that it is replied:
'A lodestone is seen to attract iron filings

children.translated_text: even without sense organs;
the operation is not seen,
[yet] the effect — [produced by] will — is perceived.'

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tadānīmayaskāntamaṇinānaikāntiko hetuḥ| sa hīndriyahīno 'pi śalyātmakāyaḥsamākarṣako dṛṣṭo yataḥ| atrāpi prāguktakālavadanaikāntikākṣepatatsamarthanaṃ tathaiva draṣṭavyamiti|
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
In that case, the reason is inconclusive because of the lodestone. For it, though devoid of sense organs, is seen to attract iron bodies. Here too, the refutation of inconclusiveness as in the case of time previously mentioned should be understood in the same way.
