Thus, when the refuting [argument] that would establish non-existence has been removed, now a proof is stated for removing the doubt about existence:

children.translated_text: 'The gross and variegated effect
would not exist otherwise, like a pot;
therefore there exists some cause.' ||

body.text:
Vṛtti:
iha hīśvarasiddhau sāṃkhyasaugatajaiminīyārhatacārvākāḥ pratipakṣāḥ| tatra pūrvayoryadetadvicitrakamityadṛṣṭakartṛkaṃ tanukaraṇabhuvanādikaṃ prāguktaṃ jagaddharmitvena cikīrṣitaṃ tatpratikṣaṇaṃ pariṇāmādutpādādvā kāryatvena siddhameva| apareṣāṃ tu
body.translated_text:
Vṛtti:
Here, in establishing God's existence, the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>, Buddhists, <s>Jaiminīyas</s>, <s>Jainas</s>, and <s>Cārvākas</s> are the opponents. Among them, for the first two, this variegated [universe] — without a [known] creator — consisting of bodies, instruments, worlds, and the like, previously described as having the property of being a world — is already established as an effect through its constant transformation or production. But for the others,
'The world has never been different [from what it is now]' —

body.text: na kadācidanīdṛśaṃ jagat Source unknown. Also quoted ad \Nar\ 2:1, p.115.

ityabhyupagamāttadekadeśabhuvanādi tathā na siddhamiti tānprati
sthūlatvena kāryatvamatra sādhyate| yatsthūlaṃ tatkāryaṃ yathā ghaṭādi sthūlaṃ caitadadṛṣṭakartṛkaṃ bhuvanādi tataḥ kāryamiti|
na cātreśvaraśarīreṇa nityena vedena vānaikāntikatvam| yathoktaṃ jaiminīyaiḥ
body.translated_text:
since they accept this, a particular portion [of the world] such as the worlds and the like is not established [as an effect] for them. Therefore, for them, effect-nature is to be established here through grossness. Whatever is gross is an effect, like a pot and the like; and this — worlds and the like without a [known] creator — is gross; therefore it is an effect.
Nor is there inconclusiveness here because of the eternal body of God or the eternal <s>Veda</s>. As the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> say:
'Your reason would be inconclusive because of that [God's] body and the like.'

body.text: anekāntaśca hetuste taccharīrādinā bhavet \Slokas\ 77ab. Quoted ad \Nar\ 2:8, p.133 and ad \Mrg\ 1:9, p.21.

tasyāsmābhiḥ sarvathā vedasya cānityatvenābhyupagamāt| tasminnapi ca kārye siddhe 'dhunā kāryatvenātra sarvasmiñjagati kartṛpūrvakatvaṃ sādhyate|
na tu sthūlatvena tadvyāpakatvāditi|
yatkāryaṃ tadviśiṣṭajñānakriyāyuktakartrā vinā na sidhyatīti yathā ghaṭādi| kāryaṃ caitatsarvameva jagat|
atastadapi viśiṣṭajñānakriyāyuktena kartrā vinā na bhavatīti|
yastatkartā sa īśvaraḥ siddha evetyevamatra padatrayasya nānyonyaṃ gatārthatetyavirodhaḥ|
na ca kāryatvamatra tathābhūtaṃ na siddhamityāśaṅkanīyam| yadāhuḥ saugatāḥ
body.translated_text:
Since both [the body of God and the <s>Veda</s>] are accepted by us as non-eternal in every respect. And when effect-nature has been established in that [universe], now what is to be established is that all this world, being an effect, is preceded by a creator.
Not [merely] through grossness, since that [creatorship] pervades [effect-nature more broadly].
That which is an effect does not come about without a creator endowed with specific knowledge and action — like a pot and the like. And all this world is an effect.
Therefore, it too does not come about without a creator endowed with specific knowledge and action.
The one who is that creator — He is God, [and His existence is] established. Thus, there is no mutual redundancy among the three statements here.
Nor should it be suspected that effect-nature of this kind is not established. As the Buddhists say:
'That which is established as possessing the invariable concomitance with the presence and absence of a presiding being,

body.text: siddhaṃ yādṛgadhiṣṭātṛ\devdot hutāśane Pramāṇavārttika 1:13--14. Also quoted ad \Mat\VP\ 6:100, p.227 and ad \Nar\ 2:5, p.122.

body.translated_text: [and] that arrangement and the like which is connected with it — from that, what is inferred;
for things that are different, from mere similarity of words, of something that is non-different —
inference is not justified, like [inferring] fire from a pale substance.'

body.text:
kāryamātrasya kartṛmātreṇa ghaṭādau kṛtakatvamātrasyānityatvamātreṇeva vyāpteḥ siddhatvāt| anyathā tatrāpyanyatrāpi ca dṛṣṭāntasādhyadharmabhedena hetubhedakalpane sarvānumānābhāva eva| aviśeṣātpāṇḍutvasya tu bhāvāt dhūmābhāve 'pi himamakkolādiṣu ca taddarśanāt vahnyanumāpakatvamayuktameva|

body.translated_text: creatorship by a non-God, [something] perishable, and the like would follow.'

body.text: viparyayavyāptyabhāvāt| dṛṣṭānte hi ghaṭādāvayaṃ hetuḥ svasādhye svakāryasarvajñatvasarvakartṛtvalakṣaṇeneśvaratvena vyāptaḥ siddho yatastasyāṃśenāpi vaikalyena ghaṭādarśanādavināśitvenāpi kumbhakārātmano nityatvāttasyaiva ca kartṛtvāt| nāpi dharmisvarūpaviparītasādhano 'yaṃ viruddhaḥ| yathāha maṇḍanaḥ
body.translated_text: Because there is no counter-pervasion. For in the example—pots and the like—this reason [of being an effect] is established as pervaded by its own probandum, namely, lordship characterized by omniscience and omnipotence of its maker. This is because even when part [of the pot] is missing—as when a pot is not seen—the pot-maker as a self is not destroyed, since he is permanent; and because he alone is the maker. Nor is this [reason] contradictory as establishing [something] opposed to the nature of the subject. As <s>Maṇḍana</s> says:
'Even though everything possessing arrangement is caused by an intelligent [agent],

body.text: pp.219 and 224. Quoted ad \Mat\VP\ 6:100, p.229 and (second verse only) ad \Nar\ 2:20, p.146.

body.translated_text: how can a well-known arrangement alone be the single cause?' ||
'The parts of a chariot and the like, though fashioned by different carpenters,
are generally seen in the world as mutually helpful and helping.' ||
Since it is observed that the parts of chariots and the like, though made by many carpenters, do not begin as a single chariot without the intelligence and action of a single master-builder.

body.text:
nāpyanīśvarakartṛkaṃ jagat kāryatvāt ghaṭādivaditi viruddhāvyabhicāryākrāntatvādaheturayamiti vācyam|
dhūmādagnyanumānavadatra vastubalapravṛttatvena tadasambhavāditi bhavatāmabhyupagamaḥ|
anyathā parvatādāvapi dhūmādagnyanumāne 'trāparvatavartī vahniḥ dhūmāt yatra dhūmastatrāparvatavartī vahniryathā mahānase 'tra ca dhūmastasmādaparvatavartī vahniriti sarvatra viruddhāvyabhicāryanumānāvaskarasaṃbhavādanumānābhāva evetyevamādayo 'tra hetudoṣā vistareṇāsmābhirnareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśe pratikṣiptā iti tata evāvadhāryāḥ|
body.translated_text: Nor should it be said that [the argument] 'the world is not made by a non-Lord, because it is an effect, like a pot' is a non-reason because it is pervaded by counter-balanced opposition (<s>viruddhāvyabhicārin</s>). For your own position is that [such reasoning] proceeds by the force of reality, like the inference of fire from smoke, and therefore that [counter-balanced opposition] is not possible. Otherwise, even in the inference of fire from smoke on a mountain—'here is fire not situated on a mountain, because of smoke; wherever there is smoke, there is fire not situated on a mountain, as in a kitchen; and here there is smoke; therefore there is fire not situated on a mountain'—since the possibility of counter-balanced opposition reasoning would arise everywhere, there would be no inference at all. Such and other flaws in reasoning have been refuted in detail by us in the <s>Nareśvaraparīkṣāprakāśa</s>, and should be ascertained from there.
Here is the opponent's view:
If <s>karma</s> [is the cause]—

body.text:
Vṛtti:
anena hi prayogavacanena bhavadbhiḥ kartṛmātraṃ sādhyamupakṣiptam|
taccobhayavādisiddhaṃ karmāstviti śrāvaṇaḥ śabda itivatsiddhasādhanatvādayuktametat| yadāhurjaiminīyāḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: By this formulation, you have introduced mere agency as the probandum. But that [agency] is established by both parties—<s>karma</s> can be [the agent]—like the auditory word being a [valid means]; thus this is the fallacy of proving what is already established (<s>siddhasādhana</s>). As the <s>Jaiminīyas</s> say:
'Regarding whatever is desired as the controller of a mere cause—
since that is established by <s>karmas</s> for all entities, it is the fallacy of proving the established.' ||
Here is the doctrinal position:

children.translated_text: For [<s>karma</s>] is not conscious. ||

body.text:
Vṛtti:
na siddhasādhanaṃ yasmātkarmācetanamiti|
ayamarthaḥ---nāsmābhiratra kartṛtvamātraṃ sādhyate 'pi tu viśiṣṭajñānakriyāyuktaḥ karteti kuto 'cetanaiḥ karmabhiḥ siddhasādhanamiti|
yadyevaṃ dharmiviśeṣaviparītasādhano 'yaṃ viruddhaḥ| yadāhuḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: It is not the fallacy of proving the established, since <s>karma</s> is non-conscious. The meaning is this: we do not establish mere agency here, but rather an agent endowed with specific knowledge and action—so how can it be the fallacy of proving the established through non-conscious <s>karmas</s>? If so, [you might say] this is contradictory (<s>viruddha</s>) as establishing [something] opposed to the specific nature of the subject. As they say:

body.text: kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena kartrā vyāptaṃ sadaiva yat|
body.translated_text: 'An effect is always pervaded by a maker who possesses a body;

body.text: kāryaṃ śarīrayuktena\devdot prasajyate Source unknown. Also cited ad \Mat\VP\ 6:100, p.229 with ghaṭādi for sadaiva
kāryatvāttena jagataḥ kartā dehī prasajyate|| iti|
body.translated_text: therefore, from the world being an effect, the maker must be embodied.' ||
That is improper, because—

children.translated_text: He has been described as without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), gross,
and also as both with and without parts (<s>sakalaniṣkala</s>).
The Lord, <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the Peaceful One—
is differentiated by the difference in functions.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
kāryasya śarīravyabhicārāt svadehaspandātmakaṃ kāryamasmadāderna dehāntarapūrvakaṃ siddhamityuktaṃ yataḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Since effect deviates from [requiring] a body—for it is established that the effect of our own bodily movement is not preceded by another body—as stated:

body.text: śaktodyuktaḥ pravṛttaśca kartā trividha iṣyate| iti|
body.translated_text: 'The agent is accepted as threefold: capable, prepared, and engaged.' ||

body.text: śaktodyuktaḥ pravṛttaśca kartā trividha iṣyate Source unknown. Also cited ad \Mat\VP\ 3:20, p.69. Bhatt there observes that it appears as
14 (p.22) and is attributed to the \Mrg. In both those places the first {pāda} reads śaktodyuktapravṛttaśca---an `improved' reading in which it is no longer necessary to assume a double sandhi.

tatra yacchaktatvaṃ kāryaṃ prati yogyatvaṃ sā niṣkalāvasthā śānta ityucyate| yattūdyuktatvaṃ sā sakalaniṣkalāvasthā sadāśivaḥ kathyate|
pravṛttakriyatvaṃ tu sthūlāvasthā īśvara iti|
kṛtyaviṣayo 'yamavasthābhedastenopacārādetattattvatrayaṃ bhinnamityucyate| na paramārthatvādityarthaḥ| yadvakṣyati
body.translated_text: Among these, the capacity—the fitness with respect to the effect—that is the <s>niṣkala</s> (partless) state, called 'the Peaceful One' (<s>Śānta</s>). The preparedness (<s>udyuktatva</s>)—that is the <s>sakalaniṣkala</s> (both with and without parts) state, called <s>Sadāśiva</s>. And the engagement in action—that is the gross (<s>sthūla</s>) state, [called] <s>Īśvara</s>. This differentiation of states pertains to [different] functions; through figurative usage, [what is really one] is said to be the three distinct <s>tattvas</s> (principles). Not because of ultimate reality—that is the meaning. As will be stated:
'But for the sake of gracing souls, even the Supreme assumes the state of the lower.' ||

body.text: evaṃ ca jñānapadārthasyāpyatraiva parīkṣāsiddhiḥ| atra praśnaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, the examination of the category of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is also established right here. Here is the question:

children.translated_text: How is the partless one (<s>niṣkala</s>) to be known?
And the person (<s>pumān</s>) when he is <s>sakala</s> (with parts)?
And the other who has a dual nature—
how is he not self-contradictory?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
iha hi pūrvaṃ śivajñānaṃ tathā tasyetyādinā
body.translated_text: Commentary: For previously, through 'the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, likewise of that' and so on—

body.text: ākāravāṃstvaṃ niyamādupāsyo na vastvanākāramupaiti buddhiḥ| iti|
body.translated_text: 'You who possess form must necessarily be worshipped; the intellect does not apprehend a formless reality.' ||

body.text: ākāravāṃstvaṃ\devdot buddhiḥ Source unknown. Cited ad \Mat\VP\ 3:23, p.71; by \Agh\ ad \TatP\ 6; and by \Tryambaka\ ad \Kir\ 3:20, p.\thinspace 66, lines 1--2. Bhatt observes that it is cited [by J\ñānaprakāśa] in the [

tataścāśakyānuṣṭheyatvāttadviṣayajñānamanupadeśyameva|
nāpīśvaraḥ sakalo bhavati śarīritvena devadattādivatsarvajñatvakartṛtvābhāvāt|
nāpi sakalaniṣkalaṃ nāma vastu sambhavati viruddhayorghaṭatadabhāvayorivaikatra samāveśāsambhavāditi tattvatrayādasmādekasya jñānopadeśavaiyarthyāddvayośca svarūpānupapatterevāvaktavyateti praśnārthaḥ| siddhāntastu
body.translated_text: And therefore, since [worship of the formless] is impossible to practice, the knowledge concerning it is simply unteachable. Nor does the Lord become <s>sakala</s> (embodied) like <s>Devadatta</s> and others, because of the absence of omniscience and omnipotence [in ordinary embodied beings]. Nor is a reality that is both <s>sakala</s> and <s>niṣkala</s> possible, since contradictory [properties] like a pot and its non-existence cannot co-exist in one [entity]. Therefore, from the three <s>tattvas</s>, the teaching of knowledge regarding one would be futile, and regarding the other two, since their essential nature is not established, they would be ineffable—this is the purport of the question. The doctrinal answer is:

children.translated_text: Through the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) upon the bound soul,
and always through the power of <s>mantra</s>,
the partless (<s>niṣkala</s>) is perceived through [the soul's awakened] power—
the subtle one, like the effect of poison.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
paśoryaḥ parameśvarācchaktipāto yā ca mantraśaktirdīkṣā tābhyāṃ yā śaktirjñānakriyātmikā nirmalīkṛtā tayā sarvadaiva niṣkalatattvaṃ lakṣyate|
viṣadīkṣāśuddhasya mantriṇaḥ śaktyaiva viṣasya vikāro mṛtitāpātmaka iva| śaktyatiśayakhyāpanāṃśatvena dṛṣṭāntatvam|
ayaṃ tvatrārthaḥ---yadi niṣkalatvādevāsya jñeyatvaṃ nopapadyata iti praśnastadātmanā vyabhicāraḥ| tasya kāryakaraṇavyatirekeṇa svataḥ parataśca kāyavāgvyavahārātmanānumānena jñeyatvāt|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Through the descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>) from the Supreme Lord upon the bound soul, and through the <s>mantra</s>-power that is initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>)—by the power consisting of knowledge and action that has been purified through these—the <s>niṣkala</s> <s>tattva</s> is always perceived. Like the transformation of poison—consisting of death and burning—[perceived through] the power of a <s>mantrin</s> (spell-master) purified by the initiation of the poison [-removing mantra]. This illustration serves to demonstrate the extraordinary nature of [spiritual] power. But the meaning here is this: if the question is that the <s>niṣkala</s> cannot be known precisely because of its partlessness, then there is deviation from [the probandum] by that [reason] itself. For it is knowable through inference—through verbal and bodily conduct—apart from [the usual] effects and instruments, both by itself and through another.

body.text: atha bauddhasya jñānasyākāragrahaṇenaiva vastuvyavasthāpakatvādanākāro na jñeya iti praśnārthaḥ| tadā siddhasādhanatvameva jñānaśaktyaivātra tasya jñeyatvenoktatvānna buddhyādibhirityadoṣaḥ| yo 'pi sakalatvāt bhagavato 'nīśvaratvaprasaṅga uktaḥ so 'pyayukta ityucyate
body.translated_text: If the question means that according to Buddhist [epistemology], since knowledge establishes objects only through grasping their form (<s>ākāra</s>), the formless cannot be known—then it is simply the fallacy of proving the established, since it has been stated here that it is knowable precisely through the power of knowledge; [thus] there is no fault [in our position] that it is not [known] through intellect and the like. As for the objection stated—that the Lord's being <s>sakala</s> would entail his being a non-Lord—that too is said to be improper:

children.translated_text: Even though <s>sakala</s> (possessing parts), the person [i.e., the Lord] is not [like an ordinary soul],
because of the exclusion of <s>māyā</s>-constituents.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
anyadevaitatsakalatvaṃ sakalaśaktiprasarātmakaṃ yadyogādīśvaro 'pi sakala ityucyate| na tu puruṣavanmāyīyakalādiśarīrayogāditi sakalaśabdavācyatve 'pyatra na puruṣatvaṃ tathābhūtasya sakalatvasyāsiddhatvāditi bhāvaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: This <s>sakala</s>-nature is of a different kind—consisting in the manifestation of all powers—by virtue of which the Lord too is called '<s>sakala</s>' through <s>yoga</s>. But it is not through union with a body of <s>kalā</s> and the like [produced by] <s>māyā</s>, as in the case of ordinary souls. Therefore, even though the word '<s>sakala</s>' is applicable, there is no personhood [as in ordinary beings], because such <s>sakala</s>-nature [as applies to ordinary souls] is not established [for the Lord]—this is the purport.

body.text: atha kartṛtvāttasya puruṣasyeva kathaṃ na māyātmikāstāḥ kalāḥ kalpyanta iti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: But if he is an agent, why should those <s>kalās</s> consisting of <s>māyā</s> not be postulated [for him] just as for the soul? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: Because of <s>Śiva</s>'s purity,
impure <s>kalās</s> should not be postulated [for him] here.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
anyathāsiddhatvādasya hetoryato na māyātmikāstāḥ kalāḥ puṃsaḥ kartṛtvaṃ janayanti yena tadanyathānupapattyātra kalpyāḥ syuḥ|
pariṇāmitvenācetanatvaprasaṅgādityuktaṃ pariṇāmo 'cetanasyetyādinā|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because this reason [of being an agent] is otherwise accounted for—since those <s>kalās</s> consisting of <s>māyā</s> do not generate agency for the soul in such a way that they would have to be postulated here because it would be impossible otherwise. As was stated—'transformation belongs to the non-conscious'—since [if the Lord underwent transformation through <s>māyā</s>] the consequence of being non-conscious would arise.

children.translated_text: His <s>kalās</s> consist of <s>mantras</s>;
and those <s>mantras</s> are of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śivasyātmabhūtā ye mantrāḥ sadyojātādayo vakṣyamāṇāsta eva
body.translated_text: Commentary: The <s>mantras</s> that are the very self of <s>Śiva</s>—<s>Sadyojāta</s> and the others, which will be described—they themselves—

children.translated_text: Having fashioned through those [mantras] his own body,
great, superimposed upon the pure sense-spheres—
As long as he does not act thus,
there is no lineage of teachers (<s>gurupaddhati</s>).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tairīśānādibhiḥ śivātmakairmantrairmūrdhādibhedena tadavāntarāṣṭatriṃśatkalābhedenendriyādyātmanā cādhyāsitaṃ svaṃ śarīraṃ dhyeyādyākāraṃ parikalpya bhagavānatra yāvadevamiti vakṣyamāṇaprakāreṇa sṛṣṭyādyanugrahaṃ na karoti tāvanna gurusādhakādikrama iti vakṣyati lakṣyate sakalaṃ dhyānāditi|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Through those <s>Śiva</s>-natured <s>mantras</s> beginning with <s>Īśāna</s>, through the division into head and other [bodily parts], through the sub-divisions of thirty-eight <s>kalās</s>, and through the sense-organs and the like as their form—having fashioned his own body in the form of objects of meditation and the like, the Lord, 'as long as thus'—until he performs grace through creation and the like in the manner to be described—there is no succession of teachers, practitioners, and the like. As will be stated: 'the <s>sakala</s> is perceived through meditation.'

children.translated_text: The embodied one [the Lord] performs grace
for all embodied beings.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śarīradvāreṇa hi sevyamāno rājādiranugrahaṃ kurvandṛśyate nāśarīrī|
asmadādyagocaratvādityatrārādhanopāyatvenākāropadeśo 'yaṃ bhagavata iti||
body.translated_text: Commentary: For a king and the like, when served through the medium of a body, is seen to bestow grace—not one who is bodiless. Since [the formless Lord] would be beyond the reach of beings like us, this teaching of form is given as a means of worship of the Lord.

body.text:
nanu yadi bhagavatastvapāramārthikaṃ śarīraṃ kathamadhiṣṭheyam|
adhiṣṭhīyamānaṃ kathaṃ na śarīramiti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: But if the Lord's body is not ultimately real, how can it be governed? And if it is being governed, how is it not [really] a body? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: Just as the power of a <s>yogin</s>
[operates] in grasping and releasing,
so too should the grasping and releasing
of the all-pervading Lord be understood.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā yogaśaktyā yogī kuḍyādikamaśarīrabhūtamapi saṃsāryanugrahārthamadhiṣṭhāya parityajati| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as a <s>yogin</s>, through yogic power, governs and then abandons even a wall and the like that are not [his] body, for the purpose of gracing transmigrating beings—as they say:
'By his mere presence, like a wish-fulfilling gem for a person,
teachings emerge at will, even from walls and the like.' ||

body.text: tathaiva parameśvaro 'pyanugrahārthaṃ bāhyapratimādivattaddhyeyākāraṃ buddhinirmitaśarīrabhūtamapyadhiṣṭhāya parityajatītyadoṣaḥ| api ca
body.translated_text: So too the Supreme Lord, for the purpose of grace, governs and then abandons [a body] that is fashioned by the intellect in the form of an object of meditation—like an external image and the like—even though it is not [his real] body. Thus there is no fault. Moreover—

children.translated_text: Through <s>mudrās</s> (gestures), <s>maṇḍalas</s> (diagrams), and <s>mantras</s>,
and the threefold activities of <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment),
the <s>sakala</s> is perceived through meditation,
from the operation of all knowledge.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
mudrāḥ parameśvarasyāvāhanavisarjanādau tacchaktyabhivyaktisthānatayā vakṣyamāṇāḥ karasanniveśaviśeṣāḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: <s>Mudrās</s> are the specific hand-configurations to be described, which serve as the loci for the manifestation of the Supreme Lord's power during invocation (<s>āvāhana</s>) and dismissal (<s>visarjana</s>) [of the deity].
'From the crown, the <s>Vijaya</s> Tantra; from the forehead, the <s>Pārameśvara</s>;
from the mouth of <s>Maheśa</s>, the <s>Mukhabimbaka</s>.' || And so on.

body.text:
niṣkalasya tvavayavavibhāgābhāvādetāḥ śrutayo 'nupapannāḥ syuriti|
evametatprakaraṇaṃ dhyeyākāraniṣṭhatvena buddhyākāraniṣṭhatvena ca vyākhyeyam|
na tu baindavaśarīrapratipādakatvena tasya bhagavatyasambhavāt|
śarīraṃ hi yadacetanamapi vyavadhānena jñānakriyāśaktyabhivyañjakaṃ tadasmadāderityucyate|
vidyāvidyeśānāṃ tu kriyāśaktyabhivyañjakameva teṣāṃ sarvajñatvādbhagavatastvabhivyaktasarvaśaktitvānna kathañcittadupapadyata ityadhiṣṭhānamātreṇa tu śarīratve sarvaṃ sarvasya śarīraṃ syādityanavasthā|
tasmātpūrvaiva vyākhyā yukteti|
evaṃ sakalaviṣayamapi dūṣaṇaṃ parihṛtyādhunā sakalaniṣkalaviṣayaṃ parihriyate
body.translated_text: But for the partless one, since there is no division into limbs, these scriptures would be untenable. Thus this entire chapter should be explained as pertaining to the meditation-form body and to the form existing in the intellect—not as establishing a <s>baindava</s>-body (body of light-drops), since that is impossible for the Lord. For a body—even though non-conscious—which, through mediation, manifests the powers of knowledge and action, is said to belong to beings like us. But for the <s>Vidyeśvaras</s> and <s>Īśānas</s>, it only manifests the power of action, since they are already omniscient. And for the Lord, who has all powers already manifest, [a body] is never appropriate in any way. But if mere governance were sufficient for body-hood, then everything would be the body of everything—resulting in an infinite regress. Therefore, the former interpretation alone is proper. Having thus resolved the objection concerning the <s>sakala</s> [form], the [objection] concerning the <s>sakalaniṣkala</s> [form] is now resolved:

children.translated_text: The other deity (<s>deva</s>) who possesses the dual nature
is declared to be not [truly] partless (<s>niṣkala</s>);
in comparison to the great body [of <s>Īśvara</s>],
he is remembered as being without <s>kalās</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yastvābhyāṃ niṣkaleśvarābhyāmanyastṛtīyo devaḥ sadāśivabhaṭṭārakaḥsa
dvisvabhāvagatatayā sakalaniṣkalatvenāpekṣābhedātkevalamasmābhiḥ prokta eva| na tu viruddhasvabhāvo 'bhyupagataḥ|
śivāpekṣayā hyasāvudyuktaśaktyavasthātmakatvāda niṣkalaḥ sakala ityucyate|
īśvaraśarīraṃ tu pravṛttakriyātmakatvena bṛhaditi sthūlataramapekṣya niṣkala ityavirodhaḥ|
tataśca na niṣkalavadatrājñeyatva doṣaḥ prāgukta ucyate|
body.translated_text: Commentary: The third deity, other than these two [i.e., the partless <s>Śiva</s> and the <s>Īśvara</s>]—the lord <s>Sadāśiva</s>—has merely been declared by us as having a dual nature, as <s>sakalaniṣkala</s>, due to the difference in perspective. He has not been accepted as having contradictory natures. For in comparison to <s>Śiva</s>, he is called <s>sakala</s> (not partless) because his state consists of prepared power. But in comparison to the body of <s>Īśvara</s>, which consists of engaged action and is therefore 'great' (grosser), he is [called] <s>niṣkala</s> (partless)—thus there is no contradiction. And therefore, the previously stated fault of unknowability, as in the case of the [truly] partless, does not apply here.

children.translated_text: Thus the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) stands directly
as the cause of <s>yoga</s> for <s>yogins</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ dhyeyākāraśarīrayogeneśvaraḥ sadāśivaśca sākṣādākāravattvena cittaviṣayatvādyogādikāraṇaṃ samupapadyate|
tadevam|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Thus <s>Īśvara</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>, through the connection with a meditation-form body, are directly established as the cause of <s>yoga</s> and the like, since they are objects of the mind by virtue of possessing form. And thus—

children.translated_text: Without a target [of meditation], <s>yoga</s> [is not possible],
nor [the meditation on] the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel), nor concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>).
But for the sake of gracing souls,
even the Supreme assumes the state of the lower.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yato niṣkale lakṣyabhūtasyākārasyābhāvānna yogo jñānaṃ vopapadyate|
nāpi madhyanāḍyādinā yogaprakaraṇavakṣyamāṇanayena gamāgamādi vyāpake tadanupapatteḥ|
nāpi deśabandhaścittasya dhāraṇeti tataḥ samastapuruṣānugrahānupapattirityālocya bhagavānniṣkalo 'pi dhyeyākāraśarīreṇāparatāṃ śarīritvaṃ gata iti tathātve prayojanamapyatroktamiti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because for the partless one, since there is no form to serve as a target [of meditation], <s>yoga</s> and knowledge are not possible. Nor [can there be] movement through the central <s>nāḍī</s> and the like, according to the method to be described in the section on <s>yoga</s>, since that is impossible for the all-pervading one. Nor can there be concentration (<s>dhāraṇā</s>)—the fixing of the mind on a [specific] place. Therefore, reflecting that grace for all souls would be impossible [without form], the Lord, though partless, has assumed the lower state—embodiment—through the meditation-form body. Thus the purpose for this [assumption of form] has also been stated here.

body.text: na kevalamanenaiva sadāśivādyātmanā dhyeyaśarīrabhedenāparatāṃ gato yāvatsvavācakamantrāvasthābhedena mantrāntaravācyavācakabhedena cetyucyate|
body.translated_text: Not only through this [meditation-form body] as <s>Sadāśiva</s> and the rest has he assumed the lower state, but also through the differentiation of states as his own designating <s>mantras</s>, and through the differentiation of word and meaning belonging to other <s>mantras</s>—so it is stated:

children.translated_text: Encompassing <s>nāda</s> (resonance), <s>bindu</s> (point), <s>kha</s> (space), <s>mantra</s>, <s>aṇu</s> (atom),
<s>śakti</s> (power), <s>bīja</s> (seed), and <s>kalā</s> (part)—

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatra nādaḥ kuṇḍalinyabhidhānāyāḥ parasyā vākcchakteravyaktaśabdātmakaḥ prathamaḥ kṣobhaḥ|
binduśca tasyaiveṣatsthūlatāntaḥsaṃjalpātmakatvam|
khaṃ cātra paramākāśaṃ mahāmāyaiva sarvapuruṣasaṃyuktā śaktistata eva nādātmanaḥ śabdasyodayādisaṃvedanāt| proktaṃ ca śrīmatkālottare
body.translated_text: Commentary: There, <s>nāda</s> (resonance) is the first vibration, of the nature of unarticulated sound, of the supreme speech-power called <s>Kuṇḍalinī</s>. And <s>bindu</s> (point) is its slightly grosser form, of the nature of internal murmuring. And <s>kha</s> (space) here is the supreme space — <s>Mahāmāyā</s> itself, the power conjoined with all souls — because from that very [source] arises the awareness of sound in the form of <s>nāda</s>. And it has been declared in the glorious <s>Kālottara</s>:
'From cowherds, their women, children, foreigners, and speakers of vernacular tongues,

body.text: antarjalagatāḥ sattvāste 'pi nityaṃ bruvanti tam|| iti
body.translated_text: and creatures beneath the water — even they always utter it.'
That very [level of speech] is [called] <s>Paśyantī</s> (the 'seeing' level) — [so say] those who follow other <s>āgamas</s>. As they say:
'<s>Paśyantī</s>, because of non-differentiation, has all sequence withdrawn everywhere;

body.text: avibhāgāttu\devdot vāganapāyinī Quoted thus ad \Mat\VP\ 7:45--6, p.247 and \Sar\ 1:8, p.16. Bhatt observes that it is cited in the supposed auto-commentary on the \Vakya\ (ad 1:143). Rau includes the verse (with avibhāgā tu) in small type as \Vakya\ 1:166. Cf.\ also \Rat\ 75c--76d: avibhāgena varṇānāṃ sarvataḥ saṃhṛtikramāt| svayaṃprakāśā paśyantī māyūrāṇḍarasopamā| svarūpajyotirevāntaḥ sūkṣmā vāganapāyinī

body.translated_text: it is inner light of its own nature, subtle, imperishable speech.'

body.text:
mantraśca sthūlaśabdaḥ parameśvarābhidhāyako 'tra vyomavyāpyādika ityevamavasthābhedena catvāri sthānāni vācaḥ proktāni|
śrutirapyāha
body.translated_text: And <s>mantra</s> [here refers to] gross articulated sound that designates the Supreme Lord — such as <s>Vyomavyāpin</s> and the like. Thus, through the distinction of levels, four stations of speech have been declared. Scripture too says:

body.text: catvāri vākparimitā padāni tāni vidurbrāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ|
body.translated_text: 'Speech has been measured into four levels; those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are wise know them.

body.text: guhā trīṇi nihitā neṅgayanti turīyaṃ vāco manuṣyā vadanti||
body.translated_text: Three are hidden, deposited in the cave; they do not stir. Humans speak the fourth [level] of speech.'

body.text: śrīmatkālottare tu bindunādayordvayorapi sūkṣmatayā viśeṣābhāvāttrīṇi rūpāṇyasyāḥ
body.translated_text: But in the glorious <s>Kālottara</s>, because of the subtlety of both <s>bindu</s> and <s>nāda</s> and hence the absence of distinction between them, three forms of speech [are given]:

body.text: sthūlaṃ śabda iti proktaṃ sūkṣmaṃ cintāmayaṃ bhavet|
body.translated_text: 'The gross is declared to be [audible] sound; the subtle is said to be of the nature of thought;

body.text: cintayā rahitaṃ yacca tatparaṃ parikīrtitam|| iti|
body.translated_text: and that which is free from thought is called the supreme.'
In another <s>āgama</s> too, three levels of speech are stated:
'The sounding, the one born without sound, and the soundless — these operate;
and between the sounding and the soundless, the soundless is the weightier.'

body.text: kevalamātmasamavetā evaikāntatastairiṣyante| asmābhistu tasyāpariṇāmitvātparigrahavartinya iti darśitaṃ nādasiddhau|
body.translated_text: The only [difference is that] they consider [these levels] to be exclusively inherent in the Self. But we have demonstrated in the <s>Nādasiddhi</s> that, because of the Self's immutability, they belong to [the Self's] accessories.

body.text: arke cenmadhu vindeta kimarthaṃ parvataṃ vrajet|
body.translated_text: 'If one could find honey in a tree, why would one climb a mountain?

body.text: arke cenmadhu\devdot yatnamācaret Source unknown. Quoted (variously with akke cen and atraiva) ad \Moksa\ 153--4; \Sar\ 8:12, p.69 and in the
1.2.1.4, p.11, where the first word is indisputably arke.

body.translated_text: When the desired object is attained, what wise person would exert further effort?'
Here is an illustration:

children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s>, knowing [what constitutes] benefit,
being omniscient, grants [appropriate] fruits.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
sa hyupakārakebhyaḥ svalpamahadupakārāpekṣayā tathārūpameva phalaṃ dadaddṛṣṭo yataḥ| tadevaṃ
body.translated_text: Commentary: For he is observed granting fruit of exactly the kind [appropriate to the] benefit — in accordance with whether the benefit [received] is small or great — to those who have rendered [him] service. Thus,

children.translated_text: because of being the agent of grace through [His] will,
He has authority over dissolution and enjoyment.
He is shown to be threefold by the distinction of functions,
and by the distinction of names.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
dhyeyākāraśarīrabhedabhinno 'pi bhagavānparamārthata icchāmātreṇānugrahādikartṛtvādeva prāguktanayataḥ kṛtyabhedena vibhinno layabhogādhikāravān bhinna ityucyate|
sarvajñatvasyābheda iti yāvat|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Although the Lord is undifferentiated in ultimate reality [regardless of differences in] the bodies [assumed for] meditation-forms, because of being the agent of grace and the like through mere will alone, by the previously stated principle, He is said to be differentiated by the distinction of functions, and differentiated [as] having authority over dissolution and enjoyment. [He is undifferentiated] in omniscience — that is [the limit of the differentiation].
Now, after the examination of the category of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), [comes] the examination of the category of deliberation (<s>vicāra</s>).

children.translated_text: The Lord impels the lords
of the <s>vidyās</s> (mantric knowledge-systems) that are below [Him].

body.text: Testimonium: \Narayana\ quotes this unit exactly as constituted ad \Mrg\ 13:160, p.133.

children.translated_text: Being merely impelled by Him, they
create the world below.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
prakṛtatvātpatibhyo 'dhastiṣṭhantīti adhaḥsthā vidyāḥ saptakoṭisaṃkhyātā mantrāsteṣāṃ ye patayo 'nantādayo vakṣyamāṇāstānprerayati|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Because [the <s>vidyās</s>] are the subject under discussion — 'standing below the lords' means the <s>vidyās</s>, [which are] <s>mantras</s> numbering seven crores; [He impels] those who are their lords — <s>Ananta</s> and the others who will be described.

body.text: anantādayo vakṣyamāṇāḥ See \Kir\ 3:26c--27 and commentary and Chapter 4 passim.

body.translated_text: If so, who creates the world above? It is said:

children.translated_text: In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is the creator;
<s>Ananta</s> is declared to be the lord in the impure [path].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śuddhe vidyātattvabhuvanādyātmake mantramantreśādhvani śivaḥ kartā|
tatkṛtāste tadbhuvanādikaṃ ca samastamityarthaḥ|
ananto 'nantādirityarthaḥ| anantādiko vargo 'site māyāvartmani prabhuḥ sthityādikarteti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: In the pure path — consisting of the <s>Vidyā</s>-tattva, worlds, and the like — the path of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mantreśas</s> (lords of mantras) — <s>Śiva</s> is the creator. They [the mantras, mantreśas] are created by Him, along with all their worlds and the like — this is the meaning. <s>Ananta</s> means <s>Ananta</s> and the others — this is the meaning. The group [beginning with] <s>Ananta</s> is the lord in the impure path, the path of <s>Māyā</s> — [they are] the agents of maintenance and the like.

body.text: atha śuddha ivāśuddhe 'pi kathaṃ na sa eva prabhuriti| ucyate|
body.translated_text: Now, [the question arises:] why is He not the lord in the impure [path] just as in the pure? It is said:

children.translated_text: Just as [a king, though] of equal sovereignty,
[rules] through one appointed over a portion of the territory,
so does He accomplish everything,
being awakened by His (<s>Śiva</s>'s) power.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
dṛṣṭavadadṛṣṭakalpanā| yathā bhūmaṇḍaleśo 'tra nṛpatirantaraṅgamamātyapurohitādiprakṛtivargaṃ svayameva kurvandṛśyate bahiraṅgamātmakalpāmātyādipreraṇenaivetyevamatrāpi śruteravirodhaḥ|
tacchaktipratibodhita ityanena vijñānakevalinaḥ sato 'nantādivargasyānugraha iti| apratibuddho hi pratibodhyate|
taccāpratibuddhatvaṃ malata evoktaṃ yataḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: The unseen is conceived by analogy with the seen. Just as a king over a portion of the territory is seen to directly manage his inner circle — the group of ministers, priests, and the like — while [managing] the outer [realm] through the impelling of ministers and the like who are like himself, so too here [the analogy holds] without contradiction with scripture. By [the phrase] 'awakened by His power,' [it is indicated that] the group [beginning with] <s>Ananta</s>, being <s>vijñānakevalins</s> (souls with knowledge alone), receives grace. For the unawakened is awakened. And that unawakened state is said to be due to <s>mala</s> (impurity), since:

body.text: malata evoktaṃ yataḥ e.g.\ \Kir\ 2:14d and commentary thereon.

body.translated_text: Now, the nature of <s>Ananta</s> and the others:

children.translated_text: Omniscient, with a pure body,
the illuminator of all knowledge.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
īśvarādayaṃ kartṛtvenaiva kalayā nyūno, na tu jñatvenāpītyarthaḥ|
śuddhadehaśca na māyāgarbhādhikārivadaśuddhadehaḥ|
sarveṣāṃ ca daśāṣṭādaśabhedabhinnānāṃ śivajñānānāmupadeṣṭṛtvena sthitaḥ, na tu gurvantaravatkatipayānāmiti||
body.translated_text: Commentary: From the Lord [<s>Īśvara</s>], this one [<s>Ananta</s>] is inferior only in agency (<s>kartṛtva</s>), not in knowledge (<s>jñatva</s>) — this is the meaning. And [he has] a pure body — not an impure body like those who have authority within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>. And he stands as the teacher of all the <s>Śiva</s>-knowledges, divided into ten and eighteen varieties — not [the teacher] of only a few, like other teachers.
Colophon: Thus ends the third chapter in the commentary (<s>vṛtti</s>) on the glorious <s>Kiraṇa</s>, composed by <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, son of <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>.
CHAPTER 4
Now, for the purpose of a detailed examination of the category of deliberation (<s>vicāra</s>), a new chapter preceded by questions [begins].

children.translated_text: Through the power of <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>śakti</s> (energy),
indeed, <s>Ananta</s> is awakened.
And that power which awakens
is described as all-pervading.
Even though it is proximate to others,
does it not awaken them too?
If [it awakens only] the qualified, then [it shows] partiality —
in that case, <s>Śiva</s> would be possessed of <s>rāga</s> (attachment).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atra ca sūtrapadārthaprakaraṇasambandhāḥ prāgvadeva draṣṭavyāḥ|
pāṭalikastu vicārapadārthasyaivānantaraṃ viśeṣaparīkṣātmakaḥ|
vākyātmakastu prokto 'nanto 'site prabhurityādibhiranekavidhaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Here, the connections of sūtra, subject matter, and chapter are to be understood as before. The section-marker (<s>pāṭalika</s>) indicates [this chapter] as a specific examination immediately following the category of deliberation. The sentence-form is the multi-faceted [exposition beginning with] 'In the pure [path], <s>Śiva</s> is the creator, <s>Ananta</s> is declared to be the lord in the impure [path]' and so on.

body.text:
tataśceśvaraśaktervyāpakatvena sarvatra sannihitatvato viśeṣābhāvāt sarveṣāmātmanāmanantādirūpatā syāt na vā kasyacidapi|
sevanādiyogyatāpekṣayā tatkaraṇe ca tasya rāgadveṣādiyogāt puruṣavadanīśvaratvaprasaṅga iti|
body.translated_text: And since the Lord's <s>śakti</s>, being pervasive, is present everywhere without distinction, either all souls would have the status of <s>Ananta</s> and the others, or none would. And since, in conferring [grace] with regard to qualification through worship and the like, He would have attachment, aversion, and the like, the consequence of non-lordship — like an [ordinary] person — would follow.
Here is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: Just as through the contact with the sun's rays
the awakening of lotuses is not uniform —
some awaken,
while others never [awaken] —
and there is no attachment or aversion in the sun,
likewise there is none in the Lord; because
His engagement [arises] from qualification;
without engagement, there is no [such] state.
Through that capacity,
the omniscience of <s>Ananta</s> is established, O <s>Khaga</s> (Sky-goer).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
satyam| vyāpikā śaktiryogyatāpekṣayā cānugrāhikā|
na ca tayā rāgadveṣānumānam|
tathābhūtāyāstasyā atrāsiddhatvādyato 'dhikāriṇāmadhikāro malasya pakvatvamatra yogyatā|
pakvamalānāṃ sā bodhapradetyucyate|
yathā savitrā pratibodhayogyaṃ pratibodhyate|
tasmādadhikārādyogyatālakṣaṇādanantasya niyogastanniyogaṃ vinā bahiraṅgakāryasya na vyavasthānamupapadyata ityuktaṃ yataḥ|
na ca tathābhūtasya yogyatānusaraṇasya rāgadveṣādyavinābhāvaḥ siddha iti na tato 'trānīśvaratvaprasaṅgaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: True — the <s>śakti</s> is all-pervading and confers grace with regard to qualification. But attachment and aversion are not to be inferred from it, because [a śakti] of such a nature is not established here [as the cause of partiality]. For the qualification of those who are qualified — the maturation of <s>mala</s> — is [what constitutes] the qualification here. It is said that [the <s>śakti</s>] bestows awakening upon those whose <s>mala</s> has matured — just as the sun awakens [only] those capable of being awakened. Therefore, from qualification characterized by eligibility, <s>Ananta</s>'s engagement [arises]; without that engagement, the organization of external effects is not possible — this is stated. And it is not established that the pursuit of qualification of such a nature is invariably accompanied by attachment, aversion, and the like — therefore, there is no consequence of non-lordship here.
Now, a question for the purpose of another examination within this very [context]:

children.translated_text: Omniscience, when a body exists,
is not possible for <s>Ananta</s>,
because the senses are limited
and have limited grasping capacity.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaduktaṃ sarvajñaḥ śuddhadehaścānanta ityetannopapadyate|
yataḥ prāguktanayena pratiniyatakāryakaraṇātmakaśarīrayogaḥ pratiniyatagrāhakatvena vyāptaḥ sarvaśarīrigatatayā siddhaḥ|
ataḥ śarīritvena viruddhavyāpyopalabdhyā sarvajñatvaniṣedhaḥ kriyata ityarthaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: What was said — that <s>Ananta</s> is omniscient and has a pure body — that is not possible. Because, by the previously stated principle, the connection with a body consisting of particular effects and instruments is pervaded by particular grasping capacity — this is established through [its universal] presence in all embodied beings. Therefore, through the perception of a pervaded property that contradicts [omniscience] — namely, embodiment — the denial of omniscience is made — this is the meaning.

Objection: this reason is unestablished, because the effects and instruments [in <s>Ananta</s>'s case] are different, since <s>Ananta</s> has been described as having a pure body. To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: That body is composed of <s>Māyā</s>,
born from residual <s>karma</s>.
Even if there were a distinction,
it would [only] be [something] like hearing from afar and the like.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
na tāvadamāyātmakatvamakarmajatvaṃ vā taccharīrasya śuddhatvaṃ saṃbhavati śarīratvādasmadādiśarīravaditi| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: First, the purity of that body cannot consist in its not being composed of <s>Māyā</s> or not being born from <s>karma</s> — because of its being a body, like our own bodies. As they say:

body.text: māyordhvaṃ dehasadbhāva iti vārtaiva bhadrikā| iti|
body.translated_text: 'The existence of a body above <s>Māyā</s> — that is just a nice story.'

body.text: māyordhvaṃ dehasadbhāva iti vārtaiva bhadrikā Source unknown. Cf.\ verses with the same concluding formula in

\crux yadi paraṃ brahmādiśarīrasyeva viśiṣṭakarmajatvameva tato 'sya vācyam\crux |
tataśca tathābhūtaśarīrayogāttasya tadvadeva sudūraśravaṇādika eva viśeṣaḥ sidhyatīti| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: \crux If, however, like <s>Brahmā</s>'s body, it is born from distinguished <s>karma</s>, then that must be stated\crux. And in that case, through the connection with such a body, only a distinction like hearing from afar would be established for him — as it is for [<s>Brahmā</s>]. As they say:

body.text: yo yatrātiśayo dṛṣṭaḥ sa evānyatra laṅghanāt| iti|
body.translated_text: 'Whatever extraordinary [capacity] is seen in one case, the same [applies] elsewhere through inference.'

body.text: yo yatrātiśayo dṛṣṭaḥ sa evānyatra laṅghanāt Source unknown.
na tu sarvajñatvamato nāyamasiddho heturiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: But not omniscience — therefore this is not an unestablished reason. This is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>).
Here is the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: His body is said to be
born from a pure source, not from <s>karma</s>.
Since he is thus free from bonds (<s>pāśa</s>),
by what is his knowledge obstructed?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śarīrasya māyātmakatveneha vyāptirasiddhā, śuddhavidyātmano 'pi sambhavādityuktaṃ śuddhe 'dhvani śivaḥ kartā ityādinā|
body.translated_text: Commentary: The pervasion [that 'all bodies are composed of <s>Māyā</s>'] is not established here, because [a body] of the nature of pure <s>Vidyā</s> is also possible — as stated by 'In the pure path, <s>Śiva</s> is the creator' and so forth.

children.translated_text: Just as the poison residing in a serpent
does not afflict [the serpent] in which it resides,
so too, the collection of bonds
residing in him does not afflict <s>Ananta</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hi viṣasraṣṭuḥ sarpasya śarīrasthamapi viṣaṃ
sarpāntarādvā pratisaṃkrāntaṃ tanna viṣatayā bādhakaṃ tathānantasya
\crux tatsthānasādhakagataḥ śarīrādijanakatvākṣiptaśuddhavidyākartṛtvāttadātmakaḥ\crux\ pāśasañcayaḥ śarīrātmako na bādhaka iti|
evaṃ māyā garbhādhikāriṇo 'pi vīrabhadrādayo na māyāpāśasañcayena bādhyanta ityuktaṃ bhavati|
taduktaṃ gurubhiḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: For just as the poison residing in the body of a serpent — the creator of poison — or even transferred from another serpent, does not afflict [that serpent] as poison, so too for <s>Ananta</s>, \crux the collection of bonds, being of the nature of the body [produced by] pure <s>Vidyā</s> and the agency implied by its being the creator of bodies and the like — [that collection]\crux consisting of the body does not afflict. Thus it is also stated that <s>Vīrabhadra</s> and the others, who have authority within the womb of <s>Māyā</s>, are not afflicted by the collection of <s>Māyā</s>-bonds. As the teachers have said:
'Even in connection with <s>kalā</s>, they are not subject to [the power of] <s>kalās</s>, as the groups of bound souls (<s>paśus</s>) are;

body.text: kālayoge 'pi\devdot taduparyataḥ \Moksa\ 82c--83b. Also quoted ad \Nar\ 2:8, p.133.
vaśyāstāḥ paśubhiḥ sārdhaṃ teṣāṃ te taduparyataḥ| iti|
body.translated_text: those [<s>kalās</s>] are subject to them, along with the bound souls — for they [the mantreśas] are above those [<s>kalās</s>].'

body.text: yadyevaṃ pāśāntaravacchuddhavidyāpi pāśatvenānantasya bhagavato vicchinneti kathaṃ tato 'yaṃ śarīrātmakaḥ pāśasañcaya iti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: If so, then just like another bond, pure <s>Vidyā</s> too, being a bond, would be separated from the Lord <s>Ananta</s> — so how is this collection of bonds of the nature of the body? To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: Just as [a creeper] that has been cut [but] grows again from the cut,
through dependence on a particular location, would [grow again],
so too, by virtue of [his] station, in the lord of <s>mantras</s>,
body-bearing [occurs] forcefully.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā chinnodbhavā gaḍūcī mūlato vicchinnāpi sthānaviśeṣamāśrayamāśritya punaḥ prarohaṃ yāti|
evaṃ śuddhavidyāpi chinnāpi anantasya tadadhikāritvalakṣaṇaṃ sthānaviśeṣamāśritya taccharīrādyātmanā punaḥ prarohamāyātītyadhikārasāmarthyādananteśasyānicchato 'pi balādiva śarīradhāraṇamityavirodhaḥ|
yadapi taccharīrasya karmajatve 'numānamuktaṃ tadapyanaikāntikamityucyate|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as the <s>gaḍūcī</s> creeper (<s>Tinospora cordifolia</s>), even though cut from the root, resorts to a particular location as its support and sprouts again, so too pure <s>Vidyā</s>, even though cut, resorts to the particular station characterized as <s>Ananta</s>'s authority, and sprouts again in the form of that body and the like. Therefore, through the power of [his] authority, even the unwilling Lord <s>Ananta</s> bears a body as if by force — thus there is no contradiction. And as for the inference stated [by the opponent] that that body is born from <s>karma</s> — that too is said to be inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>):

children.translated_text: Just as a body sustained by <s>mantra</s>-power
endures for a long time,
and [one] attains the desired station
even though bitten by death (<s>kāla</s>), through [that] power —
so too, through the capacity of His power,
that body of his exists.
Therefore, his body should be known as utterly pure,
like a lotus leaf [untouched by water].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
maraṇakāla eva yo daṣṭaḥ sarpeṇa sa kāladaṣṭaḥ kṣīṇakarmetyarthaḥ|
tasya yathā mantraśaktyaiva dhṛto dehaściraṃ tiṣṭhatyabhīpsitañca sthānaṃ prāpnoti prāguktasyaiva puṃsaḥ śaktyā jñānakriyātmikayā tatheśvaraśaktisāmarthyādadhikārākhyādananteśasya śarīramakarmajameveti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: One who is bitten by a snake at the very time of death is 'bitten by <s>kāla</s>' — meaning one whose <s>karma</s> has been exhausted. Just as his body, sustained solely by <s>mantra</s>-power, endures for a long time and attains the desired station — through the power of the very soul mentioned before, [whose power is] of the nature of knowledge and action — so too, through the capacity of the Lord's power, characterized as [<s>Ananta</s>'s] authority, <s>Ananta</s>'s body is indeed not born from <s>karma</s>.
'Therefore, by that reasoning as well, known as untouched
by the defects (<s>malas</s>) characterized by <s>karma</s> and <s>Māyā</s> — like a lotus leaf by water.'

body.text:
asmadādīnāmapi keṣāñcidakarmajadehadarśanāccharīratvādityasya hetoratrānaikāntikatvamityuktaṃ bhavati|
nanu bodhāyatanaṃ śarīramasmadādīnāmiva tasyeti kimucyate haṭhavattanudhāraṇamiti tadarthametat|
body.translated_text: Since even for beings like us, some are observed to have bodies not born from <s>karma</s>, the reason 'because of being a body' is said to be inconclusive here. Objection: since the body is the basis of awareness for him as for us, why is it said that body-bearing [occurs] 'forcefully'? For this purpose, [the following is stated]:

children.translated_text: A <s>rasa</s> (mercury), [which is] inherently unstable,
residing in a body, [when] aided by chemical processes (<s>tantras</s>),
remains in this body;
likewise, awakening (<s>bodha</s>), of great power.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā kalane gatau sādhuḥ kalyo 'tyantānavasthitaḥ śarīre rasaḥ pārataḥ sa eva tantraistatkuṭumbadhāraṇādibhirdravyāntarairupakṛtaḥ
body.translated_text: Commentary: Just as a <s>rasa</s> — mercury (<s>pārata</s>) — which is inherently extremely unstable (<s>kalya</s>), meaning disposed to movement — that very [mercury], when aided by processes (<s>tantras</s>) such as the maintenance of its household [i.e., chemical fixation agents] and other substances,

children.translated_text: Just as through the power of medicine,
the supreme strength of the powerless
arises through that power's capacity,
so the strength of <s>Ananta</s> in the supreme [<s>Śiva</s>-principle]
through that conjunction of capacity
impels the womb (<s>yoni</s>) in an instant.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
aśaktānāṃ yathauṣadhādisāmarthyācchaktirupacayaṃ yāti|
evaṃ tasya śarīrasya yā śaktiḥ tayā yatsāmarthyaṃ kartṛtvasamarthanaṃ tasmādananteśasya parasmiñchivatattve balaṃ saṃskāryasaṃyojanādyātmakaṃ yātīti|
ayamarthaḥ---sarvajñatve 'pi tasya śivātkalayā kartṛtvanyūnatvenātra saṃskāryasaṃyojanādivyāpārānupapatteravaśyaṃ tāvato 'pi kartṛtvāṃśasyābhivyañjanāyāsmadāderiva śarīramupayujyata ityadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as the power of the powerless attains increase through the capacity of medicines and the like, so through the power (<s>śakti</s>) of that body — by which capacity [means] the enabling of agency — from that, the strength of <s>Ananta-Īśa</s> in the supreme <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, consisting of the conjunction with the purifiable and the like, arises. The meaning is this: even though he possesses omniscience, since his agency is diminished relative to <s>Śiva</s> by a degree, the impossibility of activities such as conjunction with the purifiable and the like here [necessitates that] for the manifestation of at least that portion of agency, a body is useful just as for us — therefore there is no fault.
Here, a question for another examination:

children.translated_text: If [<s>Ananta</s>] is the impeller on the lower path,
what is the role of <s>Māyā</s>'s impeller?
By its own transformation,
is it transformative in this world?
Since [<s>Māyā</s>] is declared to be the womb of the world,
<s>kalā</s> and the rest are its transformations.
From transformation, there would be total destruction;
how then is transformation not [the destruction of] the world?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
nanu cāyaṃ praśno 'nupapannaḥ pūrvameveśvarasiddhau nyāyanirākṛtatvātsamādhirapi prāgukta eva yataḥ| yaduktaṃ karma cenna hyacetanamiti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Now this question is inappropriate, since it was already refuted by reasoning in the prior establishment of <s>Īśvara</s>; the resolution too has already been stated, because it was said: 'And if [you say it is] <s>karma</s>, [we reply:] no, for the unconscious [cannot act independently].'
Here the established conclusion:

children.translated_text: Being unconscious, she [<s>Māyā</s>] is to be impelled,
with the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) as the cause.
There is no transformation by herself; therefore
<s>Ananta</s> is her impeller.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
mahāpralaye 'pi puruṣārthatayā kalādivyaktyanuguṇena sūkṣmasūkṣmatarādyavasthābhedena bhagavataḥ sākṣātpreryaiva|
tadānīmapīśvarādyavasthānupasaṃhārānna pūrvaḥ prasaṅga ityarthaḥ|
yaduktaṃ śrīmanmṛgendre
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even in the great dissolution (<s>mahāpralaya</s>), for the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s>, she is directly impelled by the Lord in various states of subtlety — subtle, subtler, and so forth — corresponding to the manifestation of <s>kalā</s> and the rest. Even then, since the Lord's state is not withdrawn, the previous objection does not arise — this is the meaning. As stated in the venerable <s>Mṛgendra</s>:
'Even in sleep, he remains — awakening those fit to be awakened, restraining those to be restrained, ripening the <s>karma</s> of the active ones,
manifesting the <s>Māyā</s>-powers fit for manifestation, seeing everything, all objects as they are.' Thus.

body.text: svāpe 'pyāste\devdot vastujātam \Mrg\VP\ 4:15. Also quoted ad \Nar\ 2:31, p.153.

mahāpralayaśca bahiraṅgakalādikāryopasaṃhāraḥ|
tatraiva cānantādeḥ kartṛtvamityuktaṃ yataḥ|
nāpi dvitīyaprasaṅga ityucyate
body.translated_text: And the great dissolution is the withdrawal of the external effects of <s>kalā</s> and the rest. And there too the agency of <s>Ananta</s> and the rest has been stated, because. Nor does the second objection arise — it is said:

children.translated_text: Just as the ocean, by the force of wind,
undergoes transformation only on its surface,
so <s>Māyā</s>, being unshakeable [in its totality],
is [only partly] transformed through <s>kalā</s> and the rest.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hyudadhiḥ parimitābhiḥ śaktibhistaraṅgātmakaṃ vikāramanubhavati na sarvābhirevaṃ śaktisamāhārātmakatvānmāyāyāḥ katipayābhireva śaktibhiḥ sā kalādivikāramanubhavati na sarvābhistena rūpeṇākṣobhyatvāditi|
atra parābhiprāyaḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as the ocean undergoes transformation in the form of waves through limited powers, not through all [its powers], so because <s>Māyā</s> is of the nature of an aggregate of powers, she undergoes transformation of <s>kalā</s> and the rest through only some powers, not all — therefore she is unshakeable in that form. Here the opposing view:

children.translated_text: If that which is unshaken is not the agent of effects —

body.text:
Vṛtti:
vikṛtānāmapyavikṛtānāmiva śaktīnāṃ tatsahabhāvitvādakṣobhe tāsāmapi vikārānupapatteḥ kāryānupapattirityavaśyaṃ sarvaiva kṣubdhābhyupagantavyetyakṣobhyatvādityayaṃ heturatrāsiddha iti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Since even the transformed powers coexist with the untransformed ones, when there is no agitation of those [untransformed powers], there is impossibility of transformation of those too, and hence impossibility of effects — therefore all [powers] must necessarily be admitted as agitated. Hence 'because of unshakeability' — this reason is unestablished here.
Here the established conclusion:

children.translated_text: Her agitation would be that [Lord's] impulsion;
that power, impelled by him,
would eternally be the performer of effects.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ayaṃ sāmānyakṣobhaḥ sarvaśaktiviṣayaḥ preraṇātmakastasyā abhyupagamyata eva|
kāryātmakastu viśeṣakṣobhaḥ kasyāścideva śakteriti|
evañca nātrāsiddhatetyucyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: This general agitation, pertaining to all powers and of the nature of impulsion, is indeed accepted for her. But the specific agitation that constitutes effects belongs to only some power. And thus it is said that there is no unestablishment here:

children.translated_text: She is declared unshakeable due to her all-pervasiveness,
abiding as the cause of the world.
Just as <s>Māyā</s>, being superior, pervading
[all], that group of effects is not [equal to her] in extent;
pervading the entities — <s>kalā</s> and the rest —
she abides [and is] therefore called unshakeable.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
vibhutvena sarvaśaktyātmanā na kāryatayā kṣobhyata ityakṣobhyatvenoktā bhavati|
jagatkāraṇātmanānumīyate| tena rūpeṇākṣobhyaiva yato bhavantīti bhāvāstatkāryātmakāḥ kalādayaḥ tānvyāpya sthitā| ghṛtakīṭanyāyena tadgarbha eva teṣāmutpattirityarthaḥ na tu tadbhāvabhāvitvāt|
ghaṭādeḥ kāryasya mṛdādidravyameva kāraṇaṃ loke dṛṣṭaṃ na tu tacchaktiḥ|
tatkimucyate śaktiḥ kāryakarīti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: She is declared unshakeable because she is not agitated as an effect in her entirety as all powers. She is inferred as the cause of the world. In that form she is indeed unshakeable, since the entities that are her effects — <s>kalā</s> and the rest — arise within her very womb while she pervades them — by the analogy of insects in ghee — this is the meaning. Not because their existence depends on her existence. In the world, it is the material substance like clay that is seen as the cause of effects like pots, not its power. So why is it said that the power is the performer of effects? To this it is replied:

children.translated_text: The power that performs those effects
is called <s>kriyā</s> (action), of subtle form;
though subtle, it abides in gross effects
like the seed of a banyan tree.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
loke 'pi nyagrodhabījavat sūkṣmāpi śaktistasya sthūlasya kāryasya kārikā pariṇatiśabdavācyā nityānumeyadharmiṇī siddhaiva|
na tu dravyamaśaktyavasthāyāmapi
tasya bhāvāt| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Even in the world, like a banyan seed, although subtle, the power that is the performer of that gross effect — designated by the word 'transformation' — is an eternally inferable property, established indeed. Not the substance, because that [substance] exists even in the state of powerlessness. As they say:
'Power is the causal factor, not the substance, due to deviation [of the invariable concomitance].'

body.text: śaktiḥ kārakaṃ na dravyaṃ vyabhicārāt Source unknown.

nāpi sahakārisannidhānamaśaktasya tatsahakāriyoge 'pi tatkāryādarśanāditi śobhanamuktam śaktiḥ kāryakarīti|
tataḥ prakṛte kimucyate
body.translated_text: Nor is the proximity of auxiliary causes [the factor], because even when there is conjunction of auxiliary causes with the powerless, the effect is not seen. Therefore it is well said that power is the performer of effects. Then what is said regarding the matter at hand:

children.translated_text: Therefore she [<s>Māyā</s>] should be known as the cause
of this gross [world] entirely.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yenaivamanekaśaktirūpāpi māyā na sarvaśaktyātmanā pariṇamata ityuktaṃ
tena kāraṇena sā kācideva śaktirasya sthūlasya kalādeḥ kāryasya sāmastyena kāraṇaṃ proktā|
na tu śaktyantaramiti dvitīyo 'pi prasaṅgo 'nupapanna iti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: By this [argument] — that although <s>Māyā</s> is of the nature of many powers, she does not transform through all powers — it is said that for that reason, only some power is declared as the cause, in its entirety, of this gross effect — <s>kalā</s> and the rest — not another power. Thus the second objection too is untenable.

body.text: atha kiṃ sarvasya jagataḥ sākṣātkāraṇam| netyucyate
body.translated_text: Now, is [<s>Māyā</s>] the direct cause of the entire world? No — it is said:

children.translated_text: From that [<s>Māyā</s>], <s>kalā</s> (activity), <s>tuṭi</s> (time),
<s>saṃsthā</s> (fixed order), <s>bodhinī</s> (awakening [knowledge]), and desire-producer (<s>rāga</s>)
and the subtle — from that, the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); from them,
<s>buddhi</s> (intellect); from <s>buddhi</s>, <s>ahaṃkṛti</s> (ego);
from that, the eleven sense-organs,
and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements);
from them the [gross] elements are born —
the Lord creates all [this] below.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tasmānmāyātattvātkalā tuṭiśca kālaḥ saṃsthā ca prāguktā niyatireva sākṣādutpannāḥ| yaduktaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: From that <s>Māyā-tattva</s>, <s>kalā</s>, <s>tuṭi</s> — that is, <s>kāla</s> (time) — and <s>saṃsthā</s>, previously mentioned as <s>niyati</s> (fixed order) itself, are directly produced. As stated in the venerable <s>Svāyambhuva</s>:
'From that, time and <s>kalā</s>' —

body.text: tasmātkālakale \Svayam\ 2:9a. Cf.\ \Sadyo's interpretation (p.43): kalā ca kalā cetyekaśeṣaḥ| kālaśca kalā ca kālakale| tatraikaḥ kalāśabdo niyatimabhidhatte, dvitīyastu kalāmeva| kathaṃ kalāśabdo niyatimabhidhatte| yataḥ sāpi kalayati prerayatīti niyatiḥ karmaphalabhojakatvena|

kalāśabdena tatra niyaterapyupādānāt| bodhanī tu prāguktā vidyā|
hīti yasmātkāraṇādutpannā tasmādevābhilāṣakṛt prāgukto rāgaḥ|
sūkṣmaṃ ca guṇakāraṇatayā prāguktaṃ pradhānamutpannaṃ tata eva|
prakramāntaranirdeśānna māyātaḥ kintu kāryaprakramātpūrvaśrutāyāḥ kalāta eva| yaduktaṃ śrīmadraurave
body.translated_text: since by the word '<s>kalā</s>' there, <s>niyati</s> too is included. And <s>bodhanī</s> is the previously mentioned <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). 'Hi' [indicates] that from which cause it is produced, from that very [<s>kalā</s>] the desire-producer — the previously mentioned <s>rāga</s> (attachment) — [arises]. And the subtle, previously mentioned as the cause of the <s>guṇas</s> — <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) — is produced from that very [source]. Due to indication by a different sequence, [it is produced] not from <s>Māyā</s> but from <s>kalā</s> itself according to the sequence of effects. As stated in the venerable <s>Raurava</s>:
'From the <s>kalā-tattva</s>, <s>rāga</s> and <s>vidyā</s> — these two <s>tattvas</s> came into being,
and <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest)' — thus.

body.text:
ata iti sūkṣmapadopāttāttattvātpradhānādguṇāḥ sattvādayastrayastebhyo buddhiriti guṇebhyaḥ|
buddhyādeḥ sāmānyaśāstraprasiddhasya tattvādivastunaḥ prakāraviśeṣaparigrahārthamanuvāda iti darśitaṃ prāgeva| proktaṃ ca sāṃkhyaiḥ
body.translated_text: 'From that' — from the <s>tattva</s> taken up by the word 'subtle,' from <s>pradhāna</s>, the three <s>guṇas</s> — <s>sattva</s> and the rest; 'from them, <s>buddhi</s>' — from the <s>guṇas</s>. Since the <s>tattvas</s> from <s>buddhi</s> onward are well-known from general <s>śāstra</s>, it has been shown previously that this is a restatement for the purpose of specifying the particular manner of those <s>tattvas</s> and so on. And it is stated by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>:
'From <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Mahat</s> (the Great); from that, <s>Ahaṃkāra</s> (ego); from that, the group of sixteen;
and from those sixteen, from five [<s>tanmātras</s>], the five elements.' Thus.

body.text: sarvamiti bhūtabhāvabhuvanātmakam| yaccādhaḥ sthūlabhūtamayaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ tadapyasṛjat| tadevaṃ
body.translated_text: 'All' means consisting of elements, states of being, and worlds. And that which is below — the <s>brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg) made of gross elements — that too he created. Thus:

children.translated_text: He, the Lord, the blessed one,
endowed with <s>Śiva-śakti</s> (the power of <s>Śiva</s>),
created the entire effect that is of the nature of <s>Māyā</s>,
mixed of pure and impure.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
pāramparyeṇaitatsarvaṃ māyātaḥ sa evānanteśo 'sṛjat|
tat pratisthānaṃ śuddhaiścāśuddhaiścādhikāribhirvimiśritam|
te 'pi tenaiva nirmitā ityarthaḥ| yaduktaṃ śrīmadraurave
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: All this, in succession, from <s>Māyā</s>, was created by that very <s>Ananta-Īśa</s>. That abode is mixed with pure and impure presiding beings. They too were fashioned by him alone — this is the meaning. As stated in the venerable <s>Raurava</s>:
'The lords beyond impurity and those with impurity, of various kinds,

body.text: patayaścāñjanātītāḥ\devdot vyavasthitāḥ \RauS\ 2:20 (Ed.\ reads vāpi for devās).

body.translated_text: are established in each world by his command.' Thus.

body.text:
svarūpeṇāpi tacchuddhamaśuddhaṃ ca vimiśritaṃ so 'sṛjaditi|
yaduktaṃ sāṃkhyaiḥ
body.translated_text: In its own nature too, that [creation] — pure and impure and mixed — he created. As stated by the <s>Sāṃkhyas</s>:
'Above, the creation is extensive in <s>sattva</s>; extensive in <s>tamas</s> at the root;
in the middle, extensive in <s>rajas</s>, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass.' Thus.
Here the opposing view:

children.translated_text: Since [everything] is born from one womb (<s>yoni</s>), and due to difference in cognition,
if that [creation] is one, how can it be twofold?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yonirmāyā tajjatvenāviśeṣāt sarvameva \crux śuddhānāṃ śarīraṃ śuddhaṃ \beginsupply śuddhaṃ \endsupply vā bhuvanaṃ syāt\crux |
ekarūpamevetyarthaḥ|
kiñcittvaśuddhānāmaśuddhaṃ vā miśritaṃ vetyevaṃ dvidhā kathamasṛjat| asaṃbhavāt| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The womb is <s>Māyā</s>; since everything is born from that without distinction, all [should be of one kind]. The meaning is: it should be of one form alone. But some [beings] of the impure have impure [bodies] or mixed [worlds] — how then did he create [it as] twofold? Because of impossibility. As they say:
'The material cause cannot [produce] what is contradictory [to its nature].'

body.text:
athaikasmāddvitayametatprakāratayā bhidyate|
yathānnādodanāpūpāviti|
tato nānayorvirodhasambhava iti| tadayuktamityucyate buddhibhedācceti|
buddhibhede hyannādodanādestatprakāratayā dvitayatvam|
yasya tvekasmādbuddhibhede 'satyanekatvaṃ nāsau tatprakāratayā dvidhā bhavati| ghaṭa iva tadabhāvatayā| buddhibhede 'satyanekatvaṃ ca|
prāguktādaśuddhācchuddhaṃ śuddhāccāśuddham| atastadapi tatprakāratayā dvidhā katham| naiveti| prakārabhedābhāvādatra ghaṭatadabhāvayoriva vastubheda eva|
ato nopādānaṃ viruddhasyeti yukta eva praśnaḥ| siddhāntastu
body.translated_text: Now, if from one [source] this duality is distinguished merely as a mode — as from rice [come] boiled rice and cake — then there would be no contradiction between the two. That is incorrect — it is said: 'due to difference in cognition.' For when there is cognitive difference, there is duality as modes, as in rice, boiled rice, and cake. But for that from which one [source], when there is no cognitive difference, multiplicity [arises] — that is not twofold as a mode, like a pot [and its absence] due to the absence of that [mode-relation]. And when there is no cognitive difference, there is multiplicity: from the previously stated impure [comes] the pure, and from the pure, the impure. Therefore, how can that too be twofold as a mode? Not at all. Due to the absence of mode-difference, there is only a real difference of entities here, as between a pot and the absence of a pot. Therefore 'the material cause cannot [produce] what is contradictory' — the question is valid indeed. The established conclusion, however:

children.translated_text: It is seen in the case of fireflies and the like — that
[what is] contradictory [can come] from one cause.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ayuktametadasiddhatvāt| na hi \crux prakārāntarasya prakārāntarakāraṇaprakārāntaratvamasmābhistadbuddhibhedādiṣyate\crux |
api tu prakāriṇa eva tathādṛṣṭatvāt|
khadyotamaśakamakṣikādīnāṃ hi prakāśāprakāśarūpeṇa buddhibhede 'pi svedaikayonijatvena buddhyabhedāttatprakāratvaṃ dṛṣṭam|
tadvadatra śuddhāśuddhayorutpadya jñānājñānarūpeṇa buddhibhede 'pi yonijatvena buddhibhedābhāvāttatprakārabhedenaiva dvidhābhāvo yukta iti prakārāṇāṃ parasparaparihāravirodhe 'pyekaprakāryupādānahetutvaṃ khadyotamaśakamakṣikādīnāmiva dṛṣṭaṃ na virudhyata ityadoṣaḥ| tathā hi
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: This is incorrect, due to unestablishment. For we do not maintain that a different mode's being of the nature of another mode — a cause of another mode — [is the case]. Rather, it is of the possessor of modes itself that [duality] is seen. For in the case of fireflies, bees, and flies, although there is cognitive difference in the form of luminous and non-luminous, due to cognitive non-difference through [their shared] origin from sweat alone, mode-relation is seen. Similarly here, although there is cognitive difference between pure and impure in the form of knowledge and ignorance, due to the absence of cognitive difference through [shared] birth from one womb, the duality is valid only through mode-difference. Even though modes mutually exclude each other, being the material cause of one possessor of modes — as is seen in the case of fireflies, bees, and flies — is not contradicted. Therefore there is no fault. For thus:

children.translated_text: Thus that [creation] of different configurations,
endowed with pure and impure parts,
should be known as arising from causal power —
an effect born from seed and instrumental cause.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evamekabījabhūtayoniśaktinimittatve 'pi śuddhāśuddhāmita pakṣasthaṃ bhinnasaṃsthānaṃ bhinnaprakāratayā jñeyam| na ghaṭatadabhāvavadbhedeneti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Thus, even though [originating from] one seed-womb-power as instrumental cause, the [creation] endowed with pure and impure parts, of different configurations, should be known through different modes — not through [real] difference as between a pot and the absence of a pot.
Now, the conclusion of the topic at hand:

children.translated_text: Thus this has been taught —
that effect [of <s>Māyā</s>], which has the body as its support.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
vigrahe 'sminsthūlaśarīre sūkṣmadehatayāśrayo yasya tanmāyākāryaṃ kalādi sūkṣmadehatayaivamādiṣṭaṃ parameśvareṇa| kathamityucyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: That which in this body — the gross body — is the support as the subtle body — that effect of <s>Māyā</s>, namely <s>kalā</s> and the rest, has thus been taught by the Supreme Lord as the subtle body. How so — it is said:

children.translated_text: Although this effect is mutually
contradictory and of dark nature,
nevertheless it is well-conjoined
clearly in one entity.
Being different, it accomplishes the purpose of the soul
like the parts of a cart for the person.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadyapyaśuddhaṃ māyākāryaṃ kalādyetatparasparaparihārasvabhāvatayā ghaṭatadabhāvādivattadviruddhaṃ tathāpyetadekasminsūkṣmadehe vastuni saṃśliṣṭaṃ sphuṭaṃ kṛtvā puruṣasyārthaṃ prāguktena caitanyopodbalenopalabdhaṃ kalādivyāpārabhedena sādhayatīti sambhāvyate śakaṭāṅgānīva śakaṭāśliṣṭānīti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Although the impure effect of <s>Māyā</s> — <s>kalā</s> and the rest — is contradictory like a pot and its absence by being of the nature of mutual exclusion, nevertheless, being clearly conjoined in one entity — the subtle body — it accomplishes the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul), apprehended through the previously mentioned empowerment of consciousness, through the different operations of <s>kalā</s> and the rest — this is conceivable — like the parts of a cart conjoined to the cart.

children.translated_text: Thus by <s>Ananta</s>
this was created as the binding of the body.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yasmādevaṃ puruṣārthasādhakametattasmātkāraṇāddehe nibandhanaṃ sthitiryasya taddehanibandhanaṃ sthūladehādhāratvena puruṣārthasādhakatayānanteśena sṛṣṭaṃ nānyatheti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Since this thus accomplishes the purpose of the soul, for that reason it — whose binding is in the body, i.e., whose abiding is in the gross body — was created by <s>Ananta-Īśa</s> as serving the soul's purpose through being the support of the gross body — not otherwise.

body.text: atha ko 'sau puruṣārthaḥ kathaṃ ca dehanibandhano 'sāvityucyate
body.translated_text: Now, what is that purpose of the soul, and how is it bound to the body? It is said:

children.translated_text: Without the body there is no liberation,
nor is there enjoyment — the teacher of consciousness and action.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatra muktirbhogaśca yaścitkriyayorgururupadeṣṭā bhogena hi citkriye upadiśyete|
yenābhoge na pralayakevalādyavasthāyāmityeṣa dvividhaḥ puruṣārthaḥ| sa ca dehena vinā nopapadyate| muktirhi malaparipākaṃ vinā nopapannā|
nāmiśraṃ pariṇamata iti nyāyena|
kevalasya ca tasya paripākāsambhavādavaśyaṃ tatparipākasahabhāvitvena śarīrāpekṣetyuktam|
bhogo 'pi bhogasādhanānāmeṣāmadhikaraṇaṃ vinā vyāpārādarśanāddehāpekṣā susiddhaivetyavirodhaḥ|
na kevalamatrānanta eva kartā yāvat
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Therein, liberation and enjoyment — and the <s>guru</s> (teacher) who instructs in the activities of consciousness (<s>citkriyā</s>) — for through enjoyment, the activities of consciousness are taught. Thus, 'not in enjoyment' means not in the state of dissolution-isolation (<s>pralayakevala</s>) etc. — this is the twofold goal of man (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). And that is not possible without a body. For liberation is impossible without the maturation of <s>mala</s> (impurity). Because 'the unmixed does not undergo transformation' — this is the principle. And since maturation is impossible for that [soul] in isolation, it has been said that a body is necessarily required as a concomitant of that maturation. Enjoyment too — since no operation is seen without a substratum for these instruments of enjoyment — the dependence on a body is well-established. There is no contradiction. Not only here is <s>Ananta</s> the agent, but also

children.translated_text: And this <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) does
because of [his] independence and lordship.
The benefactor of all, the peaceful one —
through his will, all fruit [comes about].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
parameśvaraśca tatkaroti na kevalo 'nanteśa iti cakāro 'tra bhinnakramaḥ|
prayojyaprayojakabhāvena dvayoratra kartṛtvamityarthaḥ||
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: And the Supreme Lord does that — not <s>Ananta</s> alone — the word 'ca' (and) here is in a different sequence. The meaning is: both have agency here in the relation of the impelled and the impeller.
Colophon: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the glorious <s>Kiraṇavṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Kiraṇa) composed by <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, son of <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>.
CHAPTER 5
Now, for the purpose of a further examination of the category of <s>pāśa</s> (bond) itself, another chapter beginning with a question.

children.translated_text: From <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace), <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) would occur;
[but] there is no descent [of śakti] because of [its] all-pervasiveness.

body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Here the connections of the <s>sūtra</s> (aphorism), word-meaning, and chapter are to be understood as before. But the sentence-form [of the objection] is:
'When one is initiated by the <s>guru</s> through the intense descent of <s>śakti</s> (power)' —
thus it is of many kinds. But the reciter [states]: 'The benefactor of all, the peaceful one' — and so forth.

body.text:
ayaṃ cātra praśnārthaḥ| yaduktaṃ
tīvraśaktinipātena guruṇā dīkṣita ityetadayuktam| pāto hyavyāpakatvena vyāptaḥ kuṇḍabadarādisiddhastadviruddhaṃ ca vyāpakatvaṃ tato vyāpakaviruddhopalabdhyātra vyāpakatvena śakteravyāpakatvābhāve patanābhāvaḥ sādhyata iti| na cāyamasiddho hetuḥ|
body.translated_text: And here the purport of the question is as follows: What was stated — 'initiated by the guru through the intense descent of śakti' — this is unjustified. For 'descent' is invariably accompanied by non-pervasiveness, as established in [the case of] a pot, a jujube fruit, etc. And pervasiveness is contradictory to that. Therefore, through the perception of what contradicts the pervader, the absence of non-pervasiveness of <s>śakti</s> and hence the absence of descent is to be proved here through [its] pervasiveness. Nor is this an unestablished reason (<s>asiddha hetu</s>),

body.text: prabodhikā ca sā śaktiḥ sarvagā paripaṭhyata iti
body.translated_text: because 'that <s>śakti</s> which awakens is recited as all-pervading' —

body.text: prabodhikā ca sā śaktiḥ sarvagā paripaṭhyate \Kir\ 4:1cd.
pūrvameva vyāpakatvenāsyāḥ samabhyupagamāditi| na tu māyayā naikāntikatvamatretyucyate
body.translated_text: since its pervasiveness has already been accepted previously. But it is not said that there is merely non-conclusiveness here due to <s>Māyā</s> —

children.translated_text: Because of being inherent in <s>Śiva</s>,
[the śakti] is always established in the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
parigrahavarttinī śaktiracetanā māyetyuktam| tataśca pariṇatisvabhāvatvātkāryakrameṇa puṃsaḥ pralayottarakālaṃ sā patatīti yujyate vaktum| iyaṃ tu parameśvarasamavetatvāccidrūpatvenāpariṇatidharmiṇī| yaduktam
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: It was stated that <s>Māyā</s> is an unconscious <s>śakti</s> operating through limitation. And therefore, since it is of the nature of transformation, it is appropriate to say that it descends upon the soul in a sequential manner of effects after the time of dissolution. But this [divine śakti], because of being inherent in the Supreme Lord, being of the nature of consciousness, does not have the property of transformation. As was stated:
'Transformation belongs to the unconscious; it is not appropriate for the conscious.'

body.text: tataśca sarvadaiva paśau sānugrāhikātvena saṃsthiteti nānaikāntikatā samavetatve satīti viśeṣitatvādatra hetorityarthaḥ|
body.translated_text: Therefore, since [the śakti] is always established in the <s>paśu</s> (bound soul) in a gracious manner, there is no inconclusiveness — because the reason here is qualified by 'when inherent' — this is the meaning.

body.text: atha saiva sthitiḥ pāta ityucyate| yadyevaṃ
body.translated_text: Now if it is said that the very abiding [of śakti] is called 'descent' — if so,
