children.translated_text: Since the <s>śakti</s> always abides,
would not the cessation of <s>bhava</s> (worldly existence) always occur?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tasyāḥ sarvapuruṣagatatvenānādivyavasthiteḥ sarvapuruṣāṇāmapyanādireva dīkṣāyogānmokṣa iti saṃsārābhāvaprasaṅgaḥ| abhyupagamyāpi śakteḥ prāguktaṃ pātamityucyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Since [the śakti] is established from beginningless time in all souls, for all souls too, liberation should be beginningless through the fitness for <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) — thus the unwanted consequence of the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) [arises]. Even accepting the previously stated 'descent' of <s>śakti</s>, it is said:

children.text: kālo vā sa ca kaḥ prokto
children.translated_text: 'Or is it time? And what is that [time] proclaimed [to be]?'
If time [is the cause], what [need] of <s>Śiva</s>?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
vāśabdaḥ pakṣāntarābhyupagamasūcanārthaḥ| athavā yaduktaṃ prāk
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The word 'vā' (or) is for indicating the acceptance of an alternative position. Or, what was previously stated —
'When the same karma arises, through the force of another time' —

body.text:
malaparipākakālaḥ proktaḥ| caśabdāt ko 'nyaḥ prokta iti| kiṃ prāgukta eva śaktipātasya kālo 'nyo vetyarthaḥ| na tu tasyaivājñātatvena vyākhyeyaṃ prāk pratipāditatvena tasyājñānasambhavābhāvāt|
yadapi kālaḥ śaktipātasya nimittaṃ, śaktipāto dīkṣāyā iti prāguktaṃ tadapyayuktam|
yataḥ kālo yadi śaktipātasya heturiṣyate tataḥ sa eva dīkṣāheturastu kiṃ śivenātra śaktipātadvāreṇa mokṣahetunā kalpitena|
bhoge tu sthūlaṃ vicitrakaṃ kāryamityādinā pratipāditatvāttasya kartṛtvamastviti praśnārthaḥ|
body.translated_text: the time of the maturation of <s>mala</s> (impurity) was proclaimed. And from the word 'ca' (and): 'What else is proclaimed?' — meaning, 'Is the time of <s>śaktipāta</s> the one previously stated, or another?' But this should not be explained as unknown, since the impossibility of its being unknown [arises] from its having been previously explained. Moreover, what was also stated — that time is the cause of <s>śaktipāta</s>, and <s>śaktipāta</s> [is the cause] of <s>dīkṣā</s> — that too is unjustified. For if time is desired as the cause of <s>śaktipāta</s>, then let time itself be the cause of <s>dīkṣā</s> — what [need] of <s>Śiva</s> here, imagined as the cause of liberation through the door of <s>śaktipāta</s>? But regarding enjoyment, since it has been explained through 'the gross and varied effect' etc., let his agency [of Śiva] be there — this is the purport of the question.
This collection of questions is refuted in order:

children.translated_text: Words are seen to operate here
through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>);
Just as the soul, [which is] all-pervading,
though eternal, is called 'perishable.'
Just as the cutting of <s>pāśa</s> (bonds) is proclaimed,
[just as] the king of <s>mantras</s>, the blessed <s>Śiva</s> [is so called] —
so too the 'descent of <s>śakti</s>'
is spoken of figuratively.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatra yaduktaṃ nipāto na vibhutvataḥ śakteriti tatsiddhasādhanameva|
ata eva tvaduktapramāṇabādhitatvānmukhyārthāsambhavenāsmābhirapi śaktipātaśrutīnāmupacaritārthatvamabhyupagataṃ|
yathā nityavyāpakadharmayukto 'pi puruṣo gantā vinaśvaraśca svaśarīreṇopacāreṇocyate| yathā ca pāśānāṃ dīkṣitaṃ puruṣaṃ pratyapravartanameva ccheda iva ccheda ucyate|
na tu vāstavo dvaidhībhāvaḥ| yathā ca mantrairvirājata iti mantrarāṭ parameśvaro 'pi san bhagavānupacārāducyata ityavirodhaḥ|
athātropacārasya nimittamanādisthitāyā vāmaśaktestāvat pātapadapravṛttāvucyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Regarding what was said — 'there is no descent because of the all-pervasiveness of śakti' — that is merely proving what is already established. Therefore, precisely because the literal meaning is impossible — being contradicted by the proof you yourself have stated — we too accept that the scriptural statements about <s>śaktipāta</s> have figurative meaning. Just as the soul, though endowed with the properties of being eternal and all-pervading, is figuratively called 'goer' and 'perishable' through [its] body. And just as the mere non-operation of the <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) toward the initiated soul is figuratively called 'cutting,' as if it were cutting — but there is no actual splitting in two. And just as the Supreme Lord too, being [called] '<s>mantrarāṭ</s>' (king of mantras) because mantras shine through him, is figuratively called '<s>Bhagavān</s>' (the Blessed One) — there is no contradiction. Now, regarding the basis for the figurative usage — for the [śakti] called <s>Vāmā</s>, which has been established from beginningless time, the ground for the application of the word 'descent' is stated:

children.translated_text: Just as the sudden fall
of a thing produces fear,
so too the 'descent of <s>śakti</s>'
is said to produce fear of worldly existence.
Therefore, [the soul] goes elsewhere —
just so, the <s>Ātman</s> (self) [goes] toward the <s>deśika</s> (teacher).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hi pāṣāṇādipāto bhayadaḥ puṃsāmevamanādirapi parameśvaraśakteḥ sambandhaḥ saṃsārabhayahetutvātpāta ivocyate|
jyeṣṭhāśaktisambandhino 'pi dīkṣāpūrvabhāvitvena prāguktasya pātasyopacāranimittamucyate
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as the fall of a stone etc. produces fear in people, so too, even though beginningless, the connection with the Supreme Lord's <s>śakti</s> is figuratively called 'descent' because it is the cause of fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). The basis for the figurative usage of the previously stated 'descent,' which precedes <s>dīkṣā</s> even for one connected with the <s>Jyeṣṭhā śakti</s> (supreme power), is stated:

children.translated_text: Just as a teacher awakens pupils
who are asleep before him, with a rod,
so too <s>Śiva</s>, those who are asleep
in the slumber of delusion, awakens through [his] <s>śakti</s>.
When the knowledge of one's own true nature
has 'fallen' — that is what is called [śaktipāta].
Therefore, <s>śaktinipāta</s> (descent of power) would be
[a figurative expression where] 'descent' denotes a sign.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathāgre sthitatvāviśeṣe 'pi śiṣyāñchāsane 'rhān yogyāneva gururdaṇḍena bodhayati na tvaśiṣyān|
evaṃ moho malastasya nidrā kāryaṃ pratyasāmarthyaṃ paripākaviśeṣastasyāṃ satyāmapi ye suptāstannivṛttyupāyasaṃvidvikalāstānparameśvarastayaiva pūrvavyavasthitayā śaktyā bodhayati|
evaṃ saiva malaparipākayogyatānusāreṇa yadā viśiṣṭaṃ tannivṛttyupāyavijñānaṃ saṃsāravaitṛṣṇyādikrameṇa janayati tadā jyeṣṭhā śaktitvena kāryahetuḥ patitetyupacārāducyate| yaduktaṃ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Just as, though there is no difference in standing before [the teacher], the <s>guru</s> awakens with a rod only those pupils who are worthy of instruction, who are fit — not the non-pupils — so too: delusion is <s>mala</s> (impurity); its 'sleep' is the incapacity with respect to effects; the particular maturation [of mala] — even when that [sleep] exists, those who are 'asleep' in the sense of being devoid of the knowledge of the means for its cessation — them the Supreme Lord awakens through that very <s>śakti</s> that was previously established. Thus, that very [śakti], in accordance with the fitness for the maturation of <s>mala</s>, when it generates the distinguished knowledge of the means for its cessation through a sequence beginning with dispassion toward <s>saṃsāra</s> — then it is figuratively called 'having fallen' as the cause of an effect in the role of the <s>Jyeṣṭhā śakti</s> (supreme power). As was stated:
'Having produced the obstruction of that <s>śakti</s>, one is made free from desire for worldly existence.'
In the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> [Āgama] also:
'He would become dispassionate toward <s>saṃsāra</s>, with impurity always destroyed.'
In the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Āgama] also:
'From that descent, the <s>mala</s> (impurity) that is the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> diminishes for this one;

body.text: kṣīṇe tasminyiyāsā syātparaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ prati| iti||
body.translated_text: when that is exhausted, there arises the desire toward the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).'
Therefore, what was stated —
'Since the śakti always abides, would not the cessation of worldly existence always occur?' —

body.text: tadapyadūṣaṇameva| sarvadāsthitatve 'pi tasyāstatra malaparipākānusāreṇa tadaiva bhavavicchittikāraṇatvaṃ nānyadānyatra ceti yataḥ|
body.translated_text: that too is not a valid objection. For even though [the śakti] always abides there, in accordance with the maturation of <s>mala</s>, only at that [particular] time and not at another time or elsewhere does it become the cause of the cessation of worldly existence.
The third question too is refuted:

children.translated_text: The time of that descent
is the very equality of <s>karmas</s> (actions).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaduktaṃ kālo vā sa ca kaḥ prokta
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: What was stated — 'Or is it time? And what is that proclaimed [to be]?' —

body.text: kālo vā sa ca kaḥ proktaḥ \Kir\ 5:2c.
samatve sati yo bhogaḥ kathaṃ tasya prajāyata iti|
body.translated_text: 'When there is equality, how does that enjoyment arise?'

body.text: samatve sati yo bhogaḥ kathaṃ tasya prajāyate \Kir\ 5:11ab.

evaṃ ca satyanādau saṃsāre kasyacitkadācittathābhūtakarmasaṃkaṭāntaḥpraveśena bhogānupapatteḥ saṃsārābhāvaprasaṅga ityavaśyaṃ tatparihārāyānīśvaravādibhirapyatreśvaraśaktipātaḥ kāminyādau rājaśaktivadabhyupagantavyo gatyantarābhāvāt|
anenaiva ca rūpeṇa karmaṇoḥ samatvamatra śaktipātasya kālo jñeyo na tu saṃkhyākṛtamiti darśayituṃ punaruktiḥ|
body.translated_text: And thus, in beginningless <s>saṃsāra</s>, since for someone at some time, entering into the narrow passage of such <s>karmas</s> would make enjoyment impossible — the unwanted consequence of the absence of <s>saṃsāra</s> [arises] — therefore, to avoid that, even by those who do not maintain the doctrine of a Lord (<s>anīśvaravādin</s>), the descent of the Lord's <s>śakti</s> must be accepted here, like the king's power in the case of a queen etc., since there is no other recourse. And to show that it is in this very form that the equality of karmas is to be known as the time of <s>śaktipāta</s>, and not as something determined by number, [there is] the repetition:

children.translated_text: The equality of <s>karma</s> is the time [of śaktipāta].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
samasaṃkhyatvena hyavirodhato na kadā cidbhogānupapattiḥ|
anyathā viśeṣābhāvāt sarvadaiva śaktipātaprasaṅgataḥ karmabhogāsambhavāt|
nābhuktaṃ karma naśyatītyāgamavirodhaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Because through equality of number, there is no impossibility of enjoyment at any time, since there is no contradiction. Otherwise, because of the absence of distinction, there would be the unwanted consequence of <s>śaktipāta</s> at all times; and because of the impossibility of experiencing <s>karmas</s> — 'Unexperienced <s>karma</s> does not perish' — there would be contradiction with scripture.

body.text: nābhuktaṃ karma naśyati Source unknown. Also quoted (as
) ad \Mat\VP\ 8:103, p.288 and thereafter (see note to translation).
ata eva malaparipākaliṅgatvena prāguktādapi karmasāmyādidamanyadeva karmavirodhātmakaṃ śaktipātaikanivartyaṃ karmasāmyamityadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Therefore, because it is indicated by the maturation of <s>mala</s>, this equality of <s>karma</s> — different from the previously stated [numerical equality] — being of the nature of mutual opposition of karmas, removable only by <s>śaktipāta</s>, is indeed something other [than numerical equality] — there is no fault.
Now, what kind of twofold <s>karma</s> results from <s>śaktipāta</s>? For that purpose, this [is stated]:

children.translated_text: [karma is] either exhausted or equal.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadā tayorviruddhayorapi karmaṇoravaśiṣṭaṃ sarvameva karmāvāpagatatvena samameva sampadyate tadānīṃ karmāntarasyānāvāpagatasyānurodhyasyāsambhavāttattvaiḥ samagraireva saha kṣīṇaṃ bhavatīti puṃsāṃ vijñānakevalitvameva|
yadvakṣyati same bhogastadā na hīti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: When all the remaining <s>karma</s> of both those mutually opposed [types], having been fully experienced, becomes equal [i.e., zero] — then, since there is no possibility of any other unexperienced <s>karma</s> that would need to be honored, it becomes exhausted together with all the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) — thus the souls attain the state of <s>vijñānakevala</s> (isolation in pure knowledge). As will be stated: 'When [karmas are] equal, there is no enjoyment then.'
'From the connection of excess and deficiency, confusion does not arise.'
Here, the opponent's view:

children.translated_text: How is that equality to be attained?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadetadyugapatparasparavirodhātmakaṃ samatvaṃ tatkathaṃ tābhyāṃ karmaviśeṣābhyāṃ prāpyam|
naivetyarthaḥ| anuṣṭhānakramasyaiva phaladānāpekṣitatvāditi bhāvaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: This equality, which consists in the simultaneous mutual opposition [of karmas] — how is it attained by those two particular types of <s>karma</s>? It is not [attainable] — this is the meaning. Because the sequence of performance alone requires the giving of fruit — this is the import.
Here, the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):

children.translated_text: How [is there to be] a lesser and greater time-unit?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
nyūnā cādhikā ca tuṭiḥ kālaḥ| sa kathaṃ gamyate|
kṛṣyādibhirdṛṣṭaiḥ karmabhirityadhyāhāraḥ|
etaduktaṃ bhavati---kṛṣyādikarmabhirayaṃ heturanaikāntikaḥ|
yatasteṣāṃ krameṇāpyanuṣṭhitānāṃ kadācitpaścādanuṣṭhitasya nyūnaḥ kālaḥ śīghrameva pūrvānuṣṭhitena sahabhāva phalaṃ kurvandṛśyate|
pūrvānuṣṭhitasya tvadhikaścirātmaka iti tadvadatrāpi sambhavādgamyamevaitat karmaṇoḥ samatvamityavirodhaḥ| tataśca
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: A time-unit (<s>tuṭi</s>) that is lesser and one that is greater — how is it known? Through visible <s>karmas</s> such as agriculture etc. — this is to be supplied. The meaning of this is: this reason is inconclusive with respect to <s>karmas</s> such as agriculture etc. For among those, even when performed in sequence, sometimes the later-performed one has a lesser time [to fruition] and is seen to produce fruit simultaneously with the earlier-performed one very quickly. But the earlier-performed one has a greater, longer time. Similarly, since the same is possible here too, this equality of <s>karmas</s> is indeed attainable — there is no contradiction. Therefore:

children.translated_text: Thus, the subtle equality —
at whatever time that [occurs], at that very [time] she (the śakti)
illuminates [the soul's] true nature quickly,
indeed through the power of the sign of awakening.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ dṛṣṭasyevādṛṣṭasyāpi karmaṇaḥ sambhāvyamānaṃ parasparavirodhātmakaṃ samānatvamasmadādyagocaratvāt sūkṣmaṃ yasmin kāle bhavati tasminneva kāle sā pārameśvarī śaktiḥ|
bodhacihnasya yadbalaṃ malaparipāko yaduktam
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Thus, the equality of invisible <s>karma</s> too — which is to be inferred like the visible — consisting of mutual opposition, being subtle because it is beyond the range of beings like us — at whatever time it occurs, at that very time, that supreme <s>śakti</s> of the Lord — through the power of the sign of awakening, [meaning] the maturation of <s>mala</s> — as was stated:
'Having produced the obstruction of that śakti, one is made free from desire for worldly existence.'
In the glorious <s>Mataṅga</s> [Āgama] also: 'He would become dispassionate toward saṃsāra, with impurity always destroyed.'
In the glorious <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Āgama] also:
'When that is exhausted, there arises the desire toward the supreme good.'

body.text: tena svarūpaṃ sarvajñatvādi puṃso dīkṣādvāreṇa dyotayati| yaduktaṃ
body.translated_text: Through that, [the śakti] illuminates the true nature — omniscience and the like — of the soul through the door of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). As was stated:
'When one is initiated by the <s>guru</s>,'

body.text: guruṇa dīkṣito yadā| sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvat \Kir\ 1:21bc.

body.translated_text: 'He becomes omniscient, like <s>Śiva</s> himself' —

body.text:
na tatra malaparipākāpekṣo 'nyaḥ śaktipātaḥ api tu sa eva prasaṅgādubhayanimittaṃ sampadyata iti bhāvaḥ|
vaiśabdo 'pi prakārāntare bodhacihnabalābhāve tu
kṣīṇaṃ vā yadi vāsamamityuktameva
body.translated_text: there is no other <s>śaktipāta</s> dependent on the maturation of <s>mala</s>; rather, that very [śaktipāta] incidentally becomes the cause of both — this is the import. The word 'vai' (indeed) [indicates] in another manner: when there is absence of the power of the sign of awakening, 'either exhausted or equal' — this has already been stated.

body.text:
nanūbhayorapyanayormokṣahetutvamastu| evamapyeṣa virodho na bhavatyeveti| astu yadi malaparipākasyeva karmasāmyasyāpi tannimittatvapratipādakaṃ sphuṭaṃ vacanaṃ bhavettasya tu karmasāmyaparihāramātraphalaṃ śaktipātaṃ prati tannimittatvaṃ pratipādayati nānyatretyuktam|
vakṣyati ca same bhogastadā na hīti|
body.translated_text: Is it not the case that both of these — <s>mala</s>-ripening and <s>karma</s>-equilibrium — should be causes of liberation? Even so, this contradiction does not arise, it is said. Let it be so, if there were a clear statement establishing that <s>karma</s>-equilibrium, like <s>mala</s>-ripening, is also a cause thereof. But that [argument] amounts merely to the removal of <s>karma</s>-equilibrium [as a cause],

body.text: atha kena hetunā viruddhayoḥ karmaṇoryugapatsambhava ityucyate
body.translated_text: Now, for what reason do contradictory <s>karmas</s> occur simultaneously? It is said:

children.translated_text: The portion of <s>karma</s> that is predominant first,
that alone gives experience; the other, however, [waits].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
śubhāśubhānekakarmavattve 'pi puṃso ya eva karmaviśeṣaḥ kṛṣyādivatpaścādanuṣṭhito 'pi karmāntarādyupakārajanitaparipākavaśāttīvravegatvena cādhikaḥ śaktyā bhavati sa eva prathamaṃ bhogapradaḥ| proktaṃ cānyairapi tīvravegānāmāsannaṃ phalamiti|
yastu tasmādanyaḥ punariti paścātkutaścitkarmāntarapratibandhakāpagamataḥ śaktipratilambhato vā bhogada iti| kimata ityucyate
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even though a person possesses many auspicious and inauspicious <s>karmas</s>, whichever particular <s>karma</s> — even if performed later, like agriculture — through the ripening generated by the assistance of other <s>karmas</s> and the like, becomes predominant in power by the intensity of its momentum, that alone first gives experience.

children.translated_text: When there is equality, what experience
how does it arise for that [person]?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ ca sati kutaścitkāraṇasāmarthyāddvayoḥ śubhayoraśubhayorvā paripākavaśāttīvravegatvena vā samatve saṃjāte sati tasya puṃso yugapadviruddhakarmadvayākṛṣṭasya kathaṃ bhogaḥ|
naiva jāyata ityavaśyaṃ virodhaparihārāyātra śaktipāto 'bhyupagantavya ityuktaṃ prāgeva|
nanvevaṃ sarvāṇyeva karmāṇi svasvaphalamātrasādhakatvātparasparaviruddhatvena
samānānīti sarvadā śaktipātaprasaṅgaḥ| netyucyate
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: And this being so, when through some causal potency, equality arises between two auspicious or two inauspicious [<s>karmas</s>] — through ripening or through intensity of momentum — for that person who is drawn by two contradictory <s>karmas</s> simultaneously, how does experience [arise]? It simply does not arise, thus —

children.translated_text: Or the initiating <s>karma</s> is mixed;
when equal, there is no experience then.
And some predominant [<s>karma</s>] must be stated;
otherwise, there would be no pleasure or its opposite.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
trividhaṃ hi karma jātyāyurbhogadaṃ puṃso bhogārambhakaṃ na kevalaṃ bhogapradamevāyuḥpradaṃ vā jātiviśeṣaṃ vinā bhogānupapatteḥ| nāpi jātipradameva tābhyāṃ vinā janma samanantarameva puṃso maraṇāt bhogā nupapatteriti|
same vijātīyenāmiśre kevalabhogaprade kevalāyuḥprade kevalajātiprade vā karmaṇi sati bhogo nopapadyata iti tatrādhikaḥ kaścitkarmaviśeṣo vijātīyaḥ| bhogaprade jātipradaḥ| tasminvā bhogaprada ityādirvaktavyaḥ|
anyathā sukhaduḥkhabhogānupapattestathābhūtakarmasadbhāve 'pi vijñānakevalitvameva tasyeti na sarvadā karmaṇāṃ virodhena śaktipātaprasaṅgaḥ| tadavirodhasyaiva sarvadā sambhavāditi|
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: For <s>karma</s> is threefold: giving birth, lifespan, and experience to a person. The initiating [<s>karma</s>] does not merely give experience alone, nor lifespan alone, nor a particular birth-type, since experience is impossible without [a specific birth]. Nor does it give birth alone, without those two, since immediately after birth the person would die —

children.translated_text: From the relationship of predominance and deficiency,
confusion does not arise.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yatrāpi puruṣe dvayorviruddhayoryugapadupasthitayoḥ karmaṇoḥ sāmyaṃ tatrāpi prāguktanayena karmāntarānurodhataḥ śaktipāto na kṣayaṃ vidhatte| api tu kasyacidadhikatvaṃ kasyacinnyūnatvamiti tayorvyākulatvaṃ virodho na jāyata iti|
ayamevāyurvede 'pyāyuṣyānāyuṣya karmaṇorvyākulatvaparihārāya prakāraḥ proktaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Even where in a person there is equality between two contradictory <s>karmas</s> that have simultaneously arisen, even there, by the previously stated method, the decline of power in accordance with other <s>karmas</s> does not effect destruction. Rather, one becomes predominant and another deficient, and of those two —
Through the application of <s>śilājatu</s> (mineral pitch), or through the grace of <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
or through the application of goat-hide [shields] — destruction [of karma] would occur, not otherwise.' Thus —

body.text: nidrāstotrādau ca nārāyaṇabhaṭṭokta eva mahābhārate ca darśitaḥ
body.translated_text: In the <s>Nidrāstotra</s> and elsewhere, as stated by <s>Nārāyaṇabhaṭṭa</s>, and as shown in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>:

body.text: kāntāreṣu ca sannānāṃ magnānāṃ ca mahārṇave|
body.translated_text: 'For those stranded in wildernesses, for those drowning in the great ocean,

body.text: kāntāreṣu ca\devdot gatiḥ paramā nṛṇām Not traced in
dasyubhirvā niruddhānāṃ tvaṃ gatiḥ paramā nṛṇām||
body.translated_text: for those besieged by robbers — You are the supreme refuge of men.'
And by the Buddhists also, in the <s>Tārāstotra</s> and elsewhere:
'O remover of the fears of elephants, lions, peacocks (?), serpent-hoods, thieves, fetters, the great ocean, and demons,

body.text: harikariśikhiphaṇitaskara@\devdot bhagavati tāre namastubhyam Source unknown.

body.translated_text: O <s>Bhagavatī</s> <s>Tārā</s>, whose beauty steals the radiance of moonbeams, salutations to you!' Thus —
How then does that [experience] arise? To this he says:

children.translated_text: Due to the absence of predominance and deficiency,
[the soul] attains that state.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadā tayorviruddhayordvayorapi karmaṇoḥ sarvamevānyat karmāvāpagatatvenādhikanyūnarahitaṃ samameva saṃpadyate kasmiṃścitpuruṣe tadānīṃ vyākulatvaṃ na jāyata iti karmāntarasyānurodhyasyā sambhavena śaktipātātteṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ kṣayaḥ prokta iti
sa kṣīṇakarmā puruṣastadānīṃ tatsthānaṃ prāk yatsame bhogastadā na hītyatroktaṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: When both of the two contradictory <s>karmas</s> — all other <s>karma</s> having departed — become equal, devoid of predominance and deficiency, in some person, then confusion does not arise, because of the impossibility of any other <s>karma</s> to be accommodated —

body.text: atha yathāyaṃ śaktipāto 'smadādyagocaratvena prāksūkṣma ukto vyādhyādinivṛttyanumeyo vā tathaiva kimasau prāgukto na vetyucyate
body.translated_text: Now, just as this descent of power (<s>śaktipāta</s>), being beyond the scope of people like us, was previously described as subtle, or is to be inferred from the cessation of diseases and the like — in the same way, is that previously described [descent] [recognizable] or not? It is said:

children.translated_text: That descent [of grace] is to be understood thus:
his devotion is distinctive.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
sa prāgukto malaparipākakālabhāvī śaktipāta ityevaṃ niyatapuruṣagatatvena mantavyaḥ| yasya hyasau bhavati tasya bhaktirvilakṣaṇā bhavatīti| yaduktaṃ prāk
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: That previously described <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power), which occurs at the time of <s>mala</s>-ripening, is to be understood as pertaining to a specific person in a determined manner. For the one in whom it occurs, his devotion becomes distinctive. As was stated before:
'Having obstructed that power, [the soul] is made free from desire for worldly existence.' Thus —
And in the illustrious <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [Āgama] also: 'When that [mala] is exhausted, the desire to depart arises,' and so forth.
Now, from these two [perspectives on] time:

children.translated_text: that very time is the skilled one —
the power's embrace of the self.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
sa eva prāguktaḥ śakteḥ pātakālaḥ| sa niṣṇātaḥ kuśalaḥ yasmādātmā parigṛhyate anugṛhyate tasminnityātmaparigrahaḥ sa kāla iti|
tasmāttameva tatrāpekṣate bhagavānnānyaṃ punaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: That very previously mentioned time of the descent of power — it is 'skilled' (<s>niṣṇāta</s>) because the self is embraced, i.e., graced, at that time — hence it is called 'the self's embrace' (<s>ātmaparigraha</s>), that time. Therefore, the Lord awaits precisely that [time] and no other. Moreover —

children.translated_text: Due to the beginningless connection with <s>karma</s>,
<s>Śiva</s> awaits the [right] time.
'The gap in time' — thus it is called;
and the knower of that is Lord <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
anādiryaḥ karmātmakaḥ samyagbandhastasmādeva yo bhogastasyānupapattyā kālacchidramityanena śabdena proktaḥ karmavirodhātmakastamatrāpekṣate śaktipātahetutvena| śaktipātātteṣāṃ virodhaparihāraḥ kṣayo vā nānyathā sambhavatītyevaṃ bhagavān jānāti yataḥ|
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: The beginningless complete bondage that is of the nature of <s>karma</s> — the experience arising therefrom, by reason of its impossibility [at certain times], is denoted by the term 'gap in time' (<s>kālacchidra</s>), which is of the nature of the contradiction of <s>karmas</s>. [<s>Śiva</s>] awaits that as the cause of <s>śaktipāta</s>. Through <s>śaktipāta</s>, the removal of that contradiction [occurs] —

body.text: atha kathamasau tameva kālaṃ karmaṇāṃ kṣaye 'pekṣate| na tu tadavirodhakālamapītyucyate|
body.translated_text: Now, how does He await precisely that time of the destruction of <s>karmas</s>, and not also the time of their non-contradiction? It is said:

children.translated_text: Just as someone, at a moving target,
awaits a certain moment,
so too does <s>Śiva</s>, the knower of that,
await the right moment.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yathā hyatyantasuśikṣito 'pyarjunādirdhanurdharo na sadaiva śatruto vinirgataṃ śarādyāyudhajātaṃ svaśaraiśchinatti|
api tu yadā svaśarīropaghātāyāyuṣyakarmavirodhena tadupasthitaṃ bhavati tasminneva kāle viruddhatvādeva tadvadeva tat bhagavānapi karmavirodhalakṣaṇaṃ sāmyameva śaktipāte 'pekṣate viruddhatvādeva tadānīṃ bhogāsambhavādityuktam| na tu tadavirodhakālamapyavirodhenaiva tadānīṃ bhogopapatteriti|
yadā tvetannābhyupagamyate tadā
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Just as even the most excellently trained archer such as <s>Arjuna</s> does not always cut down with his own arrows the weapons — arrows and other projectiles — discharged by the enemy, but rather, when [the enemy's weapon] presents itself through the contradiction of the life-sustaining <s>karma</s> threatening his own body, at that moment —

children.translated_text: Due to the absence of such equality [of karmas],
otherwise liberation [would occur] simultaneously [for all].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
anyathā virodhābhāvena sarvapuruṣāṇāṃ yugapacchaktipātaprasaṅgāt karmabhyo
muktirvijñānakevalitvaṃ syādityavaśyaṃ tatparihārāyātra karmasāmyameva hetutvena vācyamityavirodhaḥ|
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Otherwise, in the absence of contradiction, since <s>śaktipāta</s> would occur simultaneously for all persons, liberation from <s>karmas</s> — the state of being endowed with pure knowledge alone — would result. Therefore, necessarily, to avoid that [absurdity], <s>karma</s>-equilibrium alone must be stated as the cause. Thus there is no contradiction.

body.text: yadyevaṃ sa malaparipākalakṣaṇaḥ kālo bhagavatānugrahe 'pekṣyate| na tu tadaparipākalakṣaṇo 'pītyatra ko heturityucyate
body.translated_text: If this is so — that the time characterized by <s>mala</s>-ripening is awaited by the Lord for [bestowing] grace, but not the time characterized by non-ripening of that — what is the reason for this? It is said:

children.translated_text: There would be no need for means and instruments
if that sequence were not accepted.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadi sa kramaḥ kālo 'nugrahe nāpekṣyate tadā gurvādyupāyadīkṣādisādhanāpekṣā nātra bhavet| sarveṣāṃ yugapadanugrahastadānīṃ prasajyata ityarthaḥ| tataścāvaśyaṃ tatparihārāya kenāpi nimittena bhavitavyam|
taccakṣurādau paṭalādīnāmiva malasya paripākātmakamevoktamiti na kaściddoṣaḥ||
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: If that sequence — that time — were not required for grace, then there would be no need for means such as <s>guru</s> and the like, or instruments such as <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the like. For then, simultaneous grace for all would follow — this is the meaning. Therefore, necessarily, to avoid that, by some cause —
Now he resolves the fourth question as well:

children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is to be known as the Lord here;
what is lordship, if not that of a mere fragment?
Lordship is due to having knowledge as one's nature;
a fragment is not lord, due to being unknowing.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yaduktaṃ kāla eva mokṣaheturastu| kiṃ śaktipātahetunātra śivena kalpiteneti| tadayuktaṃ hetutvabhedāt| nimittaṃ hi kālo 'trācetanatvādamāvāsyādiryāgāderiva kartā tu bhagavānamāvāsyādiyāge dvijātivaccetanatvāt|
na ca nimittābhyupagame kartrabhāvaprasaṅgo yuktaḥ| virodhābhāvāt| kartrantarābhyupagame tu sa yukta eva| sa evāvirodhaḥ kārye kartṛnimittayordṛṣṭāntenocyate
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: As was stated: 'Let time alone be the cause of liberation; what need is there for <s>Śiva</s> imagined here as the cause of <s>śaktipāta</s>?' — that is improper, because of the difference in the type of causation. For time is here a circumstantial cause (<s>nimitta</s>), being non-conscious, like the new-moon day for a sacrifice and the like; but the agent is the Lord, like a twice-born person in a new-moon sacrifice —

children.translated_text: When the time is right, lordship would obtain,
as the sun's [role] in the awakening of a lotus.
And without time,
the blossoming does not take place there.
Even so, the sun is declared
in this world to be the awakener of the lotus.
If time is [merely] that fitness,
then even the illuminator [is so] only figuratively.

body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: It is also stated in the illustrative example [<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>]:

children.translated_text: Thus, even though there is equality
of <s>karma</s>, that is [merely] time.
Even so, the Lord <s>Īśa</s> is the master here,
established as [the agent] of <s>śaktipāta</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
paśūnāmaśaktatvenāndhādīnāmiva pāśavimokṣakartṛtvāsambhavāt|
pāśānāñca jaḍatvena paṭalādīnāmiva svataḥ paśubhyo nivṛttyanupapattestatpatireva pratiniyatakālāpekṣayā cakṣurvaidyādiriva mokṣakartā yukta eva prokta ityadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Since the <s>paśus</s> (bound souls), being incapable — like the blind and the like — cannot themselves be the agents of release from their bonds (<s>pāśa</s>); and since the bonds, being insentient — like cataracts and the like — cannot by themselves withdraw from the <s>paśus</s>; therefore, the Lord (<s>Pati</s>) alone, awaiting the appropriate time, is the agent of liberation, like an eye-doctor and the like —
Here, the opponent's view is that since [Śiva's] power awakens many persons, the fault of multiplicity would follow:

children.translated_text: If it, being one, [awakens] many,
how does it produce awakening? — if [one objects thus:]

body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: The established doctrine is:

children.translated_text: Even for many, there is no fault,
because of [its] all-pervasiveness, it is not obstructed.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yato vyāpakatvena bahūnāmapyupakāro 'syāḥ śakterna nivāryate| tato 'yamadoṣa iti|
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Since, by virtue of being all-pervading, the benefit of this power to many is not obstructed; therefore, this is not a fault.
Now, the summary of the topic:

children.translated_text: Thus the conjunction with [divine] power
has been taught as subtle in this doctrine.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evaṃ śaktipātaḥ prāguktaḥ| sarvapraśnaśūnyo mayā prokto 'treti| atra prasaṅgātpraśnaḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: Thus <s>śaktipāta</s> has been previously described. 'It has been taught by me as free from all objections' — thus. Here, incidentally, a question [arises]:

children.translated_text: If thus, through conjunction with His power,
<s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is established,
even after the time of initiation,
concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>) is seen.
If the power that causes concealment
does not [lead to] his liberation,
then let that Master act
so that he does not become otherwise.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
evamanena krameṇa viśiṣṭāt parameśvaraśaktisambandhādyadi puṃso dīkṣeti mokṣaheturanugrahastato dīkṣottara kālamapi tacchaktisambandhasya bhāvāttirobhāvaḥ samayollaṅghanādyātmako na bhavet| dṛśyate cāsau tatastadbhāvabhāvitvasya vyabhicārācchaktipātasyānugrahahetutvāsiddheḥ| yaduktaṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Vṛtti</s>: If by this sequence — through the distinguished connection with the supreme Lord's power — <s>dīkṣā</s> is the cause of liberation for the person as grace, then even after the time of <s>dīkṣā</s>, because of the persistence of that power-connection, concealment — characterized by transgression of observances and the like — should not occur. But it is seen —
'When [a person] is initiated by a <s>guru</s> through the intense descent of power' —

body.text: ityetatpunarapyayuktameva| athānugrahaheturasāviṣyate yadyevaṃ tathā karotu sa śaktipātalakṣaṇaṃ svamasyāstīti svāmī yathāsau puruṣo nānyathā bhavenna tirobhāvahetuṣu pravartata ityarthaḥ| na ca tathā karoti tadānīmapi tirobhāvahetuṣvanuṣṭhānadarśanāttat nānugrahahetuḥ śaktipāta iti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ| atra siddhāntaḥ
body.translated_text: this again is simply improper. Now, if it is maintained that this [<s>śaktipāta</s>] is the cause of grace, then let that Master — the one who possesses as his own (<s>svāmin</s>) the characteristic of <s>śaktipāta</s> — act so that that person does not become otherwise, does not engage in causes of concealment — this is the meaning. But it is not so, because —

children.translated_text: For those persons who have entered concealment,
by the will of <s>Śiva</s>,
it is not called 'the concealing [power]'
because it causes concealment;
the descent [of grace] is not for concealment,
since it has the nature of grace.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
iha tāvattirobhāvagatānāmapariṇatamalānāṃ na sā śaktiranugrāhikā saṃsthiteti sambandhaḥ| nāpi sā dīkṣā teṣāmācāryairlobhājñānādibhiḥ kṛtā śivecchayā tasyāḥ saṃsthitatvādityuktam| na tasyā jñānaṃ sambhavatīti śūdrāṇāmupanayanādivadanadhikāriṇāṃ sā niṣphalaiva|
teṣāṃ tu tirobhāvakartrī tadānīmanyaiva tirohikā śaktiḥ saṃsthitetyucyate|
yatastasyā naiva tirobhāvāya pātaḥ sambhavati anugrahadharmitvāditi yaduktam
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Here, first, for those who have gone into concealment (<s>tirobhāva</s>) and whose <s>mala</s> (impurity) is unripened, that grace-bestowing <s>śakti</s> (power) does not remain established — this is the connection. Nor is that <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) performed for them by teachers [acting] out of greed, ignorance, and the like [valid], since it is established [only] by the will of <s>Śiva</s> — so it has been stated. Knowledge of that [grace] is not possible [for them] — thus, for <s>Śūdras</s> and others who lack qualification, like [being unqualified for] <s>upanayana</s> (sacred thread ceremony) and the like, that [initiation] is fruitless indeed.
But for them, the <s>śakti</s> that effects concealment (<s>tirohikā śakti</s>) — a different one — is said to remain established at that time.
Since for that [grace-bestowing śakti], a fall [leading] to concealment is indeed not possible, because of its nature as grace — so it has been stated.
If the <s>śakti</s> that effects concealment [prevents] his liberation (<s>nirvṛti</s>),

body.text: ityetattāvadasiddhameva| yadyevamanugrahadharmitvāt kathaṃ na sarveṣāmanugrahaṃ vidhatta iti| tatrocyate
body.translated_text: this much remains unestablished. If it is so [that grace-śakti is of the nature of grace], then why does it not bestow grace upon all? To that it is said:

children.translated_text: For whomever the time [of mala-ripening] is nearest,
to that one [Śiva] reveals himself.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yena kāraṇena yasyaiva puṃso malaparipākakālo 'sāvāsannastena tasyaivātmānaṃ prakāśayatītyuktam
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
For the reason that the time of ripening of <s>mala</s> is near for that very person — to that person alone [<s>Śiva</s>] reveals himself — so it has been stated.
Having effected the obstruction of that <s>śakti</s> [of concealment], [the soul] is made free from desire for existence. Thus.

body.text: tato 'yamapyadoṣaḥ| yaduktaṃ dīkṣottarakālamapi sā śaktiḥ kathaṃ tirobhāvahetutvena saṃsthiteti| tadapyayuktam| yataḥ
body.translated_text: Therefore this too is not a fault. As for what was said — that even after the time of <s>dīkṣā</s>, how does that <s>śakti</s> remain as the cause of concealment — that too is inappropriate. Because:

children.translated_text: Having illuminated [the soul], it departs like lightning —
that <s>śakti</s> which awakens the soul.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
puṃsastadānīṃ pratibodhaṃ malakṣayātmakaṃ kṛtvā sā śaktiracireṇaiva kālena vidyudvadyāti tasmādvyāpārānnivarttate| kṛtasya punaḥ karaṇāsambhavāditi nyāyasiddha evāyamartha iti bhāvaḥ|
dīkṣottaraṃ tu mokṣaprāptiryāvat sāmānyena sā tasyādhiṣṭhāyakatvena sthiteti na śaktipātasyānugrahaṃ prati vyabhicāradoṣaḥ|
evamapi dīkṣāyā mokṣavyabhicāraprasaṅgadoṣastaduttarakālaṃ tirobhāvadarśanāditi| atrāpyucyate
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Having produced the awakening of the soul — which is of the nature of the destruction of <s>mala</s> — that <s>śakti</s> departs, i.e., ceases from its operation, within a very short time, like lightning. Because it is logically established that what has already been accomplished cannot be accomplished again — this is the purport.
But after <s>dīkṣā</s>, until the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), in general that [<s>śakti</s>] remains as the presiding [power] over that [soul] — therefore there is no fault of deviation of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) with respect to grace.
Even so, there is the fault of the contingency of the deviation of <s>dīkṣā</s> from [producing] <s>mokṣa</s>, since concealment is seen after that [dīkṣā]-time — to this too it is said:

children.translated_text: If this one, even though initiated (<s>dīkṣita</s>),
is completely (<s>sarvātmanā</s>) concealed,
in both kinds of concealment,
attainment of a [particular] station may occur in some cases.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
\crux adīkṣitastāvatsarvātmanā tirohito 'pi sankṛtadīkṣastasyetyuktam|
yadi samyagdīkṣito 'pyayaṃ kadāciddaivānmānuṣādvā pratibandhātsarvātmanā tirohito vāśabdādasarvātmanā ca tadāsyāsmin dvividhe 'pi tirobhāve kvaciditi kasmiṃścitkravyādayonyādau samayātikramaphalaprāptirbhavatīti| yaduktaṃ śrīmatpauṣkare
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
[Regarding] one who is not initiated — he is completely concealed; but for one who has received initiation, it has been stated [that the case is different].
If even one properly initiated is at some time, by fate or by human obstruction, completely concealed — or [if] by the word 'or' (<s>vā</s>), not completely [concealed] — then, in both kinds of concealment for him, 'in some cases' means in some [rebirth such as] a flesh-eating womb and the like, there occurs the attainment of the fruit of transgression of observances (<s>samayātikrama</s>). As stated in the glorious <s>Pauṣkara</s> [āgama]:
'From transgression of observances, the state of being a flesh-eater for a hundred years is declared.' Thus.

body.text: samayollaṅghanātproktaṃ kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ Not traced in \Pau, but = \Sar\ 25:2cd. Cf.\ note ad \KirV\ 1:10.5. The same half-verse is quoted there and in 6:8.12.
na tu sarvasminsamayātikrame vakṣyamāṇaiḥ prāyaścittaiḥ kṣapita iti kvacidgrahaṇam| kimata ityucyate|
body.translated_text: But not in every case of transgression of observances, since [some transgressions] are expiated by the penances (<s>prāyaścittas</s>) to be described — hence the word 'in some cases.' What follows from this is stated:

children.translated_text: For that one who remains in that [state of punishment],
that very <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) arises here.
For one endowed with that [vāsanā], liberation occurs —
of the self, free from conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpaka</s>).

body.text:
Vṛtti:
tatra samayātikramaphalabhogasthāne kravyādayonyātmani piśācādiśarīre 'pyavasthitasya samayātikramakarturdīkṣitasya vāsanā saiveti| yaivānatikrāntasamayānāṃ śivabhaktyādiheturvāsanā dṛṣṭā saivābhivyajyate|
ataśca dīkṣitatvavāsanāyogāttatprāyaścittaphalaṃ kāmyavaddīkṣāphalavighnabhūtaṃ bhuktvāsāvātmā mokṣaṃ dīkṣāphalaṃ prāpnotyeva| yaduktam
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
For one who remains in that place of experiencing the fruit of transgression of observances — in a body of a <s>piśāca</s> (spirit) and the like, which is the self of a flesh-eating womb — even for that transgressor of observances who has been initiated, 'that very <s>vāsanā</s>' means: the very <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) that is seen as the cause of devotion to <s>Śiva</s> and the like in those who have not transgressed their observances — that very one manifests.
And therefore, due to the connection with the <s>vāsanā</s> of being initiated, having experienced the fruit of the penance for that [transgression] — which obstructs the fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s> like [the fruit of] a desire-fulfilling [ritual] — that self attains <s>mokṣa</s>, which is the fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s>, indeed. As stated:
'For one purified by penance (<s>prāyaścitta</s>), a pure destiny is declared.' Thus.

body.text: prāyaścittaviśuddhasya gatiḥ śuddhā prakīrtitā Source unknown.

body.translated_text: Moreover:

children.translated_text: By this sequential process (<s>kramayoga</s>),
one who has gone into concealment —
there would be the contingency of purposelessness [of dīkṣā]
if that liberation were not to occur.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
pūrvaṃ malaparipākastataḥ śaktipātastato dīkṣetyanena kramayogena yo dīkṣitaḥ kathañcittirobhāvagato bhavettasya yadi samayātikramaphalabhogādanantaraṃ na taddīkṣāphalaṃ muktirbhavet|
tatastaddīkṣākramasyānarthakyaṃ prasajyeta| na ca parameśvaravyāpāratvāttasyāsāvupapadyata iti avaśyaṃ tata eva tasya tadānīṃ muktirabhyupagantavyeti na dīkṣāyā api svakāryavyabhicāraprasaṅgadoṣa iti|
nanu tulye śaktipāte dīkṣāyoge vā kathaṃ kaścidevottarakālaṃ tirobhāvena yujyate nānya ityatrocyate|
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
First the ripening of <s>mala</s>, then the descent of <s>śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>), then <s>dīkṣā</s> — by this sequential process, for one who has been initiated and has somehow gone into concealment, if after the experience of the fruit of transgressing observances, that fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s> which is liberation were not to occur —
then the purposelessness of that sequence of <s>dīkṣā</s> would follow. And since that [purposelessness] is not possible because [dīkṣā] is the operation of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), it must necessarily be accepted that liberation occurs for him precisely from that [dīkṣā] at that time — thus there is no fault of the contingency of deviation from its own effect even for <s>dīkṣā</s>.
Now, given equal <s>śaktipāta</s> or equal application of <s>dīkṣā</s>, how is it that only some are subsequently subject to concealment and not others? To this it is said:

children.translated_text: The <s>śakti</s> [may be] mild or milder,
due to the intention [to express] equality with <s>karma</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
karmaṇā malaparipākalakṣaṇena yatsāmyaṃ mandatvaṃ mandataratvaṃ vā tasya vivakṣāhetutvādvivakṣā jñānameva tayā hetubhūtayā mandā mandatarā vā śaktiḥ pārameśvarī dīkṣā vā yasyopatiṣṭhate tasya pratyavāyayogo bhavatyeva| yasya tu malaparipākalakṣaṇena karmaṇā tīvreṇa tīvratareṇa vā sāmyaṃ tadvivakṣayā tīvrā tīvratarā vā śaktiḥ patati tasya na pratyavāyaḥ kathamapi sambhavatītyuktaṃ bhavati|
evamanugrahaśaktermandatvopacāreṇa pratyavāyahetutvaṃ mantavyam| nānyathetyucyate
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Due to the equality — mildness or greater mildness — with <s>karma</s> characterized by the ripening of <s>mala</s>, and because that [equality] is the cause of the intention to express [it] — the intention being knowledge itself — due to that as the cause, for one upon whom the mild or milder <s>śakti</s> of the Supreme Lord, or <s>dīkṣā</s>, descends, the connection with adversity (<s>pratyavāya</s>) indeed occurs. But for one whose equality is with <s>karma</s> that is intense or more intense — characterized by the ripening of <s>mala</s> — due to the intention [expressing] that, the <s>śakti</s> that falls is intense or more intense, and for him adversity is not possible in any way — so it has been stated.
Thus, through the figurative attribution of mildness to the grace-<s>śakti</s>, its being a cause of adversity should be understood. Not otherwise — it is said:

children.translated_text: But that <s>śakti</s> is not of such a nature
as to undergo transformation like milk.
Because the <s>śakti</s> of the possessor of <s>śakti</s> [i.e., Śiva]
is differentiated [only] by the difference in the arrangement of [His] activities (<s>kṛtya</s>);
that [śakti] is a ladder for the twice-born and other <s>varṇas</s> (classes)
and it clearly liberates.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
na punaranugrahaśaktireva tirobhāvātmatāṃ gacchatītyupapadyate yataḥ parameśvarasya śaktiḥ kṛtyasya yatsaṃsthānaṃ sthitiḥ tenaiva bhedaṃ prāptā na mukhyata ityuktam|
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
But it is not tenable that the grace-<s>śakti</s> itself assumes the nature of concealment, because the <s>śakti</s> of the Supreme Lord has reached differentiation only through the arrangement — i.e., the establishment — of [His] activity (<s>kṛtya</s>), not essentially — so it has been stated.
'<s>Īśa</s> (the Lord), <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the Peaceful One — [He] is differentiated [only] by the differentiation of activities.' Thus.
And therefore, like the Supreme Lord Himself, that [śakti] too is without transformation. As stated:
'Transformation belongs to the insentient; for the sentient, it is not tenable.' Thus.

body.text: sā ca dvijādīnāṃ varṇānāṃ paramapadaṃ mokṣākhyaṃ gacchatāṃ niśreṇī sopānapaṅktiḥ ūrdhvagatihetutvāditi| evaṃ
body.translated_text: And that [śakti] is a ladder — a flight of steps — for the twice-born and other <s>varṇas</s> going to the supreme state called <s>mokṣa</s>, because it is the cause of upward movement. Thus:
'When [one is] initiated by the <s>guru</s> through an intense descent of <s>śakti</s>'—
this has been well stated. Thus the fifth chapter is concluded.

Colophon:
Thus [ends] the fifth section in the glorious <s>Kiraṇa-vṛtti</s> composed by <s>Bhaṭṭa Rāmakaṇṭha</s>, son of <s>Nārāyaṇakaṇṭha</s>.
CHAPTER 6
Now, for the purpose of examining the category of means (<s>upāya</s>), another section preceded by a question:

children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme cause,
has been declared the bestower of grace upon all.
But the <s>varṇas</s> (classes) that are twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>)
are established with [varying degrees of] inferiority and superiority.
If the <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) is indeed of this nature,
why should the fruit not be likewise [equal for all]?
Their <s>saṃskāra</s> is similar —
how then [can there be] inferior and superior attainment?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atra sūtrapadārthaprakaraṇasambandhāḥ prāgvaddraṣṭavyāḥ| vākyātmakastu guruṇā dīkṣito yadetyādibhiranekavidhaḥ|
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Here, the connections of the <s>sūtra</s>, category, and section are to be seen as before. But in terms of sentence-meaning, with 'when initiated by the <s>guru</s>' and so forth, [the question] is of many kinds.

'The first birth is from the mother; the second is from the <s>upanayana</s> (sacred investiture) —
by which the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, and <s>Vaiśyas</s> are called twice-born (<s>dvijāti</s>).' Thus.

body.text: mātṛtaḥ prathamā\devdot tenoktāste dvijātayaḥ Source unknown.

jātisvābhāvyādevagogavayagardabhādivatsāmānyaśāstreṣūttamamadhyamanyūnatvena sthitāsteṣāṃ ca yaḥ sāmānyaśāstravihito garbhādhānādiraṣṭacatvāriṃśadbhedabhinnaḥ saṃskāraḥ tajjātereva patitatvamātranivṛttiphalo vedavidbhiriṣyate taccharīrasya vā| yadāha manuḥ
body.translated_text: By the natural character of birth, like [the distinction between] the cow, the buffalo, and the donkey, [the varṇas] are established in the general scriptures as superior, middling, and inferior. And the <s>saṃskāra</s> prescribed by the general scriptures for them — consisting of the forty-eight divisions beginning with <s>garbhādhāna</s> (conception rite) — is accepted by the knowers of the <s>Veda</s> as having only the removal of the fallen state as its fruit for that birth, or for that body. As <s>Manu</s> states:

body.text: kāryaḥ śarīrasaṃskāraḥ pāvanaḥ pretya ceha ca|
body.translated_text:
'The purifying <s>saṃskāra</s> of the body should be performed, [effective] both in this life and after death,
through the womb-rites, <s>homas</s> (fire offerings), the birth-ceremony, tonsure, and investiture with the sacred girdle.' Thus.

body.text: tataścāyamapi dīkṣākhyaḥ saṃskāraḥ saṃskāratvā devamiti jāteḥ śarīrasya vā syāt| tathā ca phalaṃ tadvadevāsyānugrahātmakaṃ na kiṃ bhavet| naiva kiñcidbhavediti| tataśca
body.translated_text: And therefore, this <s>saṃskāra</s> called <s>dīkṣā</s> too, being a <s>saṃskāra</s>, should likewise be [merely] for the birth or the body. And accordingly, its fruit too should be of the same kind — of the nature of grace — should it not? It would not be anything [different] at all. And therefore,

body.text:
guruṇā dīkṣito yadā|
sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvad
body.translated_text:
'When initiated by the <s>guru</s>,
omniscient, he [becomes] like <s>Śiva</s>'—

body.text: guruṇā dīkṣito yadā| sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvat \Kir\ 1:21bc.
ityasyāḥ śrutervirodha ityarthaḥ| yato vaidikenāyaṃ saṃskāraḥ sadṛśasteṣāṃ tato vaidikāt nyūnā gatirasmāccādhiketyetatkatham| naivopapadyata iti praśnaḥ| siddhāntastu
body.translated_text: there is a contradiction with this <s>śruti</s> (scripture) — this is the meaning. Since this <s>saṃskāra</s> is similar to the Vedic [saṃskāra] for them, then how can the attainment from this be superior to and from the Vedic [saṃskāra] inferior? This is not tenable — such is the question. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), however:

children.translated_text: This <s>saṃskāra</s> is not considered to be of the birth
or of the body of the living being.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
nāyaṃ saṃskāro jāteḥ śarīrasya vā mataḥ| api tu prāṇinaścetanasyaivānugrahātmakaḥ tathāśruteriti na sādharmyamātreṇānyathā kalpanīyaḥ| tannaiṣa doṣa iti|
ye tvayamapi saṃskāratvājjāteḥ śarīrasya vā saṃskāro bhavanna dṛṣṭenaiva rūpeṇa śrāddhādi pitṛpitāmahāderiva puruṣasyopakāro bhaviṣyatīti kalpayanti tānpratyucyate
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
This <s>saṃskāra</s> is not considered to be of the birth or of the body. Rather, it is of the nature of grace for the living being — the conscious [self] alone — because such is the scripture. Therefore it should not be construed otherwise merely on the basis of similarity [with Vedic saṃskāra]. Hence this is no fault.
But to those who argue that this too, being a <s>saṃskāra</s>, must be a <s>saṃskāra</s> of the birth or of the body, and that [its benefit] will be for the person in the same visible form as <s>śrāddha</s> (death rites) and the like [benefit] the father, grandfather, and so on — to them it is replied:

children.translated_text: If [this saṃskāra were] of the birth, then when one
[person] is initiated, there would be initiation of all [of that birth-group].
Therefore it is not to be attributed to birth; nor is it considered of the body,
because of [the body's] insentience. [Rather,] grace of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>)
is declared. <s>Śiva</s> is the bestower of grace upon all.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
jāteḥ sarvapuruṣagatatvenāviśeṣādekapuruṣamokṣoddeśena saṃskāre sarvapuruṣamokṣaprasaṅgaḥ| śarīrasya tu puruṣabhedena bhedādetatprasaṅgābhāve 'pi jaḍatvānniṣphala eva saṃskāraḥ proktaḥ|
atha taddvāreṇa cetanasyaivāsau saṃskāra ityucyate yadyevamavirodhaḥ| yataścidrūpānugrahaḥ prokto 'smābhiriti|
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Since birth pervades all persons without distinction, if the <s>saṃskāra</s> [were performed] for the liberation of one person, there would be the contingency of the liberation of all persons [sharing that birth]. As for the body, although this contingency does not arise due to differentiation [of bodies] according to the difference of persons, still the <s>saṃskāra</s> is declared fruitless because of [the body's] insentience.
Now, if it be said that through the body as a medium, that <s>saṃskāra</s> is indeed of the conscious [self] — if so, there is no contradiction. Because grace of the nature of consciousness has been declared by us — this is the meaning.
Here, for another examination, a question:

children.translated_text: Since [Śiva] is the bestower of grace upon all,
grace should be bestowed upon children, the dull-witted, and those [immersed in] enjoyment,
O Lord!
And that [grace] is preceded by <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration).
If liberation were to come from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone
— as declared in the <s>tantra</s> — then,
ritual action (<s>kriyā</s>), knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), observances (<s>vrata</s>), and the like
[would be] causally ineffective as means.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
iha hi parameśvaraḥ sarveṣāmeva malaparipākātpaścātsaṃskāryatayā grāhakaḥ| teṣāṃ madhyāt
body.translated_text:
Commentary (<s>Vṛtti</s>):
Here indeed, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) accepts all as fit for consecration (<s>saṃskārya</s>) after the ripening of their <s>mala</s>. Among them,
'Up to sixteen [years], one is a child'—

body.text: ā ṣoḍaśādbhavedbālaḥ Source unknown. More of the verse is quoted in the \MrgVD\ ad \VP\ 10:14, pp.266--7 and ad \Mat\VP\ 12:5c--6c, p.339, where Bhatt observes that it appears (with some differences) in the {Śabdakalpadruma

iti smṛterbālo bālo 'prāptapadavākyapramāṇaśāstrābhyāsakālaḥ kathyate| bāliśastu na tato 'pi nyūnavarṣaḥ śaktipātaniścayābhāvādātmano 'nadhikāritvādasaṃskārya evāsau yataḥ| api tu strīśūdrādivat padavākyapramāṇaśāstraśravaṇāyogyo bāliśa iva bāliśaḥ kathyate|
bhogī punarna bhoganiṣṭha eva| tasya malaparipākābhāvena saṃskārānadhikārāt| yaduktam
body.translated_text:
according to this <s>smṛti</s> (tradition), a child (<s>bāla</s>) is defined as one who has not yet attained the time for practicing the science of words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge. The dull-witted (<s>bāliśa</s>), however, is not necessarily one younger in years than that, but rather — due to the absence of certainty about the descent of <s>śakti</s> and one's own lack of qualification — is unfit for consecration. Rather, like women, <s>Śūdras</s>, and the like, one who is unfit for hearing the science of words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge is called 'dull-witted' (<s>bāliśa</s>), like a simpleton.
The 'enjoyer' (<s>bhogī</s>), moreover, is not merely one established in enjoyment, since he lacks qualification for consecration due to the absence of ripening of <s>mala</s>. As stated:
'Having effected the obstruction of that <s>śakti</s> [of concealment], [the soul] is made free from desire for existence.' Thus.
The glorious <s>Vidyādhipati</s> (Lord of Knowledge) also says:

body.text: te tvacchaktyā naiva niyuktāḥ kila nūnaṃ yeṣāṃ bhoge saṃsṛtikartaryabhilāṣaḥ|
body.translated_text:
'Those who have desire for <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the agent [of bondage], in enjoyment — they are surely not appointed by that <s>śakti</s> at all.
Have those who are being ferried across by sea-creatures, their bodies devoured, crossed the shore of the terrible great ocean?' Thus.

body.text: kiṃ te tīrṇā bhīmamahāmbhonidhipāraṃ ye yādobhirluptaśarīrāḥ prataranta iti|
te tvacchaktyā\devdot ye yādobhirluptaśarīrāḥ pratarante Probably from the lost
, three verses of which are quoted in {Tantrāloka} 14:10--12. These are also in {mattamayūra} metre and have a similar rhetorical structure. (A Vidyādhipati is also cited ad \Moksa\ 69.)

api tu śrutapadavākyādiśāstraḥ saṃprāptatadabhyāsakālaścaiśvaryavyākṣepāttvakṛtatadabhyāso rājā direvocyate| teṣāṃ malaparipāke sati avaśyamanugrahaḥ śaktipātātmakaḥ kartavyaḥ parameśvareṇa| sa ca tathābhūto 'nugrahaḥ saṃskārasya dīkṣātmanaḥ pūrva eva pūrvokto heturityarthaḥ| tataśca
body.translated_text: Rather, one who has heard the science of words, sentences, and the like, and has reached the time for practicing them, but due to the distraction of sovereignty has not practiced them — like a king — is meant. When their <s>mala</s> has ripened, grace of the nature of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power) must necessarily be bestowed by the Supreme Lord. And that grace of such a nature is prior to the <s>saṃskāra</s> of the nature of <s>dīkṣā</s> — the previously stated cause — this is the meaning. And therefore,
'When initiated by the <s>guru</s> through an intense descent of <s>śakti</s>,
omniscient, he [becomes] like <s>Śiva</s>'—thus,

body.text: tīvraśaktinipātena guruṇā dīkṣito yadā| sarvajñaḥ sa śivo yadvat \Kir\ 1:21.

śrutyātrāgame saṃskāreṇaiva bālāderiva
proktā sarvasya muktiḥ syāditi dīkṣottarakālamanuṣṭheyatvenoktānāmasmākaṃ jñānādīnāṃ niṣprayojanatvameva padavākyapramāṇasaṃskārarahitatvenehāpi jñānādyayogyānāṃ bālādīnāṃ saṃskārādeva mukteḥ siddhatvādityasmākamapi puruṣārthānupāyabhūtametatkriyājñānādyanuṣṭhānamakartavyamiti praśnaḥ| siddhāntastu
body.translated_text: according to this <s>śruti</s> in our <s>āgama</s>, if liberation of all were declared to come from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone, like that of children and the like, then since liberation from <s>saṃskāra</s> alone is established for children and the like who are unfit for knowledge and the rest due to lacking the consecration of words, sentences, and valid means of knowledge — [the implication would be that] the practice of knowledge and the like, which has been stated as to be performed in the post-<s>dīkṣā</s> period, would be purposeless even for us, and therefore this practice of ritual action, knowledge, and the like, which is the means to the supreme goal, should not be performed by us — such is the question. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), however:

children.translated_text: Those who are established in whatever manner, O <s>Tārkṣya</s> (Garuḍa),
in that very manner the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>) bestows grace.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ye padavākyādisaṃskāreṇa vyavasthitā ye ca prakārāntareṇa bālādayaḥ teṣāṃ sarveṣāmeva bhagavānmalaparipākaparīkṣayā tatprakārānusāreṇa prasādaṃ karoti| na tu jñānāyogyānparityajatītyarthaḥ| tathā hi
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Those who are established through the refinement of words and sentences, and those who are otherwise [established], such as children and others — for all of them, the Lord, by examining the ripening of their <s>mala</s> (impurity), bestows grace according to the manner appropriate [to each]. The meaning is that He does not abandon those who are unfit for <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). As follows:

children.translated_text: Some here are fit for <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action),
their liberation is indeed in that very way.
Others likewise are fit for <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
and still others are fit for <s>caryā</s> (observance).
Thus, for whomever in whatever way liberation
has been declared, [it comes] through union with the Lord.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yeṣāṃ muktiḥ sadā śivatvalakṣaṇā tathaiva dīkṣāprakaraṇenaivoktā teṣāṃ madhyātkecidatra dīkṣottarasminkāle kriyāyāṃ yāgātmikāyāṃ japabāhyamānasabhinnāyāmeva yogyā bālā bhoginaśca na jñāne| nanu jñānaṃ vinā kriyāyāṃ yogyataiva na sambhavatīti| yadāhuḥ
jñātvā cānuṣṭhānamiti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Their liberation, always characterized by <s>Śiva</s>-nature, has been stated precisely through the topic of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). Among them, some, in the period after <s>dīkṣā</s>, are fit only for <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action) — which consists of worship and is distinguished into <s>japa</s> (recitation), external, and mental [forms] — namely children and worldly enjoyers, but not for <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). Now, [one might object:] fitness for <s>kriyā</s> alone without <s>jñāna</s> is not possible, as they say: 'One should practice after having known.'

body.text: jñātvā cānuṣṭhānam Source unknown. Cf. Jayaratha ad

body.translated_text: 'From transgressing the <s>samaya</s>-rules (observances), the state of being a flesh-eater for a hundred years is declared.' Thus:

body.text: samayollaṅghanātproktaṃ kravyādatvaṃ śataṃ samāḥ \Sar\ 25:2cd; but cf. \KirV\ 5:27.6 and 1:10.5 and the footnote to the translation of the latter.

na pratyavāyaphalebhyasteṣāṃ mokṣa ityarthaḥ|
evaṃ tāvadyathādhikāraṃ jñānādīnāṃ coditatvātsarvānuṣṭheyatvadoṣaḥ parihṛtaḥ|
yattūktaṃ kimarthamanuṣṭhīyanta iti tatrocyate
body.translated_text: Their liberation is not from the fruits of transgression — this is the meaning. Thus, since <s>jñāna</s> and other [practices] have been enjoined according to qualification, the fault of everything being obligatory for all is removed. Now, as to what was asked — 'For what purpose are they practiced?' — to that it is said:

children.translated_text: Of the means such as <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and others,
<s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is considered the cause.
By <s>dīkṣā</s> alone, liberation does not come about;
it [dīkṣā] is the means that regulates [the path].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
na jñānādīnāṃ niṣprayojanatvamatropāyatvena śrutatvāt| kevalaṃ dīkṣāpūrvatvena teṣāṃ śrutatvāt na dīkṣayā kāryabhūto bandhamokṣaḥ tasya tayaivāsampāditatvāt| api tūpāyaḥ sa niyāmaka iti yeṣāṃ yathā bandhanānāṃ mokṣārthaṃ vicchedātmako niyamo dīkṣayā na kṛtaḥ teṣāṃ keṣāñcideva sa jñānādirupāyo niyāmako vicchedako heturuktaḥ| tathā hi
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: There is no purposelessness of <s>jñāna</s> and the rest, since they have been taught here as means. Merely because they have been taught as preceded by <s>dīkṣā</s>, liberation from bondage — which is the effect — is not [accomplished] by <s>dīkṣā</s> [alone], since it has not been fully accomplished by that alone. Rather, 'it is the means that regulates': for those whose severance-in-the-form-of-regulation of bonds for the sake of liberation has not been effected by <s>dīkṣā</s>, for some of them, that means consisting of <s>jñāna</s> and the rest has been declared as the regulating, severing cause. As follows:

children.translated_text: Because of being the bestower of grace upon all,
those means have been proclaimed.
Why has not a single means
been declared? Because [the situation] is otherwise.

body.translated_text: Vṛtti: For here, by the reasoning to be stated — through the obstruction of the experience of <s>karma</s> (action) that has begun its effects — by <s>asadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (non-immediate-liberation initiation),
'The non-causality of means such as <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vrata</s> (vows), and so forth.' Thus:
That [objection] has been shown to be unestablished, and since it pertains to the domain of specific qualification, this is [merely] proving what is already established. It is said:

children.translated_text: And the <s>samaya</s>-rules (observances) of women and others,
due to their incapacity, one should purify [them without those rules].
Due to their ignorance, there is no fault. //

body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The childlike [initiates], due to their extreme ignorance,

body.text: Testimonium: from bāliśāstāvadatyantājñatvena up to and including dīkṣāyāmanadhikāra eva is quoted (prefaced by tathā coktaṃ śrīmatkiraṇavṛttikāreṇa bhagavatā rāmakaṇṭhaguruṇā ``samayāścetyādi\devdot'') by Nirmalamaṇi (=\Nirmala) in his

body.translated_text: 'Their <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is <s>nirbījikā</s> (seedless), devoid of <s>samaya</s>-rules (observances) and the like.' Thus:

body.text: na tvatra niṣiddhāḥ samayatvena mantavyāḥ| teṣāṃ devagurvagnidrohātmanāṃ pātakopapātakamahāpātakabhedena kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādiprāyaścittakṣapaṇīyatvena vakṣyamāṇatvāt|
body.translated_text: But here they should not be regarded as prohibited in the sense of being bound by <s>samaya</s>-rules. For the transgressions against deity, teacher, and sacred fire — classified as minor sins, secondary sins, and great sins — will be taught as expiable through <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and other <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penances).

body.text: arthī śakto vidvān śāstreṇāparyudastaḥ karmaṇyadhikriyate Quoted also ad \Sar\ 1:2, p.6. Bhatt notes (ad loc.) that it appears as number 719 of a

children.translated_text: For the knowing one, the fault would be great. //
Therefore their liberation would come
through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) by the path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).
Those who are capable here — for them, however,
one should purify them and reveal [the teachings] to them.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
jñatvamatra śaktatvameva| yathāha ye 'tra śaktā na teṣāṃ dīkṣayā śodhyāḥ| kiṃ tu nityānuṣṭheyatvena prakāśayediti| tataśca śaktatve sati ye nityādyanuṣṭhānaṃ na kurvanti teṣāṃ mahāndoṣaḥ prāyaścittalakṣaṇo bhavet|
nāśaktānāmiti| tarhi kiṃ tairnityamanuṣṭheyam|
laukikena rūpeṇa śivadharmoditena vā yathāśakti devagurutadbhaktaparicaraṇādikameva svataḥ putrabhṛtyādipreṣaṇena vā| tadeva ca teṣāṃ prāguktajñānādikṛtyaṃ sādhayati| yathāha bhaktiyogata iti|
anyathā teṣāmatyantamūḍhatvena tiraścāmiva śaktipātakāryasya bhaktyāderaniścayāddīkṣāyāmanadhikāra eva| na ca putrādestatsaṃskārārthitayā teṣāṃ śaktipātānumānaṃ yuktaṃ vyadhikaraṇatvāt|
na hi dhave dhūmaḥ khadire svakāraṇamagnimanumāpayatīti|
kāraṇaṃ ca śaktipāto bhaktyādīnāmityuktam| na tvarthitādeḥ| viśeṣato bhinnādhikaraṇasya snehasaṃskārapūrvakatvenaiva tasya siddheḥ| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: 'Knowing' here means capable. As it says: 'Those who are capable here — they should not be purified through <s>dīkṣā</s> [alone]; rather, one should reveal [the teachings] to them as daily obligatory practice.' And so, when capable, those who do not perform the daily and other observances — for them, great fault in the form of [requiring] <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penance) would arise. But not for the incapable. Then what should they practice daily? In worldly form or as enjoined by <s>Śivadharma</s>, according to their capacity — service to deity, teacher, and devotees of the Lord, either by themselves or through the sending of sons, servants, and so on. And that alone accomplishes for them the function of <s>jñāna</s> and other [practices] mentioned before, as it says: 'by the path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).' Otherwise, due to their extreme dullness — as with animals — because of the uncertainty of <s>bhakti</s> and other effects of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace), there would be no qualification for <s>dīkṣā</s> at all. And the inference of <s>śaktipāta</s> for them based on the desire of sons and others for their consecration is not valid, due to the difference in substrate. For smoke in a dhava tree does not cause inference of its own cause, fire, in a khadira tree. And <s>śaktipāta</s> has been stated as the cause of <s>bhakti</s> and the rest, not desire and so forth. Especially since that [desire], being in a different substrate, is established only as preceded by affection and sacramental connection. As they say:
'One should engage the beloved in <s>dharma</s> (righteous duty).' Thus:

body.text:
na tataḥ śaktipātānumānaṃ yuktaṃ pratibandhābhāvāditi| bhaktiyogata eva teṣāṃ tiryagvailakṣaṇyena jñānasiddheratyantāśaktatvena ca śāstracoditānuṣṭhānāsambhavādaprāptadīkṣāṇāmivopāsakānāṃ bhagavadviṣayastutinamaskārasaparyādyeva nityamanuṣṭheyaṃ yuktamityavirodhaḥ|
yenaiva teṣāṃ jñānādyananuṣṭheyamityuktaṃ tena kāraṇena yaduktam
body.translated_text: The inference of <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of grace) from that is not valid, due to the absence of an invariable connection. For them, by the path of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) alone — since their <s>jñāna</s> is accomplished through their distinction from animals, and since performance of scripture-enjoined observances is impossible due to their extreme incapacity — like worshippers who have not yet received <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), praise, prostration, and worship directed toward the Lord alone is appropriate as their daily obligatory practice. There is no contradiction. By the very reason it was said that <s>jñāna</s> and the rest are not to be practiced by them, for that reason what was stated —
'The non-causality of means such as <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vrata</s> (vows), and so forth.' Thus:
'Liberation would come by <s>saṃskāra</s> (consecration) alone' —
this too, in that context, is proving what is already established, and hence is not valid.
Now the conclusion:

children.translated_text: Thus all [practices] beginning with <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
one should reveal to the one who is capable of them.
Otherwise there would be a breach of the established order,
and the established order has been declared in the <s>Śivāgama</s>.
In its absence, nothing would remain;
therefore this regulation stands firm.
For the sake of gracing all
and with the intention of [establishing] the means of the established order.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
jñānayogyasya jñānaṃ nityānuṣṭheyatayā prakāśayedācāryaḥ|
kriyādiyogyasya tu kriyādīni| so 'pi tathaivānutiṣṭhet| anyathāgamavihitāyā nityādyanuṣṭhānātmikāyāḥ sthiterananuṣṭhānāt bhaṅgaḥ syādeva| evaṃ sthiterbhaṅge jāte sati na kiñcitsyāditi vakṣyamāṇaprāyaścittākrāntatvāt tasya na dīkṣāphalaṃ samanantaraṃ syāt|
prāyaścittavighnākrāntatvāditi tena kāraṇenāyaṃ jñānādīnāṃ nityānuṣṭheyatayā puruṣārthatvena niyamaḥ sthita iti|
tadananuṣṭhāne tu teṣāṃ prāyaścittaphalabhoktṛtā| tadante tu viśuddhajñānakevalitvena parameśvarādanugrahastāvato 'pi malasya dravyatvena svato nivṛttyasaṃbhavādityevaṃ sthityupāyavivakṣayāpi sarveṣāṃ pariṇatamalānāmanugrāhako bhagavānityadoṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) should reveal <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) to the one fit for <s>jñāna</s> as a daily obligatory practice. And for the one fit for <s>kriyā</s> (ritual action) and the rest, [he should reveal] <s>kriyā</s> and so forth. That one too should practice accordingly. Otherwise, there would indeed be a breach of the established order — consisting of the daily and other observances prescribed by the <s>āgama</s> — due to non-performance. When such a breach of the established order has occurred, 'nothing would remain,' since one is overtaken by the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penance) to be described — the fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s> would not follow immediately. Because one is overtaken by the obstacle of <s>prāyaścitta</s>, for that reason, this regulation — that <s>jñāna</s> and the rest are to be practiced daily as the goal of human life — stands firm. But in the case of non-performance, they become subjects of the fruit of <s>prāyaścitta</s>. And after that, through being pure in <s>jñāna</s> alone (<s>kevala</s>), grace from the Supreme Lord [comes] even to that extent, since <s>mala</s> (impurity), being a substance, cannot cease of its own accord. Thus, even with the intention of [establishing] the means of the established order, the Lord is the bestower of grace upon all whose <s>mala</s> has matured — there is no fault.
Here, a question for another examination:

children.translated_text: For the purpose of severing the <s>pāśa</s> (bond),
<s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is indeed performed.
But the severance is not seen;
since it is unseen, how [can it be established]? Explain.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
dīkṣā pāśaviśleṣahetuḥ| apiśabdācchivatvavyaktihetuśca na bhavati kriyātvāddarśanāntaradṛṣṭajyotiṣṭomabrahmahatyādikriyāvat| karmaṇāṃ ca pāśānāṃ dīkṣayā viśleṣo na sambhavet|
śarīrāntarabhogyatve sati tato deśakāladūravartitvena dṛṣṭatvāt|
khaḍgavicchedo dūrasthitabhaṭādīnāmiveti praśnārthaḥ| siddhāntastu
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: <s>Dīkṣā</s> (initiation) is the cause of severing <s>pāśa</s> (bonds). By the word 'api' (also), [the objection is:] it does not become the cause of manifesting <s>Śiva</s>-nature either, because it is an action — like the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> sacrifice, <s>brahmahatyā</s>-expiation, and other rituals seen in other systems. And the severance of <s>karmas</s> (actions), which are <s>pāśas</s> (bonds), cannot come about through <s>dīkṣā</s>, since, when they are to be experienced in other bodies, they are seen to be distant in place and time from that [initiation] — like the cutting of a sword [cannot reach] soldiers and others standing far away. This is the meaning of the question. The established doctrine, however, is:

children.translated_text: The destruction of <s>pāśa</s> (bonds) is established through stobha (impeding),
and that too through well-accomplished <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae).
Since the <s>mantras</s> are of inconceivable [power],
it is like the destruction of embodied poison.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
pāśānāṃ duṣkṛtakarmarūpāṇāṃ stobhātkṣayaḥ| yasmātpāśastobhakarma prāyaścittātmakamucyate tasmātkṣayo duṣkṛtalakṣaṇānāṃ karmaṇāṃ yena bhavatāṃ siddhaḥ tenātra prathamo heturanaikāntika ityarthaḥ|
asiddhaścākarmatvāddīkṣāyā mantraśaktirhyācāryavyāpārābhivyaktā dīkṣetyuktam|
mantrāṇāṃ ca samyaksiddhānāmacintyaśaktitvādviṣakṣayādiriva so 'pi pāśaviśleṣādiḥ sambhāvyata ityadoṣaḥ|
loke 'pyāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: The destruction of <s>pāśas</s> (bonds), which take the form of evil <s>karma</s> (action), [occurs] through stobha (impeding). Since the act of impeding <s>pāśas</s> is said to be in the nature of <s>prāyaścitta</s> (penance), the destruction of <s>karmas</s> characterized as evil deeds — by which it is established for you — therefore the first reason [of the opponent] is inconclusive. And [the second objection] is also unestablished, since <s>dīkṣā</s> is not [mere] <s>karma</s> (action) — for the power of <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae), manifested through the activity of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), is called <s>dīkṣā</s>. And since well-accomplished <s>mantras</s> possess inconceivable power, that severance of <s>pāśas</s> and the rest is plausible — just like the destruction of poison and so forth. There is no fault. In the world too they say:
'The power of gems, <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae), and herbs is indeed inconceivable.' Thus:

body.text: acintyo hi maṇimantrauṣadhīnāṃ prabhāvaḥ Occurs also in
Act 2, p.39 and is quoted ad \Mat\VP\ 7:49, p.249 and ad \KirV\ 3:11.

body.translated_text: The second reason too is declared to be inconclusive:

children.translated_text: Just as someone is brought under control
merely by the recitation of a name,
though standing far away, through foremost <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae) —
likewise is the destruction of <s>karma</s> (action) here.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
atra dūrasthito 'pi kāminyādirarthaḥ tannāmnā saṅkīrttitamātreṇa mantraviśeṣaiḥ sādhyamāno dṛṣṭaḥ| aśubhasūcakaiśca karmabhirakāla eva puṣpaphalādiḥ| yadāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: Here, even one standing at a distance — the meaning is a beloved woman and so forth — is seen to be brought under control merely by being addressed by name through special <s>mantras</s>. And through <s>karmas</s> (actions) that indicate inauspiciousness, [effects appear] untimely, such as flowers and fruits. As they say:
'Flowers and fruits born out of season, cold and heat out of season,
a river's flood out of season — these indicate great danger.' Thus:

body.text: akālajaṃ puṣpaphalaṃ\devdot sūcayanti mahadbhayam Source unknown.
tathaiva śarīrāntarabhogyasvakarmākāla eva mantrabalādupasthāpitamupabhuktatvāttatraiva kṣayameṣyatīti na doṣaḥ kaścit|
body.translated_text: Likewise, one's own <s>karma</s> (action) to be experienced in another body, [when] brought near untimely by the power of <s>mantras</s>, having been experienced, will attain destruction right there. Thus there is no fault at all.
Here, another question:

children.translated_text: If the complete severance of all <s>pāśas</s> (bonds)
[occurs], O Lord, through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation),
once the purpose has been accomplished,
how can the body continue to exist?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadi dīkṣayā karmādisarvapāśavicchittirbhavet tato nimittābhāvāddīkṣitānāṃ śarīraṃ na bhavet| bhavacca dṛṣṭam| tato dīkṣāyāṃ sarvapāśakṣayaśrutiragninā siñceditiśrutivatpratyakṣādibādhitatvādapramāṇamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: If through <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) the severing of all <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) including <s>karma</s> were to occur, then, due to the absence of a cause, the body of the initiated would not exist. But it is seen to exist. Therefore, the scriptural statement that all <s>pāśas</s> are destroyed in <s>dīkṣā</s> — being contradicted by direct perception and other [means of knowledge], like the scriptural statement 'one should sprinkle with fire' — is not a valid means of knowledge. This is the prior position.

body.text: agninā siñcet An old example, this occurs also, e.g., in

children.translated_text: Just as, when the pot has been completed,
the [potter's] wheel continues to revolve,
accomplished through prior momentum (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
so too does this body remain.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ghaṭasya niṣpattyarthaṃ hi cakrabhramaṇaṃ tasyāṃ jātāyāṃ sampannāyāmapi yathā tatsaṃskārata eva cakrabhramaṇaṃ dṛśyate tathā sadyonirvāṇadīkṣāyāṃ karmādisarvapāśakṣaye 'pi tatsaṃskāreṇaiva dīkṣitānāṃ kiyantaṃ kālaṃ śarīraṃ tiṣṭhatīti nimittābhāvādityasya hetostatkālanaimittikābhāvāsiddhāvanaikāntikatvānna proktadīkṣāphalaśrutibādhakṣatiriti| tadidamāhuḥ
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: For the wheel's revolving is for the purpose of completing the pot; even when that [completion] has occurred and is accomplished, just as the revolving of the wheel is seen [to continue] due to that momentum alone — so too, even when all <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) including <s>karma</s> (action) are destroyed in <s>sadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (immediate-liberation initiation), the body of the initiated continues for some time due to that momentum (<s>saṃskāra</s>) alone. Therefore, the reason 'due to the absence of a cause' is inconclusive, since the absence of an immediate cause at that time is unestablished. Thus there is no damage to the stated fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s> as taught in scripture. This is what they say:
'The body is sustained due to the force of <s>saṃskāra</s> (momentum), like the revolving of a wheel.' Thus:

In the case of <s>asadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (non-immediate-liberation initiation), however, since the destruction of all <s>pāśas</s> (bonds) is not taught [in scripture], this reason, being itself unestablished, is said to be non-contradicting:

children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> (action) spanning many lives,
