like burnt seeds, [is destroyed] by the <s>aṇus</s> (mantra-particles);
even future [karma] is obstructed.
That by which this [body exists] — that indeed [is consumed] through experience.
At the fall of the body, liberation occurs,
or [in the case of] <s>sadyonirvāṇa</s> (immediate liberation) [initiation],
through the <s>aṇus</s> (mantra-particles), always well-accomplished —
by that, they are uniters with <s>Śiva</s>.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
sadyonirvāṇadīkṣāyāṃ tāvatsarvāṇyeva prāgarjitāni karmāṇi mantraśaktitaḥ phalāprasavenāpyakāla eva bhogataḥ kṣayaṃ nīyanta ityuktam| asadyonirvāṇadīkṣāyāṃ tu sadyomumukṣoranadhikārānna tasya śarīrasya vināśāya mantrāḥ prayujyante| api tu rakṣaṇāyaiva yasmādyenedaṃ karmaṇā yathā ca śarīramārabdhaṃ tasya bhogenaiva kṣayaḥ| nānayeti| yattu dīkṣottarakālamanuṣṭheyatvādbhaviṣyadityuktaṃ karma tatsaṃskārārambhasāmarthyābhāvadvāreṇānayā saṃruddham| yataḥ prakṛtau karmaṇāṃ saṃskāraḥ kārya ityuktam|
ataśca sarva eva mantraśaktyā dīkṣitaṃ prati dagdhabījāḥ sampannāste karmaviśeṣāḥ| na punastatsaṃskārapātratāṃ yāntīti sadyonirvāṇadīkṣāyāñcārādhitamantrasāmarthyatastatkṣaye 'pi cakrabhramavaddhṛtaśarīrāvasthiteruktatvānna dīkṣānantarameva śarīrapātadoṣa iti|
body.translated_text: Vṛtti: In <s>sadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (immediate-liberation initiation), all previously earned <s>karmas</s> (actions), through the power of <s>mantras</s>, even without yielding their fruits, are brought to destruction untimely through experience — this has been stated. In <s>asadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s> (non-immediate-liberation initiation), however, since the one seeking immediate liberation has no qualification [for it], the <s>mantras</s> are not employed for the destruction of that body; rather, they are for its protection alone, since the <s>karma</s> by which and the manner in which this body was begun — its destruction is through experience alone, not otherwise. As for the <s>karma</s> called 'future,' which was stated as obligatory to be performed in the post-initiation period — that is obstructed by this [initiation] through the door of the absence of capacity to initiate [new karmic] impressions, since it has been stated that the impression of <s>karmas</s> is to be made in <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature). Therefore, all those particular <s>karmas</s>, through the power of <s>mantras</s>, become like burnt seeds with respect to the initiated — they no longer become receptacles for those impressions. And since in <s>sadyonirvāṇa-dīkṣā</s>, through the power of worshipped <s>mantras</s>, even upon their destruction, the body is sustained like the revolving of a wheel — as has been stated — there is no fault of the body falling immediately after <s>dīkṣā</s>.
Here a question:

children.translated_text: Is there any sign, however small,
of one who is freed from <s>pāśa</s> (bonds)?
It is seen through the sign of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion),
but the sign is nowhere clearly manifest.
Where in some cases it is clearly seen,
even there, there is deviation [from the rule].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadyevamasadyonirvāṇadīkṣayaitaccharīrabhogapradakarmapāśāmuktvatve 'pi tasya malādyanyapāśamuktatve yaccihnamavinābhāvi sarvajñatvādikaṃ tatsvalpamapi kathaṃ na dṛśyate| taddarśanābhāvena pramāṇāntarasiddhapradīpāvaraṇanivṛttyasiddhivat na tasya tadānīṃ pāśamuktatvasiddhiriti punarapi dīkṣāphalaśruteḥ pramāṇāntareṇaiva bādhāt aprāmāṇyamiti praśnārthaḥ|
body.translated_text: Commentary: If this is so — that through <s>asadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s> (initiation that does not produce immediate liberation), even though the <s>karma</s>-bond that produces the enjoyment of this body is not removed, the person is freed from other bonds such as <s>mala</s> (impurity) and the rest — then why is not even a trace of the mark (<s>cihna</s>) that is the invariable accompaniment [of that freedom], namely omniscience and the like, visible? Due to the absence of the perception of that [mark], just as the non-establishment of the removal of a lamp's covering through another means of knowledge [remains unestablished without perception], the freedom from bonds at that time is not established for that person. Thus, due to the contradiction by another means of knowledge of the scriptural statement regarding the fruit of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), [the scripture] would lack authority — this is the purport of the question.

body.text: na ca vācyaṃ bāhyacihnāntareṇa bhaktyātmanāsau pāśamukto dṛśyata iti yato na kvacittatpāśamuktasya caitaccihnamuktam| api tu śaktipātayuktasyaiva| sphuṭaṃ ca kṛtvā yatrāpi śaktipātayukte taccihnaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ tatrāpyasya vyabhicāritetyuktaṃ prāk tirobhāvakarī śaktirityādinā|
body.translated_text: Nor should it be said that 'he is seen to be free from bonds through another external mark, namely devotion (<s>bhakti</s>),' because that mark has never been established as [invariably] present in one freed from those bonds. Rather, [it is present] only in one who has received the descent of <s>śakti</s> (<s>śaktipāta</s>). And it has been clearly shown that even where that mark is seen in one who has received <s>śaktipāta</s>, there too it is deviant — as was previously stated through 'the <s>śakti</s> that effects concealment (<s>tirobhāvakarī</s>)' and so forth.

children.translated_text: The previously stated conjunction of that [soul with the Lord]
is preceded by apprehension, through that reasoning.
Because of its all-pervasiveness, there is no apprehension of it;
likewise, because of its formlessness.
There is a great contradiction here —
tell me, how is this [resolved]?

body.translated_text: Commentary: What was previously stated — that liberation consists in the conjunction with the Lord —
'Through unseen [merit] that serves the soul's purpose, the body is merely an <s>ātivāhika</s> (transmigrating) [body];
this one, [which is] the basis of the senses and accessible to the senses, is like a <s>piśāca</s> (spirit) for those without lordship.'

body.text: tadevamātmanaḥ sarvathā grahaṇābhāvena saṃyojanādyabhāvātparapuruṣārthaikaprāptyupāyatvenoktāyā dīkṣāyā anupapattermahānvirodha iti dvitīyaḥ praśnārthaḥ| siddhāntastu prathamapraśnanirodhāya|
body.translated_text: Thus, since the <s>Ātman</s> cannot be apprehended in any way, and since conjunction and the like are therefore impossible, the great contradiction lies in the impossibility of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), which was stated as the sole means for attaining the supreme goal for another soul — this is the purport of the second question. The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>), however, for the refutation of the first question:

children.translated_text: The mark of that [liberation] is the culmination of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>);
[that is,] the absence of doubt regarding the prescribed actions.

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ayamartho 'sadyonirvāṇadīkṣāyāṃ tāvadetaccharīrabhogapradaṃ karma puṃso na kṣapaṇīyamityuktam| malena ca kāryakaraṇaiśca vinā bhogānupapatterarthānmalasya sūkṣmadehasya ca na sarvātmanā viccheda iti pratīyate| api tu tadbhogoparodhena vāsanātmanāṃśena viccheda iti tatra sarvātmanā pāśāntaravicchedasyāpyasiddheḥ śivatvavyaktyasambhavāttaccihnaṃ sarvajñatvādi na dṛśyata ityadhyāhāraḥ| yato malādivāsanā vidyata iti|
yattu cihnāntaramapi tasya nopalabhyata ityuktaṃ tadayuktaṃ yato yā malaliṅgayoranayoranayā dīkṣayā pariśeṣitāṃśamātrarūpā vāsanetyuktaṃ tasyā niṣṭhāntyo vināśaḥ tadarthaṃ yatkarma nityanaimittikamaniṣiddhaṃ jñānakriyācaryātmakaṃ prāk pratipāditaṃ tasminnavikalpanā vikalpābhāvaḥ|
yathācoditatvenānuṣṭhānavivekitāsyatāvatyapi pāśamokṣe cihnamavyabhicāri dṛśyata eva| anyathā tathābhūtatvānupapattiriti na tadabhāvāttasya pāśamuktatvāsiddheḥ proktadoṣa iti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: The meaning is this: in the case of <s>asadyonirvāṇadīkṣā</s> (initiation not producing immediate liberation), it has been said that the <s>karma</s> that produces the enjoyment of this body is not to be destroyed for the person. And since enjoyment is impossible without <s>mala</s> and the instruments of effects (<s>kāryakaraṇa</s>), it is understood that the severance of <s>mala</s> and the subtle body is not total, but only partial — namely, the severance of the portion consisting of the latent impression (<s>vāsanā</s>) that obstructs enjoyment. Therefore, since the complete severance of the other bonds is also not established there, and since the manifestation of <s>Śiva</s>-nature is impossible [without complete severance], the mark — omniscience and the like — is not visible. This must be supplied [in understanding], because the latent impressions of <s>mala</s> and the like still exist. As for what was said — that another mark too is not perceived in him — that is incorrect, because what has been called 'latent impression' is the residual portion of these two — <s>mala</s> and the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) — left over after this initiation. Its 'culmination' (<s>niṣṭhā</s>) means final destruction. The <s>karma</s> for that purpose — the daily and occasional rites that are not forbidden, consisting of knowledge, action, and conduct (<s>jñānakriyācaryā</s>), as previously explained — regarding that, the 'absence of doubt' (<s>avikalpanā</s>) is the absence of hesitation. Since [the mark consists in] being practiced as enjoined, the discriminating practice [of prescribed actions] — to that extent too, a mark of freedom from bonds is indeed invariably seen. Otherwise, the very state of being such [a practitioner] would be impossible. Therefore, the fault stated [in the objection] does not arise from the absence of that [mark], since the person's freedom from bonds is not unestablished.
The refutation of the second question as well:

children.translated_text: For how [can] this, which resides in a body,
be inferred even through activity?

body.text:
Vṛtti:
yadā vibhutvādātmano grahaṇaṃ na sambhavatīti ayaṃ hetvarthastadā tanusthamiti kāryakaraṇābhivyaktaṃ kathametadvyāpakaṃ svarūpamasyātmanaḥ svasaṃvedanenānumīyate gṛhyate jñānayogādibhiśca saṃskriyata iti tenāyaṃ heturanaikāntika ityarthaḥ| tathā svātmavadanyātmanyapi parispandeneti kāyavāgvyavahārādinā talliṅgenānumīyate gṛhyata iti tenāpyanaikāntikaḥ| ākāśenāpītyucyate
body.translated_text: Commentary: When the reason-content is that the <s>Ātman</s> cannot be apprehended because of its all-pervasiveness, then [it is replied:] 'residing in a body' — being manifested through effects and instruments — how is this all-pervading nature of the <s>Ātman</s> inferred, i.e., apprehended, through self-awareness, and purified through <s>jñānayoga</s> (the yoga of knowledge) and the like? Therefore, this reason is inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) — this is the meaning. Likewise, [the <s>Ātman</s> is apprehended] through activity (<s>parispandana</s>) in another self as well as in one's own — through the marks of bodily and verbal behavior and the like — it is inferred, apprehended. Therefore, [the reason] is inconclusive by that [counter-evidence] as well. [The objection] is also [addressed] through [the analogy of] space:

children.translated_text: Although all-pervading, [the soul can be apprehended] as space [is apprehended] through sound;
and though formless, as poison [is apprehended]
through <s>mantra</s>-power — that one [the soul] is apprehended;
[what is] to be designated is the quality empowered by that [<s>mantra</s>].

body.text:
Vṛtti:
ākāśasya prākkāryatvenoktervibhutvāsambhavādatrānyabhūtāpekṣayā visṛtatve 'pi yathā viśiṣṭena śabdātmanā guṇena tadgṛhyate yogibhiśca svīkriyate| tathaiva dīkṣyasyātrāgame mantraśaktyā grahaṇam|
saṃskāryatvasambhavānna yojanānupapattiriti|
yadapyuktaṃ sūkṣmadehasyāmūrtatvenādṛṣṭavaśāccāsmadādyagocaratvānna taddvāreṇāpi dīkṣitasya grahaṇamiti| tadapi mantraśaktyāsmadādibhiramūrtāyā api viṣaśaktergrahaṇanidarśanādanaikāntikamiti|
yathā sā viṣaśabdavācyā māraṇaśaktirasmadādibhirgṛhyate tathaivātmaśabdavācyo jñānakriyātmako guṇaḥ sūkṣmadehaśabdenaiva vācyaśca bhogasādhanātmaka āgamamantraśaktyā gṛhyate saṃskriyate ceti nātra yojanānupapatteḥ saṃskārānupapattidoṣa iti|
body.translated_text: Commentary: Since space has been previously described as an effect [of <s>Māyā</s>] and hence all-pervasiveness is not possible for it, still, even when [space is taken as merely] extended relative to other elements, just as it is apprehended through a specific quality — namely sound — and is accepted by <s>yogins</s>, so too here the apprehension of the initiate (<s>dīkṣya</s>) is through <s>mantra</s>-power according to this <s>āgama</s>. Since the possibility of purification (<s>saṃskārya</s>) [of the soul] exists, there is no impossibility of conjunction (<s>yojana</s>). And as for what was said — that because the subtle body is formless and operates through unseen [forces], it is beyond our range, and therefore the initiate cannot be apprehended even through that [subtle body] — that too is inconclusive, because even for us, formless poison-power is apprehended through <s>mantra</s>-power, as shown by the example. Just as that killing-power designated by the word 'poison' is apprehended by us, so too the quality — of the nature of knowledge and action — designated by the word '<s>Ātman</s>' and also designated by the term 'subtle body,' which is of the nature of the instrument of enjoyment, is apprehended and purified through the power of <s>āgamic</s> <s>mantras</s>. Therefore, there is no fault of the impossibility of purification due to the impossibility of conjunction here.
Now, what is the nature of the <s>mantra</s> by whose power [this is accomplished]? It is said:

children.translated_text: Through the conjunction of the signified and the signifier,
the <s>mantra</s>-<s>aṇus</s> (atomic mantra-beings) should be known, O <s>Khaga</s> (Sky-goer).

children.text: vipadyeteti śabdabhāṣaṇayogānyathaiva mantrā vācakā api ca mantraśabdenocyante| tathaiva tadvācyāścāṇavo viśiṣṭā iti||
children.translated_text: because [if mantras are spoken aloud] there would be calamity — thus, through the conjunction with the uttering of sounds in a different manner, <s>mantras</s> are signifiers, and they are also called by the word '<s>mantra</s>.' Likewise, their signified [objects] are the <s>aṇus</s> (atomic beings) — that is, the distinguished [souls].

body.translated_text: Commentary: [The word <s>mantra</s> derives from] <s>mantrī</s>, one who speaks secretly;
